BURHAN:v2p55/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p55/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p55/r4.claim: The statement that every soul acquires only against itself concerns evil alone, by the occasion of revelation or by construing the verb as committing sin; the parallel verse states both good and evil, hence its contrast in verb forms.
BURHAN:v2p55/r4.anchor: والجواب أن المراد لا تكسب شرا ولا إثما بدليل سبب النزول

BURHAN:v3p34/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p34/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p34/r4.claim: The extra syllable in اكتسبت suits the burden and effort of sin, contrasting with the lighter form كسبت for good.
BURHAN:v3p34/r4.anchor: لأنه لما كانت السيئة ثقيلة وفيها تكلف زيد في لفظ فعلها

ITQAN:v1p251/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p251/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p251/r8.claim: Rāʾ assimilates into lām in the cited phrases, but not when rāʾ is open after a sākin, as in والحمير لتركبوها.
ITQAN:v1p251/r8.anchor: والراء في اللام نحو ﴿ هن أطهر لكم ﴾ ﴿ المصير لا يكلف ﴾ ﴿ والنهار لآيات ﴾ فإن فتحت وسكن ما قبلها لم تدغم

ITQAN:v4p347/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p347/r24.speaker: جعفر بن شمس الخلافة
ITQAN:v4p347/r24.claim: Ja'far lists this Qur'anic clause among expressions used proverbially (irsāl al-mathal).
ITQAN:v4p347/r24.anchor: عقد جعفر بن شمس الخلافة في كتاب الآداب بابا في ألفاظ من القرآن جارية مجرى المثل

ITQAN:v3p236#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p236#3/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p236#3/r5.claim: The form اكتسبت suggests effort and excess in the clause about evil deeds, which weigh more heavily.
ITQAN:v3p236#3/r5.anchor: أتى بلفظ ( الاكتساب ) المشعر بالكلفة والمبالغة في جانب السيئة لثقلها

STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r24.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r24.claim: The final two verses are among the surah's most recited and are important in Muslim devotional life.
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r24.anchor: and the final two verses, which are important in Muslim devotional life.

FARRA:v1p187/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p187/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p187/r8.claim: وسعها is a noun meaning capacity; its vocalic pattern parallels the alternatives in وجد and جهد.
FARRA:v1p187/r8.anchor: الوسع اسم في مثل معنى الوجد والجهد

MAJAZ:v1p83/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p83/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p83/r8.claim: إصر means a burden or binding tie; a covenant or kinship that attaches someone to another is an إصر, as in the expression آصرة رحم.
MAJAZ:v1p83/r8.anchor: الإصر الثقل وكل شىء عطفك على شىء من عهد

THALABI:v2p299/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p299/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v2p299/r3.claim: Ibn Umar weeps at the prospect of being taken to account for everything hidden; Ibn Abbas says Muslims shared this distress and that the capacity verse made fleeting thoughts no longer accountable unless expressed or acted on.
THALABI:v2p299/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عمر: إن أخذنا الله بها لنهلكن، ثم بكا حتى سمع.

THALABI:v2p301/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p301/r1.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p301/r1.claim: One interpretation holds that God accounts for settled convictions and intentions, while passing thoughts without resolve are exempt under the capacity verse; the oath verse supplies a parallel.
THALABI:v2p301/r1.anchor: فأما ما حدثتم به أنفسكم مما لم تعزموا عليه فإن ذلك مما لا يكلف الله نفسا

THALABI:v2p309/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r1.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p309/r1.claim: One interpretation associates the burden with separation and rupture, saying severed bonds can hurt more than physical pain.
THALABI:v2p309/r1.anchor: وقيل: هو القطيعة والفرقة نعوذ بالله منها. وقيل: قطع الأوصال أيسر من قطع الوصال،

THALABI:v2p309/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r2.speaker: النظام
THALABI:v2p309/r2.claim: Al-Nazzam imagines separation as so terrible that it could shake mountains, and says punishment by separation would seem worse than the fire's heat.
THALABI:v2p309/r2.anchor: وقال النظام: لو كان للبين صورة لما [راع] الذنوب ولهد الجبال

THALABI:v2p309/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p309/r3.claim: The plea واعف عنا asks God to overlook and pardon human shortcomings and sins.
THALABI:v2p309/r3.anchor: واعف عنا. أي تجاوز واصفح عن تقصيرنا وذنوبنا.

THALABI:v2p309/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p309/r4.claim: Forgiveness asks God to cover sins and forgo punishment; mercy is needed because people cannot obey or avoid sin without divine aid.
THALABI:v2p309/r4.anchor: واغفر لنا. واستر علينا ذنوبنا وتجاوز عنها ولا [تعاقبنا] وارحمنا. فإنا لا ننال العمل لطاعتك

THALABI:v2p309/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r5.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p309/r5.claim: Some distinguish the petitions as pardon from metamorphosis, forgiveness of sins, and mercy from slander; another distinction assigns them respectively to deeds, words, and beliefs or vows.
THALABI:v2p309/r5.anchor: وقيل: واعف عنا من المسخ، واغفر لنا عن السيئات، وارحمنا من القذف.

THALABI:v2p309/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r6.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p309/r6.claim: Another interpretation assigns pardon to minor sins, forgiveness to grave sins, and mercy to the weighing of deeds despite spiritual bankruptcy.
THALABI:v2p309/r6.anchor: وقيل: واعف عنا الصغائر، واغفر لنا الكبائر، وارحمنا بتثقيل الميزان مع إفلاسنا.

THALABI:v2p309/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r7.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p309/r7.claim: A further interpretation asks pardon during death's agony, forgiveness in the grave's darkness, and mercy there as well.
THALABI:v2p309/r7.anchor: وقيل: واعف عنا في سكرات الموت، واغفر لنا في ظلمة القبر، وارحمنا في ظلمة القبر.

THALABI:v2p309/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p309/r8.claim: Calling God our master means asking Him as helper, protector, guardian, and patron to grant victory over the disbelievers.
THALABI:v2p309/r8.anchor: أنت مولانا. أي ناصرنا وحافظنا وولينا ووال بنا فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين.

THALABI:v2p309/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p309/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits God's answer to the closing petitions: He has forgiven, excused, shown mercy, and granted victory, and will not burden people beyond their capacity.
THALABI:v2p309/r9.anchor: فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين. قال: قد عفوت عنكم وغفرت لكم ورحمتكم ونصرتكم على القوم الكافرين.

THALABI:v2p309/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p309/r10.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
THALABI:v2p309/r10.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal used to say Amen after completing Surat al-Baqara.
THALABI:v2p309/r10.anchor: وروى سفيان عن أبي إسحاق عن رجل عن معاذ بن جبل أنه كان إذا ختم البقرة قال: آمين.

THALABI:v2p310/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p310/r1.speaker: مسروق
THALABI:v2p310/r1.claim: Masruq calls Surat al-Baqara and Ali Imran a poor person's treasure when recited late at night.
THALABI:v2p310/r1.anchor: قال مسروق: نعم كنز الصعلوك سورة البقرة وآل عمران يقرأهما من آخر الليل.

THALABI:v2p310/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p310/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
THALABI:v2p310/r2.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says reciting both chapters on Friday night brings light between the named cosmic bounds.
THALABI:v2p310/r2.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: من قرأ ليلة الجمعة سورة البقرة وآل عمران كان له نور ما بين عجيبا إلى غريبا.

THALABI:v2p310/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p310/r3.speaker: مسروق
THALABI:v2p310/r3.claim: Masruq says a person who recites Surat al-Baqara in a night will be crowned.
THALABI:v2p310/r3.anchor: وقال مسروق: من قرأ سورة البقرة في ليلة توج بها.

THALABI:v2p310/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p310/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p310/r4.claim: A hadith calls the chapter in which the cow is mentioned the fortress of the Qurʾan.
THALABI:v2p310/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث السورة التي يذكر فيها البقرة فسطاط القرآن

THALABI:v2p310/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p310/r5.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v2p310/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says burdening beyond ability is impossible if it means beyond one's capacity, but possible if it means what feels heavy; Israel's commanded self-killing was burdensome in the latter sense.
THALABI:v2p310/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: قيل له: إن أردت ما ليس في قدرته، فهو محال، وإن أردت ما يثقل عليه، فلله تعالى أن يفعل

THALABI:v2p310/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p310/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p310/r6.claim: In answer to whether a just God could impose beyond capacity, one view says God could do so because creation and command belong to Him, but He has promised not to.
THALABI:v2p310/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: لو كلف فوق الوسع لكان له لأن الخلق خلقه والأمر أمره

THALABI:v2p310/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p310/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p310/r7.claim: Another answer stresses God's declared vastness, mercy, and denial of injustice, even though injustice could never be attributed to Him.
THALABI:v2p310/r7.anchor: قيل: قد أخبر عن سعته ورحمته وعطفه على خلقه كما نفى الظلم عن نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r1.claim: Iṣr means a burdensome, difficult command; āṣira is a binding tie such as a pact, kinship, or pledge, while iṣār is a rope that binds loads.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r1.anchor: الإصر: الأمر الغليظ الصعب، والآصرة في اللغة: الأمر الرابط من ذمام، أو قرابة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r2.claim: A poem praises one who prevents wrongdoing and bears the heavy burden from others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر: يا مانع الضيم أن يغشى سراتهم ... والحامل الإصر عنهم بعد ما عرقوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas said Muslims shared Ibn Umar’s fear, then the assurance that God burdens no soul beyond capacity was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r3.anchor: قد وجد المسلمون منها مثل ما وجد، فنزل: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r6.claim: The sound view is that the verse remains operative, with the later verse specifying uncontrollable whispers if those are included; settled intentions are reckoned with, believers forgiven and disbelievers or hypocrites punished.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r6.anchor: والأصح أنها محكمة، وأنه تعالى يحاسبهم على ما عملوا وما لم يعملوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r8.claim: The wording could encompass passing thoughts, so the Companions were distressed until God clarified the intended scope and relieved them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p751/r8.anchor: ولما كان اللفظ مما يمكن أن يدخل فيه الخواطر، أشفق الصحابة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r1.claim: The endings of long surahs echo their openings, following an Arabic poetic habit of digressing and returning; here the ending identifies those believers as Muhammad’s community.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r1.anchor: وقد تتبعت أوائل السور المطولة فوجدتها يناسبها أواخرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وابن سيرين وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r2.claim: One report says these two verses came without Gabriel: the Prophet heard them directly on the Night of Ascension, making them exceptions to the Medinan surah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r2.anchor: أن هاتين الآيتين لم ينزل بهما جبريل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير والضحاك وعطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r3.claim: A second report says Gabriel brought the two verses down to the Prophet in Medina.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p755/r3.anchor: إن جبريل نزل عليه بهما بالمدينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p756/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p756/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p756/r5.claim: Another rationale maps faith to human origin, hearing and obeying to present life, and the plea for forgiveness onward to the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p756/r5.anchor: للإنسان مبدأ وحال ومعاد، فالإيمان إشارة إلى المبدأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r4.claim: غفرانك asks pardon for falling short, or recognizes that even perfect worship falls short beside divine majesty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r4.anchor: غفرانك ربنا أي: من التقصير في حقك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r5.claim: وإليك المصير acknowledges return to God’s recompense.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r6.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r6.claim: Sibawayh parses غفرانك as a verbal noun governed by an implicit command, “forgive us with Your forgiveness”; this makes the phrase a request.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r6.anchor: التقدير عند سيبويه: اغفر لنا غفرانك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r7.claim: Zamakhshari likewise supplies an omitted verb, “we seek Your forgiveness and do not deny You,” making the clause declarative.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r8.speaker: ابن عصفور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r8.claim: Ibn Asfur gives inconsistent accounts, alternately saying the governing verb may be stated or must remain implicit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r8.anchor: واضطرب قول ابن عصفور فيه، فمرة قال: هو منصوب بفعل يجوز إظهاره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r9.claim: Other grammarians parse غفرانك as an object of asking or as a nominative subject meaning “Your forgiveness is our aim.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r9.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم انتصابه على المفعول به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p759/r10.claim: Grammarians disagree on the verbal noun pattern for hollow verbs with yāʾ: some treat it like a regular verb, some allow two patterns for the noun but kasra for place and time, and others follow attested usage; Abu Hayyan calls the last safest.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r1.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r1.claim: Al-Tabari glosses the wording about error as “we intended,” while Qutrub says it means we missed the correct interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r1.anchor: قال الطبري: قصدنا. وقال قطرب: أخطأنا في التأويل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r2.claim: Al-Asmai distinguishes أخطأ as an unintended mistake from خطئ as deliberate wrongdoing; the cited poem witnesses the latter.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r3.claim: Zamakhshari permits taking forgetting and error literally as excused lapses, and also reads them as negligence and inattention that caused the lapse; God’s faithful servants seek continued protection from such lapses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r3.anchor: ذكر النيسان والخطأ والمراد بهما ما هما منسيان عنه من التفريط والإغفال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya says many scholars correctly understand the prayer as asking pardon for prevailing forgetfulness and error from the intended course.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r5.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet said God has pardoned his community for forgetfulness and error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r5.anchor: قال قتادة في تفسير الآية: بلغني أن النبي عليه السلام قال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r6.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the believers feared accountability when the verse came, then Gabriel told the Prophet that God had granted their request.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r6.anchor: قال السدي: لما نزلت هذه الآية تغالوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r7.claim: These reports support asking relief from involuntary forgetfulness and error after the believers feared the prior verse’s reckoning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r7.anchor: وذلك أن المؤمنين لما كشف عنهم ما خافوه في قوله تعالى: يحاسبكم به الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r8.claim: Some lapses are culpable when a person neglects precautions, such as forgetting known impurity in clothing after failing to take steps to remember.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r8.anchor: فالأول، كنسيان النجاسة في الثوب بعد العلم بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r9.claim: Another view makes the prayer hypothetical: even if forgetfulness could warrant accountability, pardon is requested because constant vigilance would be burdensome.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p763/r9.anchor: وقيل: هذا دعاء على سبيل التقدير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r1.speaker: وهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r1.claim: Wahb reports that Job was asked what was hardest in his affliction and answered: the enemies’ gloating.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r1.anchor: روى وهب أن أيوب، على نبينا وعليه السلام، قيل له: ما كان أشق عليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r2.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r2.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the burden imposed on earlier people as Israel’s restrictive prohibitions and heavy restraints.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: التغليظ والأغلال التي كانت على بني إسرائيل من التحريم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r3.claim: Other explanations of the burden are hellfire or the whispers of the soul.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r3.anchor: وقيل: عذاب النار. وقيل: وساوس النفس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r4.claim: These explanations are examples, not restrictions on the general meaning of the request.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r4.anchor: وينبغي أن تحمل هذه التفاسير على أنها على سبيل التمثيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r5.claim: The request for anything beyond capacity is broader than the earlier request for a burden like that imposed on predecessors; the intensified verb also underscores the request.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r5.anchor: وهذا أعم من الذي قبله في الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r6.claim: Abu reads the verb in an intensive form, comparable to the difference between جرح and جرّح.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r6.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي في قوله: ولا تحمل علينا إصرا للتكثير في حمل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r7.claim: Another interpretation distinguishes a first request to be spared difficult duties from a second request to be spared punishments inflicted on earlier communities for failing to keep them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r7.anchor: طلبوا أولا أن يعفيهم من التكاليف الشاقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r8.claim: Ṭāqa is an anomalous verbal noun, not a productive pattern; it can mean absolute inability or a burden that is possible but severely difficult, mapping respectively to punishment or duties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r8.anchor: والطاقة القدرة على الشيء، وهي مصدر جاء على غير قياس المصادر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains the plea as asking not to bear a load that is heavy to discharge even if one could endure it, like saying one cannot bear to look at someone one dislikes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p765/r9.anchor: المعنى لا تحملنا حملا يثقل علينا أداؤه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r1.claim: Pardon removes punishment; forgiveness conceals the sin and protects from humiliation; mercy bestows beneficence, with each petition increasing in scope and intensity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r1.anchor: العفو إزالة الذنب بترك عقوبته، والغفران ستر الذنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r2.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r2.claim: Al-Raghib similarly defines pardon as removing sin’s punishment, forgiveness as covering it and replacing it with kindness, and mercy as an outpouring of beneficence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r2.anchor: وقال الراغب: العفو إزالة الذنب بترك عقوبته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r3.claim: Specific readings assign pardon to protection from metamorphosis or actions, forgiveness to sinking or speech, mercy to the weighing of deeds, or each plea to death, the grave, and Judgment; Abu Hayyan says these restrictions lack evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r3.anchor: وكل هذه الأقوال تخصيصات لا دليل عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r4.claim: Mawla derives from waliya and can function as a verbal, temporal, or locative noun; in the sense of ruler, master, helper, or kinsman it is a lexicalized noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r4.anchor: المولى مفعل من ولي يلي، يكون للمصدر والزمان والمكان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r5.claim: The ف in فانصرنا signals causation: because God is their master and manager, they ask Him to help them against enemies and instill courage while weakening the enemy.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r6.claim: The closing passage uses antithesis, semantic contrast, repetition, paronomasia, and ellipsis for rhetorical effect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p766/r6.anchor: وتضمنت هذه الآية من أنواع الفصاحة وضروب البلاغة أشياء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r1.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r1.claim: The cited Mosaic law requires animal offerings at the sanctuary and severe punishment for slaughter or eating blood outside the prescribed rite.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r1.anchor: ومن تقرب بذبح ثور أو غيره في مكان غير باب قبة الزمان بيت الرب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r2.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r2.claim: The quoted rules isolate people with leprosy and prescribe cutting away or burning affected clothing, leather, or houses; chronic flow also brings lengthy impurity rules.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r2.anchor: من برص من الآدميين يجلس وحده ولا يختلط مع الناس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r3.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r3.claim: Purification from leprosy requires birds, cedar, ritual washing and shaving, waiting outside the home, and a further offering on the eighth day.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r4.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r4.claim: The cited laws prescribe washing and impurity after emissions or contact with menstruants, and lengthy purification periods after childbirth: shorter for a son and longer for a daughter.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r4.anchor: المرأة إذا حبلت وولدت ذكرا تكون نجسة سبعة أيام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r5.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r5.claim: The Torah forbids harvesting every olive or grape and delays eating fruit from newly planted trees for three years, dedicates the fourth year's fruit, then permits eating in year five.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r5.anchor: فدعوها ثلاث سنين ولا تأكلوا من ثمارها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r6.speaker: الرب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r6.claim: Israelites are told not to take a widow's garment as pledge and to leave forgotten sheaves and olives for resident outsiders, orphans, and widows, remembering their slavery in Egypt.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r6.anchor: وإذا حصدتم حقل أرضكم ونسيتم حزمة لا ترجعوا في طلب أخذها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r7.claim: The author presents these extensive prior-scripture burdens as examples of what earlier peoples were charged with and says Christian burdens will be discussed in al-Ma'ida.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p558/r7.anchor: وأما ما على النصارى من ذلك فسيأتي كثير منه إن شاء الله تعالى في المائدة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p560/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p560/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p560/r2.claim: Al-Harali says the surah's forgiveness treats sin as though it never occurred, and mercy raises the pardoned sinner to high ranks; its opening is guidance and its close is vicegerency.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p560/r2.anchor: أن بداية هذه الصورة هداية وخاتمتها خلافة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p560/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p560/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p560/r3.claim: Al-Harali traces the surah's close from belief and wealth to support against unbelievers, linking its ending back to its beginning and viewing al-Baqara as encompassing the Qur'an's meanings.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p560/r3.anchor: ومن الجوامع العظيمة في أمرها وشمول معناها المبين لعلو قدرها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p561/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p561/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p561/r4.claim: The surah details the decree through its opening groups of believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites, then describes their seals, illnesses, rulings, and eventual recompense.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p561/r4.anchor: من تبيين أمر المؤمنين والكافرين والمنافقين

STUDYQURAN:18:60/r84.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r84.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r84.claim: Moses’ plea about forgetting recalls the believers’ prayer in 2:286 not to be taken to task for forgetting or error.
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r84.anchor: recalls 2:286, where the believers pray, Our Lord, take us not to task if we forget or err

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r1.claim: The final two verses are among the Quran's most recited and memorized passages; verse 285 states faith, verse 286 supplicates, and they are often recited together.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r1.anchor: These final two verses constitute some of the most often recited

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r2.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r2.claim: The Prophet said that reciting the two verses at night suffices the reciter.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r2.anchor: reported that the Prophet said of these two verses,“Whosoever recites these two

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r3.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet received the two verses sealing the sūrah from a treasury beneath the Throne.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r3.anchor: verses during the night, they will suffice him,” and also, “I was given the two

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r4.claim: On the Night Journey and Ascension, the Prophet received the five prayers, the Cow's final two verses, and forgiveness for community members who do not associate partners with God.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r4.anchor: 17:1; 53:1–18) the Prophet was given three things: the five canonical prayers,

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r8.claim: Thy forgiveness is an entreaty with an implied imperative: Grant us Thy forgiveness.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r8.anchor: Thy forgiveness is understood as an entreaty

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r9.claim: The principle that God tasks no soul beyond capacity also appears in 2:233, 6:152, 7:42, and 23:62.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r9.anchor: The message that God tasks no soul beyond its capacity is also found in 2:233; 6:152; 7:42; 23:62

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r10.claim: The verbs for earning and perpetrating share a root and can be synonymous depending on context.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r10.anchor: The verbs earned and perpetrated are closely related by root and can be synonymous depending on context

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r11.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r11.claim: What a soul earns adds to its merit; sins it perpetrates are held against it.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r11.anchor: it earned is added to its merit, while subject to what it

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r12.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r12.claim: Forgetting or erring may include omissions such as missing canonical prayers and commission such as adultery.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r12.anchor: can refer to sins of omission, such as forgetting to offer the canonical prayers, or of commission, such as adultery (IK)

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r13.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r13.claim: The burden may refer to covenants imposed on earlier religious communities under different conditions, including Jews and Christians; it may also mean other burdens.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r13.anchor: refer to the covenant or pact that was also made with different conditions with other religious communities, such as the Jews and Christians (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r14.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r14.claim: Islam is usually understood as easing and reducing ritual and legal obligations borne by earlier peoples.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r14.anchor: is usually interpreted to mean that in many ways Islam represented an alleviation and reduction of the ritual and legal obligations placed on people’s past (IK)

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r15.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r15.claim: This asks God not to impose commands or prohibitions too difficult to uphold.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r15.anchor: refers to commands and prohibitions that would be too difficult to uphold (R)

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r16.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r16.claim: A hadith says God absolved the Prophet's community of mistakes, forgetfulness, and acts done under compulsion.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r16.anchor: Truly God has absolved my community of mistakes, forgetfulness, and that which they were compelled to do

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r17.speaker: God
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r17.claim: Reports say God answers the believers' successive petitions with I have done so or Yes.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r17.anchor: God says, “I have done so” or “Yes,” or the Prophet is told by Gabriel, “He has done

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r18.speaker: Gabriel
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r18.claim: In another report, Gabriel tells the Prophet that God has answered the successive petitions.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r18.anchor: the Prophet is told by Gabriel, “He has done

STUDYQURAN:2:285/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r19.speaker: Muʿādh ibn Jabal
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r19.claim: After completing the sūrah, the prominent Companion Muʿādh ibn Jabal reportedly said amen, as is customary after reciting the Fātiḥah.
STUDYQURAN:2:285/r19.anchor: Companion Muʿādh ibn Jabal would say āmīn, or “amen,” which is also usually

TAB-FULL:v5p130/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p130/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v5p130/r7.claim: Some interpreters say that the earlier ruling about inward thoughts was abrogated by 2:286; Abu Hurayra reports people’s distress and God affirming their concluding petitions.
TAB-FULL:v5p130/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم: ثم نسخ الله ذلك بقوله: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت} [البقرة: 286]

TAB-FULL:v5p130/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p130/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v5p130/r8.claim: When 2:284 was revealed, people feared accountability for inner thoughts and asked the Prophet; 2:286 followed, and God answered “yes” to their petitions.
TAB-FULL:v5p130/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: لما نزلت: {لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} اشتد ذلك على القوم،

TAB-FULL:v5p131/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p131/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p131/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that 2:284 distressed believers; the Prophet told them to hear, obey, and submit, God strengthened their faith, then revealed 2:285 and affirmed each plea in 2:286 as fulfilled.
TAB-FULL:v5p131/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء} [البقرة: 284] دخل قلوبهم منها شيء

TAB-FULL:v5p131/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p131/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p131/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains that Ibn ʿUmar feared people would perish under 2:284; 2:286 then abrogated accountability for inner whisperings while retaining accountability for speech and deeds.
TAB-FULL:v5p131/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: «يغفر الله لعبد الله بن عمر لقد فرق أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم منها كما فرق ابن عمر منها» فأنزل الله: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت}

TAB-FULL:v5p134/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Muslims shared Ibn ʿUmar’s distress over 2:284; 2:286 came afterward because inward whisperings exceeded their capacity, leaving the soul accountable for what it acquired in words and deeds.
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r1.anchor: فقال عبد الله بن عباس: «يغفر الله لأبي عبد الرحمن، لعمري لقد وجد المسلمون منها حين أنزلت مثل ما وجد عبد الله بن عمر» فأنزل الله بعدها: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} [البقرة: 286]

TAB-FULL:v5p134/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r2.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri recounts Ibn ʿUmar’s tears and fear of being judged for inner thoughts, then Ibn ʿAbbas’s report that 2:286 relieved Muslims of that burden.
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r2.anchor: أخبرنا معمر، قال: سمعت الزهري، يقول في قوله: {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه} [البقرة: 284] قال: قرأها ابن عمر، فبكى وقال: إنا لمؤاخذون بما نحدث به أنفسنا،

TAB-FULL:v5p134/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says 2:284 greatly distressed the Companions, who were told to say “we hear and obey”; it was abrogated through 2:285–286, excusing inner thoughts while holding them to actions.
TAB-FULL:v5p134/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: كنت عند ابن عمر فقال: {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه} [البقرة: 284] الآية، فبكى، فدخلت على ابن عباس،

TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas said Ibn Umar wept over 2:284 as the Companions had, and that 2:286 abrogated it.
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r1.anchor: فبلغ صنيعه ابن عباس فقال: " يرحم الله أبا عبد الرحمن، لقد صنع كما صنع أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين أنزلت، فنسختها الآية التي بعدها

TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reported that 2:286 abrogated the earlier statement that God would account for what people disclosed or concealed.
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: " نسخت هذه الآية: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه} [البقرة: 284] {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها}

TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r3.claim: Saʿid reports that believers feared being charged for thoughts they never enacted; 2:286 answered them, God said “I have done,” and this community received the closing verses uniquely.
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه} [البقرة: 284] قالوا: " أنؤاخذ بما حدثنا به أنفسنا

TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r4.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r4.claim: Amir said the verse about hidden thoughts being accounted for was abrogated by the following verse, 2:286.
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r4.anchor: عن عامر: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء}

TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r5.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbi said 2:286 abrogated 2:284, which had said that God accounts for what people disclose or hide.
TAB-FULL:v5p134#2/r5.anchor: عن الشعبي: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} [البقرة: 284] قال: «نسختها الآية التي بعدها» : {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها}

TAB-FULL:v5p136/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r1.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbi reported that the burden of 2:284 lasted until 2:286 came, whereupon the latter abrogated what preceded it.
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي، قال: " لما نزلت هذه الآية: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء} [البقرة: 284] قال: «فكان فيها شدة

TAB-FULL:v5p136/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r2.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi said the discussion reached this point and returned to the end of the verse, namely the assignment of what each soul earned or bore.
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r2.anchor: قال: فقال الشعبي: «إلى هذا صار، رجعت إلى آخر الآية»

TAB-FULL:v5p136/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud said accountability for hidden thoughts preceded 2:286, which abrogated the earlier verse.
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r3.anchor: قال: قال ابن مسعود: «كانت المحاسبة قبل أن تنزل» : {لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت}

TAB-FULL:v5p136/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r4.claim: Mujahid and his co-transmitters reported that 2:286 abrogated the earlier verse about disclosed or concealed thoughts.
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قالوا: " نسخت هذه الآية: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} [البقرة: 286] {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه}

TAB-FULL:v5p136/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r5.speaker: عكرمة، وعامر
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r5.claim: Ikrima and Amir reported the same position: 2:286 abrogated the earlier accounting for hidden thoughts.
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r5.anchor: عن جابر، عن عكرمة، وعامر، بمثله

TAB-FULL:v5p136/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r6.claim: Al-Hasan said 2:286 erased 2:284, including its statement about what is disclosed or hidden.
TAB-FULL:v5p136/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه}

TAB-FULL:v5p138/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r1.claim: Qatada reported that 2:286 abrogated the preceding verse about God accounting for disclosed or hidden thoughts.
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، أنه قال: " نسخت هذه الآية، يعني قوله: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} [البقرة: 286] الآية التي كانت قبلها

TAB-FULL:v5p138/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that believers feared accountability for unacted thoughts; after they affirmed obedience rather than Israelite disobedience, revelation relieved them by limiting the matter to deeds, not thoughts in the heart.
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r2.anchor: ثني ابن زيد، قال: " لما نزلت هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v5p138/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda reports from Ibn Masʿud that the following verse, 2:286, abrogated the prior statement about hidden thoughts.
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r3.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} [البقرة: 284] قال: «نسخت هذه الآية التي بعدها»

TAB-FULL:v5p138/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r4.claim: Al-Suddi reports that people were initially charged for inner whisperings as well as deeds; their complaint led God to abrogate that rule because thoughts exceeded their capacity.
TAB-FULL:v5p138/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} [البقرة: 284] قال: " يوم نزلت هذه الآية كانوا يؤاخذون بما وسوست به أنفسهم

TAB-FULL:v5p138#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p138#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v5p138#2/r1.claim: Aisha said that 2:286 abrogated the earlier verse about disclosed or concealed thoughts.
TAB-FULL:v5p138#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، أن عائشة أم المؤمنين، رضي الله عنها قالت: " نسختها قوله: {لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت}

TAB-FULL:v5p144/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p144/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p144/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that 2:284 remains in force: abrogation requires a later ruling to negate the earlier one in every respect, and 2:286 does not negate divine accounting.
TAB-FULL:v5p144/r3.anchor: وأولى الأقوال التي ذكرناها بتأويل الآية قول من قال: إنها محكمة وليست بمنسوخة

TAB-FULL:v5p145/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p145/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p145/r4.claim: Al-Tabari accepts that each soul is liable only for its own earning: liability requires doing what God forbade or leaving what He commanded.
TAB-FULL:v5p145/r4.anchor: إن ذلك كذلك، وغير مؤاخذ العبد بشيء من ذلك إلا بفعل ما نهي عن فعله، أو ترك ما أمر بفعله

TAB-FULL:v5p145/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p145/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p145/r5.claim: The threat in 2:284 does not target an unacted sinful inclination, since God promised pardon for minor sins when major sins are avoided; it targets concealed unbelief.
TAB-FULL:v5p145/r5.anchor: وإنما الوعيد من الله عز وجل بقوله: {ويعذب من يشاء} [البقرة: 284] على ما أخفته نفوس الذين كانت أنفسهم تخفي الشك في الله

TAB-FULL:v5p153/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r1.claim: God burdens a soul only with what lies within its capacity, imposing no constriction or excessive hardship in religious duties.
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r1.anchor: فيتعبدها إلا بما يسعها، فلا يضيق عليها، ولا يجهدها

TAB-FULL:v5p153/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r2.claim: Al-Tabari explains wusʿ as capacity, citing the expression “this matter has room for me,” like the terms juhd and wijd for hardship or ability.
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r2.anchor: وقد بينا فيما مضى قبل أن الوسع اسم من قول القائل: وسعني هذا الأمر مثل: الجهد والوجد

TAB-FULL:v5p153/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the believers were given breadth in religion, citing the absence of hardship, God’s desire for ease, and the command to fear Him as able.
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} [البقرة: 286] قال: " هم المؤمنون وسع الله عليهم أمر دينهم

TAB-FULL:v5p153/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that believers asked how to repent of involuntary whisperings; Gabriel brought 2:286 to assure them they could not prevent such thoughts.
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس، قال: " لما نزلت ضج المؤمنون منها ضجة وقالوا: يا رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v5p153/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r5.claim: Al-Suddi glosses capacity as what a person can bear and says inner talk was beyond their capacity.
TAB-FULL:v5p153/r5.anchor: عن السدي: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} [البقرة: 286]

TAB-FULL:v5p154/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r1.claim: Each soul receives what it earned in good and bears what it acquired in evil.
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت} [البقرة: 286] «أي من خير»

TAB-FULL:v5p154/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r2.claim: Qatada glosses what a soul earns as good and what it bears as evil or wrongdoing.
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت} [البقرة: 286] «أي من خير» {وعليها ما اكتسبت}

TAB-FULL:v5p154/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r3.claim: Al-Suddi likewise says the soul’s earnings are its good deeds and its burdens are its evil deeds.
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r3.anchor: عن السدي، {لها ما كسبت} [البقرة: 286] يقول: «ما عملت من خير» {وعليها ما اكتسبت}

TAB-FULL:v5p154/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the soul’s earnings and burdens as the deeds of hand, foot, and tongue.
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس: {لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت} [البقرة: 286] «عمل اليد والرجل واللسان»

TAB-FULL:v5p154/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r5.claim: Al-Tabari concludes that God neither strains nor constricts a soul in religion, and does not charge it for an unacted intention, passing whisper, or fleeting thought.
TAB-FULL:v5p154/r5.anchor: فلا يجهدها، ولا يضيق عليها في أمر دينها، فيؤاخذها بهمة إن همت، ولا بوسوسة إن عرضت لها، ولا بخطرة إن خطرت بقلبها

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r1.claim: The prayer is God’s instruction to believers about how to call upon Him and what to say.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r1.anchor: فرغبة العبد إلى الله عز وجل بقوله: {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا} [البقرة: 286] فيما كان من نسيان منه لما أمر بفعله

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r2.claim: The petition asks pardon for forgetting a required duty or mistakenly doing something forbidden without intending disobedience, through ignorance or error.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r2.anchor: عن فعله ففعلناه، على غير قصد منا إلى معصيتك، ولكن على جهالة منا به وخطأ

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd paraphrases the prayer as asking not to be charged for forgetting a duty or mistakenly committing a prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا} [البقرة: 286] «إن نسينا شيئا مما افترضته علينا

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r4.claim: Qatada relays the Prophet’s statement that God has excused this community for forgetfulness and for thoughts that occur within themselves.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا} [البقرة: 286] قال: بلغني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says Gabriel instructed Muhammad to recite this petition when the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r5.anchor: زعم السدي أن هذه، الآية حين نزلت: " {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا} [البقرة: 286] قال له جبريل

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r6.claim: Al-Tabari distinguishes forgetfulness caused by neglect from forgetfulness caused by incapacity or weak memory.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r6.anchor: إن النسيان على وجهين: أحدهما: على وجه التضرع من العبد والتفريط؛ والآخر: على وجه عجز الناسي عن حفظ ما استحفظ

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r7.claim: Neglectful forgetting is a failure to perform a command; the petition seeks pardon for it, except when the neglect amounts to unbelief. Al-Tabari cites Adam’s lapse and later neglect of prayer, fasting, or memorized Quran.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r7.anchor: فأما الذي يكون من العبد على وجه التضييع منه والتفريط، فهو ترك منه لما أمر بفعله، فذلك الذي يرغب العبد إلى الله عز وجل في تركه مؤاخذته به

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r8.claim: Forgetting caused by inability to retain what one sincerely tried to learn is not a sin, so seeking forgiveness for it has no point.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r8.anchor: وأما الذي العبد به غير مؤاخذ لعجز بنيته عن حفظه، وقلة احتمال عقله ما وكل بمراعاته، فإن ذلك من العبد غير معصية

TAB-FULL:v5p155/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r9.claim: Al-Tabari distinguishes intentional wrongdoing, which is sinful and calls for pardon except in unbelief, from an innocent mistake.
TAB-FULL:v5p155/r9.anchor: وكذلك للخطأ وجهان أحدهما من وجه ما نهي عنه العبد فيأتيه بقصد منه وإرادة، فذلك خطأ منه وهو به مأخوذ

TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari reads the anonymous poet’s خطئوا الصواب as meaning that they missed the right answer, illustrating his distinction between خطئ and أخطأ.
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r1.anchor: الناس يلحون الأمير إذا هم … خطئوا الصواب ولا يلام المرشد

TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari says the intentional kind of error is a chosen violation for which one may ask pardon, apart from unbelief.
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الوجه الذي يرغب العبد إلى ربه في صفح ما كان منه من إثم عنه، إلا ما كان من ذلك كفرا

TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r3.claim: An unintentional mistake based on a reasonable but mistaken assumption carries no sin: examples are eating at night believing dawn has not arrived or delaying prayer on a cloudy day while awaiting its time.
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r3.anchor: كالذي في شهر رمضان ليلا وهو يحسب أن الفجر لم يطلع، أو يؤخر صلاة في يوم غيم وهو ينتظر بتأخيره إياها دخول وقتها

TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r4.speaker: قوم
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r4.claim: Some held that asking not to be charged for forgetfulness or error is obedience and humility, not an actual request for pardon; al-Tabari says he will treat their view in a fuller work.
TAB-FULL:v5p155#2/r4.anchor: وقد زعم قوم أن مسألة العبد ربه أن لا يؤاخذه بما نسي أو أخطأ، إنما هو فعل منه لما أمره به ربه تبارك وتعالى

TAB-FULL:v5p158/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r1.claim: Ṭabarī reads iṣr as a covenant: believers ask not to be bound by a covenant they cannot fulfill, lest failure, error, or forgetfulness bring the punishment suffered by earlier communities.
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r1.anchor: علينا عهدا فنعجز عن القيام به ولا نستطيعه

TAB-FULL:v5p158/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses iṣr as a covenant and pledge, and says the covenant was made onerous for those before the Muslims.
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {لا تحمل علينا إصرا} [البقرة: 286] قال: «لا تحمل علينا عهدا وميثاقا»

TAB-FULL:v5p158/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r3.claim: Mujahid explains iṣr as a covenant.
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} [البقرة: 286] قال: «عهدا»

TAB-FULL:v5p158/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses iṣr as a covenant.
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {إصرا} [البقرة: 286] يقول: «عهدا»

TAB-FULL:v5p158/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the covenant as the one imposed on the Jews before the Muslims.
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r5.anchor: عن السدي: {ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا} [البقرة: 286] «والإصر العهد الذي كان على من قبلنا من اليهود»

TAB-FULL:v5p158/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it is a covenant they could not bear; Jews and Christians failed to keep it and were destroyed.
TAB-FULL:v5p158/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} [البقرة: 286] قال: «عهدا لا نطيقه، ولا نستطيع القيام به»

TAB-FULL:v5p160/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r1.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r1.claim: Al-Rabiʿ glosses iṣr as a covenant, citing the same word in 3:81 as meaning God’s covenant.
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r1.anchor: عن الربيع: " الإصر: العهد " {وأخذتم على ذلكم إصري} [آل عمران: 81] قال: «عهدي»

TAB-FULL:v5p160/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains iṣr in 3:81 as God’s covenant.
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وأخذتم على ذلكم إصري} [آل عمران: 81] قال: «عهدي»

TAB-FULL:v5p160/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r3.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r3.claim: ʿAta interprets the prayer as asking not to be transformed into apes and swine as earlier peoples were.
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن عطاء بن أبي رباح، في قوله: {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا} [البقرة: 286] قال: «لا تمسخنا قردة وخنازير»

TAB-FULL:v5p160/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the prayer to ask that God not impose a sin without repentance or expiation.
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا} [البقرة: 286] «لا تحمل علينا ذنبا ليس فيه توبة ولا كفارة»

TAB-FULL:v5p160/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r5.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r5.claim: Al-Rabiʿ explains iṣr as the severe restrictions imposed on earlier People of the Book.
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r5.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: {ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا} [البقرة: 286] يقول: «التشديد الذي شددته على من قبلنا من أهل الكتاب»

TAB-FULL:v5p160/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r6.speaker: مالك
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r6.claim: Malik defines iṣr as a weighty or stringent command.
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r6.anchor: سألته، يعني مالكا، عن قوله: {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} [البقرة: 286] قال: " الإصر: الأمر الغليظ "

TAB-FULL:v5p160/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r7.claim: Ṭabarī distinguishes fatḥa-initial aṣr from the verse’s iṣr: aṣr can mean a bond of kinship that draws one toward another, as in Arabic usage.
TAB-FULL:v5p160/r7.anchor: فأما الأصر بفتح الألف: فهو ما عطف الرجل على غيره من رحم أو قرابة، يقال: أصرتني رحم بيني وبين فلان عليه

TAB-FULL:v5p163/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r1.claim: Ṭabarī prefers the request not to impose deeds too heavy to perform, reading it as a plea for ease in religious duties.
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r1.anchor: وإنما قلنا: إن تأويل ذلك: ولا تكلفنا من الأعمال ما لا نطيق القيام به

TAB-FULL:v5p163/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r2.claim: Qatadah takes the phrase as a plea not to impose the severe strictness imposed on earlier communities.
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: {ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} [البقرة: 286] «تشديد يشدد به كما شدد على من كان قبلكم»

TAB-FULL:v5p163/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says it asks not to be burdened with deeds beyond their capacity.
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك، قوله: {ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} [البقرة: 286] قال: «لا تحملنا من الأعمال ما لا نطيق»

TAB-FULL:v5p163/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets it as asking not to be obligated to follow a religion beyond their ability.
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} [البقرة: 286] «لا تفترض علينا من الدين ما لا طاقة لنا به، فنعجز عنه»

TAB-FULL:v5p163/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the unbearable burden as transformation into apes and swine.
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج: {ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} [البقرة: 286] «مسخ القردة والخنازير»

TAB-FULL:v5p163/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r6.speaker: سالم بن شابور
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r6.claim: Salim ibn Shabur glosses the unbearable burden as overpowering sexual desire.
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r6.anchor: عن سالم بن شابور، في قوله: {ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} [البقرة: 286] قال: «الغلمة»

TAB-FULL:v5p163/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r7.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r7.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the burden as the severe restrictions and prohibitions imposed on earlier people.
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r7.anchor: عن السدي: {ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} [البقرة: 286] «من التغليظ والأغلال التي كانت عليهم من التحريم»

TAB-FULL:v5p163/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r8.claim: Because this follows prayers for pardon over forgetfulness, error, and an unbearable covenant, Ṭabarī says the request for ease in religious duties best fits the context.
TAB-FULL:v5p163/r8.anchor: فكان إلحاق ذلك بمعنى ما قبله من مسألتهم التيسير في الدين أولى مما خالف ذلك المعنى

TAB-FULL:v5p164/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r1.claim: Ṭabarī says the believers ask pardon for falling short in commanded duties, so God will overlook the shortfall and not punish them, even when the duties are light.
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r1.anchor: يعفو لهم عن تقصير إن كان منهم في بعض ما أمرهم به من فرائضه

TAB-FULL:v5p164/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says pardon is sought for falling short in any of God’s commands.
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {واعف عنا} [البقرة: 286] قال: «اعف عنا إن قصرنا عن شيء من أمرك مما أمرتنا به»

TAB-FULL:v5p164/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r3.claim: Ṭabarī explains forgiveness as concealing a slip between the servant and God instead of exposing and disgracing the sinner.
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r3.anchor: واستر علينا زلة إن أتيناها فيما بيننا وبينك، فلا تكشفها ولا تفضحنا بإظهارها

TAB-FULL:v5p164/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd also applies the request for forgiveness to committing something God prohibited.
TAB-FULL:v5p164/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد {واغفر لنا} [البقرة: 286] «إن انتهكنا شيئا مما نهيتنا عنه»

TAB-FULL:v5p165/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p165/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p165/r1.claim: Ṭabarī says only God’s mercy saves people from punishment; deeds cannot save without mercy, so the prayer also asks for guidance to what pleases God.
TAB-FULL:v5p165/r1.anchor: فإنه ليس بناج من عقابك أحد إلا برحمتك إياه دون عمله، وليست أعمالنا منجيتنا إن أنت لم ترحمنا

TAB-FULL:v5p165/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p165/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p165/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says people can obey commands and leave prohibitions only through God’s mercy, and no one is saved except by it.
TAB-FULL:v5p165/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {وارحمنا} [البقرة: 286] قال: يقول: " لا ننال العمل بما أمرتنا به، ولا نترك ما نهيتنا عنه إلا برحمتك

TAB-FULL:v5p166/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r1.claim: Ṭabarī explains God as the believers’ ally and defender: they believe and obey, while He is faithful to the obedient and opposed to disbelievers; they ask victory as His party against those denying His oneness, worshipping rivals, and obeying Satan.
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r1.anchor: القوم الكافرين الذي جحدوا وحدانيتك، وعبدوا الآلهة والأنداد دونك، وأطاعوا في معصيتك الشيطان

TAB-FULL:v5p166/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r2.claim: Ṭabarī derives mawla as the form mafʿal from waliya; the yāʾ becomes alif because the preceding lām, the word’s second radical, is open.
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r2.anchor: والمولى في هذا الموضع المفعل من ولي فلان أمر فلان فهو يليه ولاية، وهو وليه ومولاه، وإنما صارت الياء من ولي ألفا لانفتاح اللام قبلها

TAB-FULL:v5p166/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that as the Prophet recited the end of 2:285 and 2:286, God answered each petition: forgiveness, no accountability, mercy, and victory.
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: {آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه} [البقرة: 285] قال: قرأها رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v5p166/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says Gabriel instructed the Prophet to recite each successive petition, then confirmed after each that it had been granted.
TAB-FULL:v5p166/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، قال: " أتى جبريل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: يا محمد قل: {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا}

TAB-FULL:v5p167/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r1.claim: Al-Suddi reports that Gabriel confirmed to Muhammad after each petition in 2:286 that God had granted it.
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r1.anchor: زعم السدي " أن هذه الآية حين نزلت

TAB-FULL:v5p167/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports God answering each of the petitions in the final verses with قد فعلت, meaning it has been granted.
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " أنزل الله عز وجل {آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه} [البقرة: 285] إلى قوله {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا}

TAB-FULL:v5p167/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r3.claim: Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet saying that God answered the plea not to hold believers accountable for forgetfulness or error with نعم.
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: " أنزل الله عز وجل {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا} [البقرة: 286]

TAB-FULL:v5p167/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports God affirming the supplications with قد فعلت.
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت

TAB-FULL:v5p167/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr adds that the closing verses of al-Baqara were granted to this community and not to earlier nations.
TAB-FULL:v5p167/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت

TAB-FULL:v5p169/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports God answering the Prophet’s recitation: He will not hold the believers accountable or burden them, and has pardoned, forgiven, shown mercy, and granted victory.
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله عز وجل {آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه} [البقرة: 285] إلى قوله. {غفرانك ربنا} [البقرة: 285] قال: «قد غفرت لكم»

TAB-FULL:v5p169/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says Gabriel told the Prophet to ask these petitions; God granted them specifically to the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا}

TAB-FULL:v5p169/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r3.speaker: معاذ
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r3.claim: Muʿadh used to say آمين after finishing this surah at its closing request for victory over the disbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v5p169/r3.anchor: أن معاذا، كان إذا فرغ من هذه السورة: {فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين} [البقرة: 286] قال: «آمين»

TABATABAI:2:285-286/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r1.claim: The sūra’s purpose is that true worship requires belief in all revelation without distinguishing among messengers; its opening and closing frame that theme.
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r1.anchor: من حق عبادة الله تعالى أن يؤمن بجميع ما أنزل على عباده بلسان رسله من غير تفرقة بين رسله

TABATABAI:2:285-286/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r2.claim: The account of Israel recalls God’s gifts of scripture, prophethood, and rule and Israel’s disobedience; the ending turns to believers seeking God’s help against unbelievers.
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r2.anchor: وفي السورة قصص تقص ما أنعم الله به على بني إسرائيل من أنواع نعمه من الكتاب والنبوة والملك

TABATABAI:2:285-286/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r3.claim: The sūra opens with the pious believing the unseen, praying, giving, accepting revelation, and affirming the afterlife, then contrasts unbelievers and hypocrites before closing with obedient believers.
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r3.anchor: فذكر أن المتقين من عباده يؤمنون بالغيب ويقيمون الصلاة وينفقون من رزق الله ويؤمنون بما أنزل الله

TABATABAI:2:285-286/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r4.claim: Israel faced heavy burdens and punishments, while the believers humbly ask not to be held to account for lapses or burdened as earlier peoples were, and ask forgiveness and victory.
TABATABAI:2:285-286/r4.anchor: وأن يعفو عنهم ويغفر لهم وينصرهم على القوم الكافرين

TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r1.speaker: ما ذكروه
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r1.claim: He rejects the view that these verses respond to 2:284’s accounting for hidden thoughts, record acceptance of an impossible duty, and then abrogate it; he prefers the sūra-wide reading.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r1.anchor: لا ما ذكروه أن الآيتين متعلقتا المضمون بقوله في الآية السابقة إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله

TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r2.claim: He cites the reported occasion that al-Baqara was the first sūra revealed in Medina as fitting the closing passage’s message.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r2.anchor: وما ذكرناه هو المناسب لما ذكروه في سبب النزول أن البقرة أول سورة نزلت بالمدينة

TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r3.claim: The setting he describes is the Anṣār’s full support for Islam and the emigrants’ sacrifice of family, children, wealth, and homeland to follow the Prophet, making divine praise apt.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r3.anchor: لما قارن الاستقبال التام من مؤمني الأنصار للدين الإلهي وقيامهم لنصرة رسول الله بالأموال والأنفس

TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r4.claim: The final request for victory over unbelievers hints that this prayer belongs to Islam’s early emergence.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#2/r4.anchor: فإن الجملة تؤمىء إلى أن سؤالهم هذا كان في أوائل ظهور الإسلام

TABATABAI:2:285-286#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#3/r4.claim: The text moves from each person’s individual faith to the group’s rejection of division, collective burdens, and plea for victory; faith belongs to individuals, while these events concern communities.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#3/r4.anchor: وقد بدأ تعالى بالإخبار عن حال كل واحد منهم على نعت الإفراد

TABATABAI:2:285-286#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#4/r2.claim: God has also granted servants a reciprocal claim upon Him: forgiveness, which every person, including prophets and messengers, needs for their own happiness.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#4/r2.anchor: وهو المغفرة التي لا يستغني عنه في سعادة نفسه أحد الأنبياء

TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r1.claim: Wasʿ means capacity; it first denotes spatial breadth, then metaphorically the capacity that contains a person’s possible acts.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r1.anchor: الوسع هو الجدة والطاقة، والأصل في الوسع هو السعة المكانية

TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r2.claim: Answering God through hearing and obedience applies only to what a person can understand and perform; incomprehensible or physically impossible acts cannot be obligations.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r2.anchor: فإجابة داعي الحق بالسمع والطاعة لا تتحقق إلا في ما هو اختياري للإنسان تتعلق به قدرته

TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r3.claim: He illustrates impossibility with being ordered to hear using sight, occupy more than one place, or be born again to one’s parents; no such act can receive a command of obedience.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r3.anchor: كأن يؤمر الإنسان أن يسمع ببصره، أو يحل بجسمه أزيد من مكان واحد، أو يتولد من أبويه مرة ثانية

TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r4.claim: Earning is evidence that a person acquires benefit or harm through acts that lie within their capacity.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r4.anchor: فالكسب نعم الدليل على أن ما كسبه الإنسان إنما وجده وتلبس به من طريق الوسع والطاقة

TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r5.claim: The verse states God’s customary practice: He does not require belief beyond understanding or obedience beyond human power, in keeping with rational beings’ practice.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r5.anchor: كلام جار على سنة الله الجارية بين عباده أن لا يكلفهم ما ليس في وسعهم من الإيمان بما هو فوق فهمهم

TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r6.claim: The clause connects backward by explaining that God asks no more than people can hear and obey.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r6.anchor: أما بالنسبة إلى ما تقدمها فإنها تفيد أن الله لا يكلف عباده بأزيد مما يمكنهم فيه السمع والطاعة

TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r7.claim: It connects forward by distinguishing the petitions about error, forgetfulness, and hardship from obligations beyond capacity.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r7.anchor: وأما بالنسبة إلى ما تأخر عنها فإنها تفيد أن ما سأله النبي والمؤمنون من عدم المؤاخذة على الخطأ والنسيان

TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r8.claim: Imposed hardship beyond capacity is punishment for rebellion, not a legal duty; error and forgetfulness are involuntary themselves but can arise through voluntary precursors.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#5/r8.anchor: فإن الذي يمكن أن يحمل عليهم مما لا طاقة لهم به ليس من قبيل التكليف، بل من قبيل جزاء التمرد والمعصية

TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r1.claim: God may prevent wrongdoing by blocking its means or requiring precaution; burdens imposed as punishment for a person's prior bad choice are not intrinsically impossible obligations.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r1.anchor: فمن الممكن أن يمنع عنهما مانع بالمنع عن مقدماتهما أو بإيجاب التحفظ عنهما

TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r2.claim: After their unqualified assent, the believers acknowledge their weakness and the fate of earlier peoples, asking for mercy because they have no power or protection apart from God.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r2.anchor: لما قالوا في مقام إجابة الدعوة سمعنا وأطعنا، وهو قول ينبئ عن الإجابة المطلقة من غير تقييد

TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r3.claim: Although the Prophet is protected from error and forgetfulness, he relies on God's protection and may ask for what he cannot secure from himself, joining the community of believers.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r3.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وإن كان معصوما من الخطأ والنسيان لكنه إنما يعتصم بعصمة الله

TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r4.claim: One reported definition of الإصر is a heavy burden.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r4.anchor: الإصر هو الثقل على ما قيل

TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r5.claim: Another reported definition is forcibly confining something; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this is close to burden, since confinement imposes what is disliked and heavy.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r5.anchor: وقيل هو حبس الشيء بقهره، وهو قريب من المعنى الأول

TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r6.claim: “Those before us” refers to the People of the Book, especially the Jews, as the sūra's stories and 7:157 suggest.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r6.anchor: والمراد بالذين من قبلنا هم أهل الكتاب وخاصة اليهود على ما تشير السورة

TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r7.claim: The plea concerns punishment for sins—unbearably hard duties, inflicted torment, or a scourge such as transformation—not an initial impossible duty, which reason excludes.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r7.anchor: ليس هو التكليف الابتدائي بما لا يطاق، إذ قد عرفت أن العقل لا يجوزه أبدا

TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r8.claim: The three pleas progress from specific effect to general source: pardon removes sin's effect or recorded punishment, forgiveness removes and veils its inward state, and mercy is God's gift covering both.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#6/r8.anchor: العفو محو أثر الشيء، والمغفرة ستره، والرحمة معروفة، وأما بحسب المصداق فاعتبار المعاني اللغوية يوجب أن يكون سوق الجمل الثلاث من قبيل التدرج

TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r1.claim: Because these three pleas follow the request not to be charged for forgetting or error, they concern sins arising from forgetfulness, error, and similar failings.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r1.anchor: على ما للجميع من السياق والنظم يشعر بأن المراد من العفو والمغفرة والرحمة ما يتعلق بذنوبهم

TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r2.claim: The requested forgiveness is specific to sin through error or forgetfulness, unlike the absolute “Your forgiveness, our Lord” answering the believers' absolute assent; the requests are not redundant.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r2.anchor: فإنه مغفرة مطلقة في مقابلة الإجابة المطلقة على ما تقدم

TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r3.claim: Repeating “our Lord” four times evokes divine mercy and recalls the speakers' servitude and abasement.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r3.anchor: وقد كرر لفظ الرب في هذه الأدعية أربع مرات لبعث صفة الرحمة بالإيماء والتلويح إلى صفة العبودية

TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r4.claim: Mawlā means a supporter who takes charge of the supported person's affairs, not just any helper; God is believers' guardian and protector.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r4.anchor: والمولى هو الناصر لكن لا كل ناصر بل الناصر الذي يتولى أمر المنصور

TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r5.claim: Their prayer shows that after assent to religion they turn to establishing and spreading it: calling to truth, striving, enjoining right, and uniting peoples to end division, a central purpose of religion.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#7/r5.anchor: وهذا الدعاء منهم يدل على أنهم ما كان لهم بعد السمع والطاعة لأصل الدين هم إلا في إقامته ونشره

TABATABAI:2:285-286#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:285-286#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:285-286#8/r1.claim: The petition shows that public calling to religion was the believers' first concern after committing themselves to hear and obey.
TABATABAI:2:285-286#8/r1.anchor: فقولهم أنت مولانا فانصرنا يدل على جعلهم الدعوة العامة في الدين أول ما يسبق إلى أذهانهم

TABRISI:2:286#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#2/r1.claim: Wusʿ is less than ṭāqa: capacity is what a person can bear without being constrained; akhṭaʾnā means committing an error or sin.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r1.anchor: الوسع ما دون الطاقة ويسمى ذلك وسعا بمعنى أنه يسع الإنسان

TABRISI:2:286#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:2:286#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says akhṭaʾa and khaṭiʾa are both Arabic forms, but the former can be sinful or non-sinful error while the latter means sin alone.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة أخطأ وخطئ لغتان والفرق بين أخطأ وخطئ

TABRISI:2:286#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#2/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses khaṭiʾū for sinning against what is right, witnessing the sin-specific sense of khaṭiʾa.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r3.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
والناس يلحون الأمير إذا هم

TABRISI:2:286#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#2/r4.claim: Iṣr means weight or burden; it can also denote a binding covenant or kinship tie.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r4.anchor: والأصر في اللغة الثقل قال النابغة

TABRISI:2:286#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r5.speaker: النابغة
TABRISI:2:286#2/r5.claim: Al-Nābigha's poetry uses iṣr for the burden of protecting one's people from oppression.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r5.anchor:
قال النابغة:
يا مانع الضيم أن يغشى سراتهم

TABRISI:2:286#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r6.speaker: النابغة
TABRISI:2:286#2/r6.claim: Al-Nābigha also uses iṣr to mean a covenant or binding promise.

TABRISI:2:286#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r7.speaker: الكميت
TABRISI:2:286#2/r7.claim: Al-Kumayt's verse uses āṣirat al-arḥām for the bond of kinship.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r7.anchor:
قال الكميت:
نضحت أديم الود بيني وبينهم

TABRISI:2:286#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#2/r8.claim: God commands or forbids only what a person can do; another explanation says He requires ease rather than hardship and does not exhaust capacity.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r8.anchor: لا يأمر ولا ينهى أحدا إلا ما هو له مستطيع
