TABRISI:2:286#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r9.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
TABRISI:2:286#2/r9.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna calls it a good interpretation that God does not impose a person's full limit of capacity, which would exhaust their effort.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r9.anchor: عن سفيان بن عيينة وهذا قول حسن

TABRISI:2:286#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#2/r10.claim: The verse disproves the Mujabbira's allowance of obligations beyond ability: capacity lies within human power, beyond which effort is exhausted.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r10.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على بطلان قول المجبرة في تجويز تكليف العبد ما لا يطيقه

TABRISI:2:286#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#2/r11.claim: The alternative that wusʿ means only what is permitted is mistaken: it makes the command circular, since every command itself permits the commanded act.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن معناه إلا ما يسعها ويحل لها وهذا خطأ

TABRISI:2:286#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#2/r12.claim: A person receives the reward of obedience and bears the consequence of sins; both may be called earnings because they result from one's acts.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r12.anchor: معناه لها ثواب ما كسبت من الطاعات

TABRISI:2:286#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r13.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:286#2/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan understands the prayer as an instruction to say these words, teaching believers how to supplicate.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r13.anchor: قيل تقديره قولوا ربنا على جهة التعليم للدعاء عن الحسن

TABRISI:2:286#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#2/r14.claim: Another reading supplies they say, presenting the words as reported praise and supplication.
TABRISI:2:286#2/r14.anchor: وقيل تقديره يقولون ربنا على جهة الحكاية والثناء

TABRISI:2:286#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#3/r1.claim: One interpretation takes forgetting as abandoning obedience and error as committing sins, even deliberately; the prayer seeks forgiveness for neglected duties and wrongful acts.
TABRISI:2:286#3/r1.anchor: أي تركوا طاعته فتركهم من ثوابه

TABRISI:2:286#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#3/r2.claim: The author cites 9:67 and 2:44 for nasiya meaning abandonment, and an unnamed poet who uses nāsiyan for leaving off spear thrusts in battle.
TABRISI:2:286#3/r2.anchor:
ومنه قول الشاعر:
ولم أك عند الجود للجود قاليا

TABRISI:2:286#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#3/r3.claim: A second reading asks pardon if people expose themselves to circumstances that cause forgetfulness or error about a command or duty.
TABRISI:2:286#3/r3.anchor: أن معنى قوله إن نسينا أن تعرضنا لأسباب يقع عندها النسيان

TABRISI:2:286#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#3/r4.claim: A third reading means accidentally failing an obligation or unintentionally doing a forbidden act; the plea expresses humility even though such acts are not punished.
TABRISI:2:286#3/r4.anchor: لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أي إن لم نفعل فعلا يجب فعله على سبيل السهو

TABRISI:2:286#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#3/r5.claim: This humble appeal resembles the following plea not to impose what people cannot bear, which may also be devotional.
TABRISI:2:286#3/r5.anchor: ويجري ذلك مجرى قوله فيما بعد

TABRISI:2:286#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
TABRISI:2:286#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAṭāʾ understand it as asking not to be punished for disobedience, whether done in ignorance or deliberately.
TABRISI:2:286#3/r6.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس وعطاء أن معناه لا تعاقبنا إن عصينا جاهلين أو متعمدين

TABRISI:2:286#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والربيع والسدي
TABRISI:2:286#3/r7.claim: One explanation asks God not to impose a duty people cannot carry out or punish them for abandoning or violating it.
TABRISI:2:286#3/r7.anchor: لا تحمل علينا عملا نعجز عن القيام به ولا تعذبنا بتركه ونقضه

TABRISI:2:286#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#3/r8.speaker: الربيع ومالك وعطاء
TABRISI:2:286#3/r8.claim: A second explanation, reported from al-Rabīʿ, Mālik, and ʿAṭāʾ, asks God not to make the religious burden too heavy or strict.
TABRISI:2:286#3/r8.anchor: لا تحمل علينا ثقلا عن الربيع ومالك وعطاء يعني لا تشدد الأمر علينا

TABRISI:2:286#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#4/r1.claim: Earlier communities were punished for sins, had lawful foods forbidden, and received heavier covenants and obligations; this community's lighter burden is a mercy.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r1.anchor: لأنهم كانوا إذا ارتكبوا خطيئة عليهم عقوبتها وحرم عليهم بسببها ما أحل لهم من الطعام

TABRISI:2:286#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#4/r2.claim: The ban on good foods for the earlier community is illustrated by 4:160, which says they were forbidden lawful good things because of wrongdoing.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r2.anchor:
كما قال تعالى
فبظلم من الذين هادوا

TABRISI:2:286#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#4/r3.claim: One explanation asks not to be burdened with crushing duties or trials, such as killing oneself as repentance for sin.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r3.anchor: أن معناه ما يثقل علينا تحمله من أنواع التكاليف والامتحان

TABRISI:2:286#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#4/r4.claim: A second explanation asks protection from punishment that people cannot endure in this life or the next.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r4.anchor: والثاني: بمعناه ما لا طاقة لنا به من العذاب عاجلا وآجلا

TABRISI:2:286#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#4/r5.claim: A third explanation treats this as devotional petition, though God does not impose on anyone a burden beyond their capacity.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r5.anchor: والثالث: أنه على سبيل التعبد وإن كان تعالى لا يكلف ولا يحمل أحدا

TABRISI:2:286#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#4/r6.claim: The prayer asks God to pardon sins, cover errors, and show mercy through blessing in this world, pardon in the next, and admission to Paradise.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r6.anchor: ذنوبنا { واغفر لنا } خطايانا أي استرها

TABRISI:2:286#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#4/r7.claim: Mawlānā means our protector, the one entitled to direct our affairs, and our helper.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r7.anchor: أي ولينا وأولى بالتصرف فينا وناصرنا

TABRISI:2:286#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:286#4/r8.claim: The final plea asks God to help believers overcome unbelievers by force and by the strength of their argument.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r8.anchor: أي أعنا عليهم بالقهر لهم والغلبة بالحجة عليهم

TABRISI:2:286#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r9.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:286#4/r9.claim: A report from the Prophet says that at every section of this supplication God answers, I have done so and granted it.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r9.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TABRISI:2:286#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r10.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:286#4/r10.claim: A well-known Prophetic report says whoever recites the final two verses of al-Baqara at night is sufficed for that night's vigil.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r10.anchor: ففي الحديث المشهور عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

TABRISI:2:286#4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:2:286#4/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that during the Night Journey the Prophet reached the Lote Tree, received the five prayers and the final verses of al-Baqara, and his community's monotheists were forgiven except for grave sins.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r11.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن مسعود قال:

TABRISI:2:286#4/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r12.speaker: ابن المنكدر
TABRISI:2:286#4/r12.claim: Ibn al-Munkadir transmits from the Prophet that the final verses of al-Baqara are Qur'an and supplication and please the Merciful.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r12.anchor: وعن ابن المنكدر رفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

TABRISI:2:286#4/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:286#4/r13.claim: In al-Kalbī's tafsir report from Ibn ʿAbbās, an angel announces two lights not given to a prophet before—the Opening and the end of al-Baqara—and says reciters will receive their request.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r13.anchor: وفي تفسير الكلبي بإسناده ذكره عن ابن عباس قال بينا رسول الله إذ سمع نقيضا

TABRISI:2:286#4/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:286#4/r14.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:2:286#4/r14.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that when a man learned Sūrat al-Baqara, he became earnest and respected among the community.
TABRISI:2:286#4/r14.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قال: كان الرجل إذا تعلم سورة البقرة

THALABI:v2p305/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p305/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p305/r6.claim: The verse answers an implicit plea about what the believers have been required to bear: God requires of a soul only what it can manage.
THALABI:v2p305/r6.anchor: ظاهر الآية قضاء الحوائج، وفيها إضمار السؤال والحاجة

THALABI:v2p305/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p305/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p305/r7.claim: وسع is what a person can encompass or manage; another gloss connects it with what is difficult and strenuous.

THALABI:v2p305/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p305/r8.speaker: إبراهيم ابن أبي عبلة الشامي
THALABI:v2p305/r8.claim: He reads وسعها with fatḥa on waw and kasra on sin as a verb, meaning God’s command encompassed the soul, or ‘what encompassed it’ with ما omitted.
THALABI:v2p305/r8.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم ابن أبي عبلة الشامي: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها

THALABI:v2p305/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p305/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء والسدي وأكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v2p305/r9.claim: They say this answered believers’ fear that they could not repent of involuntary inner thoughts after 2:284; such thoughts exceeded their capacity.
THALABI:v2p305/r9.anchor: فقال ابن عطاء والسدي وأكثر المفسرين: أراد به حديث النفس

THALABI:v2p305/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p305/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p305/r10.claim: In another account, the verse concerns believers specifically: God eased religious duties and required only what they can do, as shown by verses affirming ease, no hardship, and duty according to capacity.
THALABI:v2p305/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية أخرى: [ ... ] المؤمنون خاصة وسع الله عليهم أمر دينهم

THALABI:v2p306/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r1.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
THALABI:v2p306/r1.claim: Sufyan glosses capacity as ease rather than hardship: God did not require the soul’s full strength, since that would exhaust it; al-Tha'labi calls this a good view because capacity is below full ability.
THALABI:v2p306/r1.anchor: فقال: إلا يسرها لا عسرها، ولم يكلفها طاقتها

THALABI:v2p306/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r2.speaker: بعض أهل الكلام
THALABI:v2p306/r2.claim: Some theologians understand the phrase as only requiring what is lawful and within a person’s permitted scope.
THALABI:v2p306/r2.anchor: فقال بعض أهل الكلام: يعني إلا ما يسعها ويحل لها

THALABI:v2p306/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p306/r3.claim: Good deeds belong to the soul with their reward, while its evil deeds and their burden are against it.
THALABI:v2p306/r3.anchor: لها ما كسبت. أي للنفس ما عملت من الخير والعمل الصالح

THALABI:v2p306/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v2p306/r5.claim: Although the verb is in a reciprocal form, it describes one actor: the sinner has effectively opened a way for the punisher and thus shares in the taking to account.
THALABI:v2p306/r5.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: وإنما خرج على لفظ المفاعلة وهو فعل واحد

THALABI:v2p306/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r6.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p306/r6.claim: One view reads forgetting literally; al-Kalbi explains that Israelites were punished when they forgot or erred, with foods or drinks forbidden in proportion to the offense, and believers were taught to ask for exemption.
THALABI:v2p306/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي: كانت بنو إسرائيل إذا نسوا شيئا مما أمروا به وأخطئوا

THALABI:v2p306/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r7.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p306/r7.claim: Another view understands forgetting as abandoning or neglecting; al-Tha'labi prefers the literal sense, though he cites 9:67 for the alternative usage.
THALABI:v2p306/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو من النسيان الذي هو الترك والإغفال.

THALABI:v2p306/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r8.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p306/r8.claim: Some take أخطأنا as deliberate intention, using خطيء for someone who sins intentionally; a line by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt illustrates the usage.
THALABI:v2p306/r8.anchor: جعله بعضهم من القصد والعمد، يقال: خطيء فلان إذا تعمد

THALABI:v2p306/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r9.speaker: الآخرون
THALABI:v2p306/r9.claim: Others take it as unintentional ignorance or oversight, which al-Tha'labi calls more correct because deliberate sin is not automatically forgiven, though it remains subject to God’s will unless it is unbelief.
THALABI:v2p306/r9.anchor: وجعله الآخرون من الخطأ الذي هو الجهل والسهو وهو الأصح لأن ما كان عمدا من الذنب غير معفو عنه

THALABI:v2p306/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p306/r10.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v2p306/r10.claim: Ata glosses the phrase as ‘if we were ignorant or did it deliberately.’
THALABI:v2p306/r10.anchor: قال عطاء: إن نسينا أو أخطأنا. يعني إن جهلنا أو تعمدنا له

THALABI:v2p307/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p307/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v2p307/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd applies forgetting to neglecting a required duty and error to doing something forbidden.
THALABI:v2p307/r1.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إن نسينا شيئا مما افترضته علينا

THALABI:v2p307/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p307/r2.speaker: الزهري
THALABI:v2p307/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that Umar corrected a man’s prayer for forgiveness of his errors, saying errors are forgiven and he should ask forgiveness for deliberate acts.
THALABI:v2p307/r2.anchor: وقال الزهري: سمع عمر رجلا يقول: اللهم [اغفر] لي خطاياي

THALABI:v2p307/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p307/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p307/r3.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying that error, forgetfulness, and what people are coerced into have been lifted from his community.
THALABI:v2p307/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما أكرهوا عليه»

THALABI:v2p307/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p307/r4.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء وقتادة والضحاك والربيع ومقاتل والسدي والكلبي وابن جريج والفراء
THALABI:v2p307/r4.claim: This group glosses إصر as an unbearable covenant or pledge, whose breach brought punishment on earlier people, especially the Jews; they cite 3:81’s use of إصر for a covenant.
THALABI:v2p307/r4.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد وعطاء وقتادة والضحاك والربيع ومقاتل والسدي والكلبي وابن جريج والفراء

THALABI:v2p307/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p307/r5.speaker: عثمان بن عطاء ومالك بن أنس وأبو عبيدة والمؤرخ والقتيبي وابن الأنباري
THALABI:v2p307/r5.claim: Another group glosses إصر as a burden or severity and asks that burdens like those imposed on the Jews not be laid on believers; examples include fifty prayers, alms on profits, cutting away impurity, and sins displayed at the door. They connect it to 7:157.
THALABI:v2p307/r5.anchor: وهذا معنى قول عثمان بن عطاء ومالك بن أنس وأبي عبيدة والمؤرخ والقتيبي وابن الأنباري

THALABI:v2p307/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p307/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v2p307/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the plea is not to impose a sin for which there is no repentance or expiation; the word can also mean a tie or bond.
THALABI:v2p307/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: معناه: لا تحمل علينا ذنبا ليس فيه توبة ولا كفارة

THALABI:v2p307/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p307/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p307/r7.claim: The word can name what binds things together, a kinship bond, or a relationship formed by covenant; the cited poem uses آصرة for such a tie.
THALABI:v2p307/r7.anchor: ويقال للشيء الذي تعقد به الأشياء: الأصر

THALABI:v2p308/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p308/r1.claim: The poem’s آصرة is evidence for the word’s sense of a bond or tie between people.

THALABI:v2p308/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r2.speaker: قتادة والضحاك والسدي وابن زيد
THALABI:v2p308/r2.claim: They take the plea to mean: do not require deeds beyond our ability.
THALABI:v2p308/r2.anchor: أي لا تكلفنا من الأعمال مالا نطيق، هذا قول قتادة والضحاك والسدي وابن زيد

THALABI:v2p308/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r3.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p308/r3.claim: Another view applies the phrase to inner speech and whisperings.
THALABI:v2p308/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو حديث النفس والوسوسة

THALABI:v2p308/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
THALABI:v2p308/r4.claim: Ibrahim, in a report from Sufyan al-Thawri through Mansur, glosses it as hardship.
THALABI:v2p308/r4.anchor: سفيان الثوري عن منصور عن إبراهيم في قوله تعالى ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به. قال: المشقة

THALABI:v2p308/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r5.speaker: محمد بن عبد الوهاب
THALABI:v2p308/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab interprets the unbearable burden as passionate love.
THALABI:v2p308/r5.anchor: سمعت محمد بن عبد الوهاب ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به. قال: يعني العشق

THALABI:v2p308/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r6.speaker: خباب
THALABI:v2p308/r6.claim: Khabbab recounts that eleven people died during a gathering where Dhu al-Nun al-Misri spoke of divine love and its overpowering effects on lovers.
THALABI:v2p308/r6.anchor: قال خباب: حضرت مجلس ذي النون المصري في فسطاطه

THALABI:v2p308/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r7.speaker: يحيى
THALABI:v2p308/r7.claim: Yahya says he would not punish lovers because their sins arise from compulsion rather than choice.
THALABI:v2p308/r7.anchor: وقال يحيى: لو تركت العقوبة بيدي يوم القيامة ما عذبت العشاق

THALABI:v2p308/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
THALABI:v2p308/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the unbearable burden with transformation into apes and swine.
THALABI:v2p308/r8.anchor: قال ابن جريج: هو مسخ القردة والخنازير

THALABI:v2p308/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r9.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p308/r9.claim: Another interpretation is that enemies gloat over the afflicted person.

THALABI:v2p308/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p308/r10.speaker: وهب بن منبه
THALABI:v2p308/r10.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih reports that Job said the hardest part of his long affliction was his enemies’ gloating.
THALABI:v2p308/r10.anchor: وروى عبد المنعم بن إدريس عن أبيه عن وهب بن منبه قال: قيل لأيوب عليه السلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r1.claim: Takallafa means to impose a burden; takalluf is the verb, and kulfa is the noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r1.anchor: يقال: كلفته الشيء فتكلف، والكلفة الاسم منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r2.claim: Al-Farra says wusʿ is a noun like wajd and jahd, meaning what a person can accommodate without being squeezed or burdened.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r2.anchor: والوسع، قال الفراء: هو اسم، كالوجد والجهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and most exegetes say this verse abrogated the burden of involuntary thoughts and whispers imposed by the earlier verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r3.anchor: وابن عباس (¬4) وأكثر المفسرين على أن هذه الآية نسخت ما ضج المؤمنون عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r4.claim: In another transmission, Ibn Abbas says God imposed only what believers can do, citing God's desire for ease, removal of hardship, and the command to fear Him as able.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r4.anchor: وروي عنه من طريق آخر، أنه قال: معناه: أنه كلف المؤمنين ما هم له مستطيعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r5.claim: The best explanation is that capacity here is below full ability: God graciously burdens people with less than their maximum; Sufyan ibn Uyayna glosses it as ease, since a full-capacity burden would exhaust them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r5.anchor: وهذا أحسن ما قيل في (¬1) تفسير هذه الآية (¬2)، وذلك أن الوسع دون الطاقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r6.speaker: القدرية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r6.claim: The Qadari objection is that if God decrees someone's disbelief yet commands faith, He has burdened that person with what is beyond his capacity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r6.anchor: وتقول القدرية: إن الله تعالى أخبر أنه لا يكلف العبد إلا ما يسعه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r7.claim: The author answers that the same objection applies to foreknowledge: if God's prior knowledge says someone will die an unbeliever, that person cannot change it; al-Shafiʿi says the Qadari are defeated if they concede foreknowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p532/r7.anchor: فيقال لهم: يلزمكم مثل هذا في العلم، لأنكم توافقوننا على أن الله تعالى إذا سبق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r1.claim: The correct linguistic view is that kasb and iktisab are synonymous; Dhu al-Rumma uses both forms for earning in one line.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r1.anchor: الصحيح عند أهل اللغة: أن الكسب والاكتساب واحد، لا فرق بينهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r2.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r2.claim: Some say iktisab is narrower: kasb may benefit oneself or another, while iktisab is only for oneself; one can be a provider for family but not an iktisab-earner for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الاكتساب أخص من الكسب؛ لأن الكسب ينقسم إلى كسبه لنفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r3.claim: Each person is accountable for their own earnings and is not punished for another person's sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r3.anchor: ومعنى {لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت} أي: لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r4.claim: Al-Hasan takes the prayer opening as an instruction: say, Our Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا} قال الحسن: معناه: قولوا: ربنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r5.claim: Another explanation treats it as reported speech: they say, Our Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r5.anchor: وقيل: أي: يقولون: ربنا. على الخبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r6.claim: La tuʾakhidhna means do not punish us.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r7.claim: The reciprocal verb is used though punishment has one agent: the sinner exposes himself and opens the way through his own deed, as if helping the punisher seize him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p533/r7.anchor: وإنما جاء بلفظ المفاعلة وهو فعل واحد؛ لأن المسيء قد أمكن من نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says Israelites were punished immediately when they forgot, so believers ask God not to hold them accountable for forgetfulness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r1.anchor: قاله الكلبي، وهو أن بني إسرائيل كانوا إذا نسوا شيئا عجلت لهم العقوبة بذلك، فأمر الله نبيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r2.claim: Even when religious law excuses forgetfulness, believers may still be taught to pray for pardon, as prophets and angels petition for things God will certainly grant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r2.anchor: بأن ندعو بذلك، كما جاء في الدعاء: {قال رب احكم بالحق} [الأنبياء: 112]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r3.claim: Here forgetting can mean abandoning an obligation; in 9:67, people abandon God's service and are left without reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p535/r3.anchor: بمعنى: الترك، فيكون معنى قوله: {إن نسينا} أي: تركنا شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r1.claim: The correct linguistic distinction is خطئ for intentional sin and أخطأ for failing to hit the right answer; Abu al-Haytham likewise distinguishes deliberate from accidental acts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r1.anchor: الصحيح في اللغة: أن يقال: خطئ الرجل: إذا أثم، فهو خاطئ آثم. وأخطأ: إذا لم يصب الصواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r2.claim: If أخطأنا means an inadvertent slip, it shares the two explanations given for forgetfulness, including Al-Kalbi's account of immediate punishment for Israelites.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r2.anchor: أحدهما: قول الكلبي (¬1) والثاني: أنا تعبدنا بهذا الدعاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r3.claim: The supplication for pardon over inadvertent error is also a devotional prayer believers are instructed to make.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda treats أخطأ and خطئ as two forms of one word, citing poetry; on this reading the verse asks pardon for deliberate sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: يقال: أخطأ وخطئ لغتان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r5.claim: Isr fundamentally conveys binding or attachment; it names burdens, covenants, and kin ties, supported by poetry and by the covenant called isr in 3:81.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r5.anchor: فالأصل في هذا الحرف الإصر بمعنى العطف، ثم يسمى الثقل والعهد إصرا لما فيهما من العطف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, in reports from Al-Walibi, Ata, and Atiyya, and Mujahid, Qatada, Muqatil, Al-Suddi, Al-Kalbi, and Al-Farra say it means an unbearable covenant whose breach brought punishment on the Jews.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p536/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي وعطاء وعطية (¬1): يعنى: عهدا وميثاقا لا نطيقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r1.claim: Ṭāqa is a verbal noun from iṭāqa, like ṭāʿa from iṭāʿa, and can stand in place of the verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r1.anchor: الطاقة: اسم من الإطاقة، كالطاعة (¬10) من الإطاعة، والجابة من الإجابة، وهي توضع موضع المصدر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r2.claim: One explanation is that the petition asks God not to subject them to Hellfire, whose punishment no one can bear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r2.anchor: أي: من العذاب، كأنهم سألوا الله تعالى أن لا يعذبهم بالنار، فإنه لا طاقة لأحد مع عذاب الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r3.claim: Another explanation is a burden that is technically possible but onerous and painful; Arabs say they cannot bear someone's sight despite being physically able, as in 11:20.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r3.anchor: أي: ما يثقل علينا أداؤه، وإن كنا مطيقين له بعد التجشم وتحمل (¬1) المكروه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes explain Mawlana as our helper or protector, as in the verses calling God the believers' wali or mawla.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: أي: ناصرنا (¬3)، ومثله: {الله ولي الذين آمنوا} [البقرة: 257]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r5.claim: Mawla in the sense of aid derives from closeness and connection; wali and mawla are equivalent, as in God's being with the believers as their helper.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r5.anchor: ومعنى المولى: من النصرة، من ولي عليه، وولي منه: إذا اتصل به ولم ينفصل عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r6.speaker: يونس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r6.claim: Yunus explains the Prophet's saying Whoever has me as his mawla, Ali is his mawla to mean whoever has me as his wali.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r7.claim: The report calling Muzayna, Juhayna, Aslam, and Ghifar God's and His Messenger's mawali means they are His allies; Al-Ajjaj's verse likewise uses mawali for allies of truth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r8.claim: Anyone joined to you and protected by your strength is your mawla; this explains calling paternal kin mawali, while poetry distinguishes allied clients from relatives and mawla can mean a guardian of one's affairs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p540/r8.anchor: وكل من انضم إليك فعز بعزك وامتنع بمنعتك (¬4)، فهو مولاك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r1.claim: God is our wali by helping us and by directing our affairs; the verb is wali, yali, wilayah, making Him wali and mawla.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r1.anchor: فمعنى قوله: أنت مولانا أي: أنت ولينا بنصرك إيانا، وأنت الذي تلي علينا أمورنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r2.claim: Muqatil reports that during the Night Journey the Prophet received the closing verses of Baqara; angels urged him to ask, Gabriel taught this prayer, and Gabriel answered after each section that God had granted it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل بن سليمان: لما أسري بالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلى السماء، أعطي خواتيم سورة البقرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God answers the prayer section by section: He will not hold them accountable or impose burdens, and has pardoned, forgiven, shown mercy, and granted victory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس في قول الله عز وجل: {غفرانك ربنا} قال: قد غفرت لكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says God placed this prayer of the Prophet and believers in scripture so later generations could preserve and frequently recite it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: هذا الدعاء أخبر الله عز وجل به عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والمؤمنين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r5.claim: The requested victory includes establishing the proof, prevailing in war and other affairs, and making the religion manifest over every religion as promised.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p543/r5.anchor: انصرنا عليهم في إقامة الحجة، وفي غلبتنا إياهم في حربهم وسائر أمورهم

QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r1.claim: God assigns each self only the unveilings and manifestations its vessel can bear, according to primordial preparedness granted through the holiest effusion.
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r1.anchor: حظ كل أحد من الكشوف والتجليات ما يطيق به وعاء استعداده الموهوب له في الأزل

QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r2.claim: Good works, knowledge, perfections, and unveilings belong to the self, intentionally acquired or not, as goods are native to its luminous essence; dark ignorance, vice, and sin are alien and incur liability only when deliberately pursued.
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r2.anchor: فإنها من عالم النور فالخيرات كلها ذاتية لها، ترجع فائدتها إليها دون الشرور من الجهالات والرذائل والمعاصي

QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r3.claim: A report says the angel on the right records each good deed immediately, while the angel on the left waits six hours; repentance, seeking forgiveness, or remorse prevents recording the sin.
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r3.anchor: إن صاحب اليمين يكتب كل حسنة تصدر عن صاحبها في الحال

QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r4.claim: Here nafs means the self or essence, not the lower soul; kasb marks good that is not deliberately sought, while iktisab marks evil actively pursued by the lower soul.
QASHANI:2:285-286#2/r4.anchor: والمراد بالنفس ها هنا الذات وإلا لكان الأمر بالعكس، فيكون حينئذ معناه لا يكلفها

QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r1.claim: Forgetting is forgetting the covenant and error is acting for other than God while veiled from Him; the prayer describes spiritual strangers far from Him, tested in darkness, with no standing of their own before Him.
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r1.anchor: في العمل لما سواك، والقران على فراقك محتجبين عنك

QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r2.claim: The burden is their own essences, attributes, and acts, which bind and exile them from God; no weight is heavier.
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r2.anchor: في ذاتنا وصفاتنا وأفعالنا، فتأصرنا وتحبسنا في مكاننا مهجورين عنك

QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r3.claim: Earlier peoples were veiled either by the outward realm of acts or by the inward realm of attributes.
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r3.anchor: من المحتجبين بظواهر الأفعال أو بواطن الصفات

QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r4.claim: What they cannot bear is the weight of estrangement and deprivation from divine nearness and witnessing God's beauty, behind veils of majesty.
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r4.anchor: من ثقل الهجران والحرمان عن وصالك، ومشاهدة جمالك، بحجب جلالك

QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r5.claim: Pardon means overlooking bad actions and attributes, which veil them from God and deprive them of the coolness of pardon and the pleasure of divine approval.
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r5.anchor: سيئات أفعالنا وصفاتنا فإنها كلها سيئات حجبتنا عنك، وحرمتنا برد عفوك ولذة رضوانك

QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r6.claim: Forgiveness is sought for the sin of separate existence, which a quoted verse of poetry calls a sin without equal.
QASHANI:2:285-286#3/r6.anchor: ذنوب وجوداتنا فإنها أكبر الكبائر كما قيل

QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r1.claim: Mercy means receiving gifted existence after annihilation.

QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r2.claim: God is their patron as helper and steward of their affairs, or their master, who is bound to support His servants.
QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r2.anchor: ومن حق السيد أن ينصر عبيده

QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r3.claim: The enemies are the powers and attributes of the commanding self and the armies of satanic imaginings and fancies, veiled from God and obscuring the seekers through disbelief and darkness.
QASHANI:2:285-286#4/r3.anchor: من قوى نفوسنا الأمارة وصفاتها، وجنود شياطين أوهامنا وخيالاتنا، المحجوبين عنك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r5.claim: This verse abrogates the believers' complaint about being held to account for intrusive thoughts and inner speech.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r5.anchor: ذكرنا أن هذه الآية نسخت ما شكاه المؤمنون من المحاسبة بالوسوسة وحديث النفس

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r6.claim: What one earns is obedience; what one bears is sin, and nobody is charged with another's sin.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r6.anchor: { لها ما كسبت } [من العمل بالطاعة] { وعليها ما اكتسبت } [من العمل بالإثم] أي: لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r7.claim: This is taught supplication asking not to be punished for forgetfulness; Israelites faced immediate punishment when forgetting a prescription.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r7.anchor: { ربنا لا تؤاخذنا } أي: قولوا ذلك على التعليم للدعاء، ومعناه: لا تعاقبنا إن نسينا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r8.claim: The Israelites faced immediate punishment when they forgot a prescription, so the Prophet and believers were taught to ask not to be held accountable for this.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r8.anchor: كانت بنو إسرائيل إذا نسوا شيئا مما شرع لهم عجلت لهم العقوبة بذلك، فأمر الله نبيه والمؤمنين أن يسألوه ترك مؤاخذتهم بذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r9.claim: To err means to miss what is correct.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r10.claim: Isr means a burden; they ask not to be given a heavy command like those imposed on the Israelites.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r10.anchor: { ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا } أي: ثقلا، والمعنى: لا تحمل علينا أمرا يثقل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r11.claim: The burdensome commands imposed on those before include the loads prescribed for the Israelites.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r11.anchor: { كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا } نحو ما أمر به بنو إسرائيل من الأثقال التي كانت عليهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r12.claim: They ask God not to punish them with the Fire.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r12.anchor: { ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به } أي: لا تعذبنا بالنار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r13.claim: God is their helper and manager of affairs; they ask to prevail in arguments, war, and other affairs so their religion triumphs as promised.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r13.anchor: { أنت مولانا } [ناصرنا] والذي تلي علينا أمورنا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r14.claim: They ask for victory in argument, war, and other affairs, and for their religion to prevail as promised.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:285-286/r14.anchor: في إقامة حجتنا وغلبتنا إياهم في حربه، وسائر أمورهم

ELMALILI:2:286/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r1.claim: God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, even though He could; duties stay below capacity without strain or hardship, as affirmed by 2:185, because of grace and mercy.
ELMALILI:2:286/r1.anchor: Allah kimseye vüs‘undan başkasını teklif etmez. Edemez değil, etmez.

ELMALILI:2:286/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r2.claim: God's obligations leave capacity beyond what is required, allowing rest and voluntary good deeds after duties; the five daily prayers do not exhaust a person's ability to act.
ELMALILI:2:286/r2.anchor: Bu suretle Allah’ın mükelleflere bahşettiği kudret ve tâkat yaptığı tekliflerden geniştir.

ELMALILI:2:286/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r3.claim: Taklīf means laying a burden upon the will; every burden requires enabling power, and the duty must not strain that power.
ELMALILI:2:286/r3.anchor: Gerçi teklif, irâdeye tahmîl-i külfet demektir, her külfet ise bir kudret sarfını iktizâ eder.

ELMALILI:2:286/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r4.claim: Individual obligations scale with differing capacities, which is justice and equality of rights: zakat is absent for the poor and varies by wealth while remaining at one rate, unlike a flat per-person levy.
ELMALILI:2:286/r4.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh efrâdın kudretleri mütefâvit olduğundan kudret ve istitâ‘atleri fazla olanların merâtib-i mükellefiyetleri de fazla olacaktır ki adalet ve müsâvât-ı hukūk da budur.

ELMALILI:2:286/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r5.claim: The same capacity principle governs how communal obligations fall on individuals, and the total duties assigned to one person must not exceed that person's capacity.
ELMALILI:2:286/r5.anchor: Sonra bir şahsın uhdesine teveccüh eden tekâlîfin mecmû‘u hesap edildiği zaman dahi kudretini geçmemelidir.

ELMALILI:2:286/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r6.claim: Some duties require not only enabling capacity without hardship but an additional, facilitative capacity grounded in greater ease.
ELMALILI:2:286/r6.anchor: Bunun için bazı tekâlîfte bilâ harac kudret-i mümekkineden başka bir de kudret-i müyessire denilen, yani daha ziyade kolaylık esasına istinad eden kudret de şart olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:286/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r7.claim: Elmalılı summarizes the greatest principle of legislative wisdom as duties being proportionate to the capacity of the person charged.
ELMALILI:2:286/r7.anchor: Velhâsıl bu âyet hikmet-i teşrî‘in en büyük esasını fezleke etmiştir: Teklif mükellefin vüs‘uyla mütenâsibdir.

ELMALILI:2:286/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r8.claim: Al-Qāmūs glosses kesb, iktisāb, and tekassub as seeking provision or something beneficial even without obtaining it; in Turkish, kesb here is working or exerting power.
ELMALILI:2:286/r8.anchor: Kāmûs’ta dahi gösterildiği üzere evvelâ “kesb”, “iktisab”, “tekessüb” taleb-i rızktır, yani intifâ‘edecek, haz alacak bir şey istemek ve aramaktır

ELMALILI:2:286/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r9.claim: If kesb and iktisāb are synonymous, the contrast between benefit and liability comes from their objects; the first mā is read as commanded good and the second as forbidden evil.
ELMALILI:2:286/r9.anchor: Bu nokta-i nazardan مَا كَسَبَتْ’teki ما ile مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ’teki ما’nın mânaları tefrik edilerek evvelki Allah’ın teklif ettiği hayır, ikinci nehyettiği şer ile tefsir edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:286/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r10.claim: Kesb can mean successfully attaining what one sought, while iktisāb means effort or action whether successful or not, making it broader in one respect and narrower in another; the terms may substitute for one another.
ELMALILI:2:286/r10.anchor: kesb isâbet, yani talebini üstüne vurdurup istediğine nâil olmaktır ki Türkçe “kazanmak” demektir. “İktisab” ise gerek isâbet etsin gerek etmesin ‘ale’l-ıtlâk tasarruf ve ictihad

ELMALILI:2:286/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r11.claim: Kesb can mean causing someone to gain and take two objects; in that sense iktisāb is the corresponding acquisition, gaining through another's action.
ELMALILI:2:286/r11.anchor: Şu hâlde “iktisab” bu mânaya tekabül ettiği zaman bi’l-mutâva‘a kazanmak, yani başkasının kazandırmasıyla kazanmak demek olur.

ELMALILI:2:286/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r12.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:2:286/r12.claim: Rāghib distinguishes kesb, which can benefit oneself or others, from iktisāb, which benefits only oneself; every iktisāb is kesb, but not every kesb is iktisāb, illustrated by forms for cooking, roasting, and baking.
ELMALILI:2:286/r12.anchor: Râgıb şunu da beyan eder ki: “‘Kesb’ hem kendi ve hem başkası için kazanıp aldığına, ‘iktisab’ ise sırf kendisi için istifade ettiğine denilir.

ELMALILI:2:286/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r13.claim: These distinctions associate iktisāb with desire and kesb with wisdom, and allow the verse's paired terms to convey multiple meanings.
ELMALILI:2:286/r13.anchor: Bunun için “iktisab” şehvet ile, “kesb” ise hikmet ile alâkadar olur. İşte bu mânaların her biri itibariyle

ELMALILI:2:286/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r14.claim: On one reading, each person's good deeds and their reward benefit that person, while their sins and the burden and punishment they incur harm that same person; 41:46 and 45:15 support the point.

ELMALILI:2:286/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r15.claim: Divine commands require good deeds, while prohibitions forbid evil; performing or abandoning each kind brings benefit or harm respectively to the person charged.
ELMALILI:2:286/r15.anchor: Allah’ın teklifleri de iki kısımdır. Birisi zâhirde veya bâtında veya her ikisinde yapılmasını teklif ettiği evâmirdir. Bunlar hayr ü hasenâttır.

ELMALILI:2:286/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r16.claim: The benefits and harms of obedience or sin accrue to those charged, not to God.
ELMALILI:2:286/r16.anchor: Bunların menfaat ve zararları da Allah’a değil, mükellefleredir.

ELMALILI:2:286/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r17.claim: The idea that God's mercy would be greater if He imposed no duties is mistaken: mercy does not permit harmful desires to go unchecked or withhold obligations that lead to lasting benefit.

ELMALILI:2:286/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r18.claim: An obligation beyond given capacity would be torment rather than a duty; God appoints such torment as just punishment for refusing His law, as in the command to enter Hell at 40:76, with worldly examples among lawbreaking peoples and individuals.
ELMALILI:2:286/r18.anchor: Bu ise artık teklif olarak kalmaz, ta‘zîb olur.

ELMALILI:2:286/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286/r19.claim: The supplications that follow are connected to the wisdom that duties are proportionate to capacity and direct people away from harm.
ELMALILI:2:286/r19.anchor: Bundan sonraki duaların tâlimi de bu hikmetle alâkadardır.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r1.claim: He reads the clause as showing the benefit of obligatory duties and urging believers to spend capacity beyond them on voluntary worship and good works, a recommendation called nadb.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r1.anchor: ferâizden mâ‘adâ tetavvu‘ât ve nevâfile teşvîki mutazammındır ki buna “nedb” tâbir olunur

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r2.claim: A second construal says properly directed effort earns benefit, while blind striving after harm costs the person; capacity-calibrated divine duties guide people toward benefit and away from loss.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r2.anchor: Her nefsin kazandığı, yani yoluyla isteyip isâbet ettiği menfaatine, aksine veya kör körüne çalışıp boğuştuğu zararınadır.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r3.claim: Without duties people would be idle, while demands beyond capacity would waste effort; either result would mean God did not will His servants’ good, contrary to the mercy of the Compassionate.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r3.anchor: Her iki surette Allah kullarının hayrını istememiş, zararlarını istemiş olurdu ki bu da Rahmân-ı Rahîm’in rahmetine münâfîdir.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r4.claim: On this reading, both occurrences of “what” may denote good: benefit actually attained and good that was not attained; even blind, fruitless striving wastes effort and may lead to worse harm.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r4.anchor: Her iki ما hayırdan ibaret olabilir ki biri ele geçen hayır, biri de ele geçmeyen hayırdır.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r5.claim: A third construal treats gains made for oneself and others as truly in one’s own favor, while selfish gain driven by appetite harms the self, since even earning depends on other people; divine duty reconciles self-interest and altruism.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r5.anchor: Asıl kazanç böyle kazançtır ki hayır buna derler.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r6.claim: A fourth construal says one’s own earnings secure rights and benefit, whereas living on another’s earnings is against oneself; duties protect people from dependence and secure rights through charity and fair exchange, while forbidding begging, usury, and aggression.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r6.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah infâk-ı hayır, mübâdele-i sahîha teklif etmiş, tese’’ülden, ribâdan, tecavüzden nehy eylemiştir.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r7.claim: Most exegetes favor the first construal and attach the others to it; Elmalılı calls that first reading the main explanation because it is clear and contains the secrets of divine obligation.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r7.anchor: Ekseriyetle müfessirîn bu dört mânadan birincisi üzerine yürümüşler, berikilerin her birini birer vechile ona ilhak eylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r8.claim: God’s answer to the believers’ plea calms their anxiety through ease and relief, making Qur’anic recitation a direct dialogue and intimate prayer for the Prophet and his community; Elmalılı compares this style with al-Fatiha.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r8.anchor: Bu, Kur’an okuyan veya dinleyen mü’minlerin ara sıra kendilerini Cenâb-ı Allah ile bizzat mükâleme hâlinde bulmaları gibi büyük bir ni‘met-i intâkı tazammun eder.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r9.claim: Although the response is separated by a pause, it is phrased as if the believers themselves were voicing it: they would immediately accept and repeat the promised ease because it matches their own hopes.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r9.anchor: yine onların sözleri ve onlardan hikâye

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r10.claim: He lists three parses: everything from “we heard and obeyed” to the surah’s end is governed by “they said”; the assurance in 2:286 is parenthetical within that speech; or an unexpressed “say” introduces the supplications.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r10.anchor: Bunun için burada nahiv nokta-i nazarından üç vecih vardır.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r11.claim: The petitions are taught as the close of the believers’ earlier prayers, without an explicit command to say them; their opening renews resolve to obey while fearing disobedience.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r11.anchor: şimdi de şöyle deyiniz diye emir tasrih olunmayarak bu da evvelki dualarının âhiri suretinde tâlim buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r12.speaker: الله
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r12.claim: A qudsi hadith cited here says the believing servant continues drawing near to God through supererogatory acts, supporting the exhortation to spend surplus capacity in good works.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r12.anchor: لاَ يَزَالُ عَبْدِى الْمُؤْمِنُ يَتَقَرَّبُ إِلَيَّ بِالنَّوَافِلِ hadîs-i kudsîsi

ELMALILI:2:286#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r13.claim: The first plea asks that the community not be punished in this world or the next for unintentional omission or error: despite renewed resolve, generic liability for what one acquires could include a forgotten duty or unintended prohibited act.
ELMALILI:2:286#2/r13.anchor: وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ ise mutlak olduğundan bunlardan muâhaze muhtemildir.

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r1.claim: Forgetfulness and error fall into two kinds: some may excuse the person, while others do not, because a person can be responsible for failing to take reasonable precautions.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r1.anchor: Nisyan ve Hata İki Nevidir: Birisi sâhibi mâzur görülebilir, diğerinde görülmez.

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r2.claim: Someone who notices impurity on clothing but delays removing it and later forgets before praying is not excused, because the initial delay was negligent; someone who never noticed it is excused.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r2.anchor: bir kimse üzerinde bir necaset görse de izâlesini tehir eylese, sonra unutup namaz kılsa mâzur olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r3.claim: A hunter who shoots without checking whether a person may be present, then hits someone, is not excused because he failed to take the necessary care.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r3.anchor: Kezâlik bir kimse bir ava tüfek atsa da bir insanı vursa

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r4.claim: A person who fails to learn religious and legal duties, or fails to review them after learning them, is not excused for later forgetting; some causes of forgetfulness are within human capacity to prevent.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r4.anchor: insan vezâif-i dîniye ve şer‘iyesini bellemeye çalışmaz

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r5.claim: Involuntary error does not change the intrinsic harm or unlawfulness of the resulting act, just as swallowed poison remains harmful or an accidental fall into a well remains dangerous; people must avoid such outcomes as far as possible.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r5.anchor: hiç nisyan ve hata yapmamak vüs‘-i beşerden hâriç de olsa

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r6.claim: Some legal duties remain in error cases such as accidental killing, and forgetfulness or error does not remove compensation for harm to other people; the plea seeks freedom from punishment, not freedom from obligation, including for causes and consequences.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r6.anchor: Nisyan ve hata hukūk-ı ‘ibâddaki zararın damânına mâni‘olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r7.speaker: رسول الله
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r7.claim: Elmalılı relates the plea to the Prophetic hadith, “My community’s error and forgetfulness are lifted,” while preserving liability for harm to others.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r7.anchor: Nitekim رُفِعَ عَنْ أُمَّتِي اَلْخَطَأُ وَالنِّسْيَان

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r8.claim: Isr is a heavy burden or bond that holds the bearer in place, associated with captivity and confinement; it can also refer to a weighty covenant, subjection, the womb, and kinship.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r8.anchor: “Isr”, asl-ı lügatta esr ü habs mânasıyla alâkadar olup altındakini yerinde tutan ağır yük ve bağ demektir

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r9.speaker: müfessirîn
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r9.claim: Exegetes describe severe requirements imposed on earlier peoples, especially Jews: fifty daily prayers, a quarter of property as tax, cutting away impurity on clothing, exile, swift executions, self-killing for repentance, immediate punishment for rebellion, and prohibition of some lawful foods after an error.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r9.anchor: Müfessirînin beyanlarına nazaran meselâ Yahudîler günde elli vakit namaz kılmak, malının dörtte birini vergi vermek

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r10.speaker: Kaffâl
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r10.claim: Kaffal says the fifth book claimed as Torah contains further examples of the Jews’ harsh laws; believers prayed for protection from such severity, which God later removed, as 7:157 states.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r10.anchor: Tefsîr-i Kaffâl’de demiştir ki: “Yahudîlerin ellerinde Tevrat

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r11.claim: The petition remains necessary because wusʿ, though broader than capacity, is also commonly used for capacity; a burden proportionate to capacity may still be severe, so the prayer asks God to make the apparent sense one of ease.
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r11.anchor: vüs‘, tâkatten geniş ise de tâkat mânasına isti‘mâli de meşhurdur.

ELMALILI:2:286#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#3/r12.claim: Actions can be broader than divine legislation: oppressive conditions may come as discipline through tyrants such as Pharaoh acting against God’s law. The verb “load” allows for this, and the surah’s Israelite stories have signaled both sources of hardship.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r1.claim: The plea covers unbearable burdens whether legal, which may drive people to revolt, or existential, which become torment and destruction; God could impose such things as a test or punishment, so believers ask for protection in every form.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r1.anchor: olursa yapılamaz, isyan ve ihtilâle sevk eder, tekvînî olursa ta‘zîb olur

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r2.claim: The assurance of ease is glad tidings for Muhammad’s community, whose faith, obedience, sincerity, sound will, and adherence to truth suit this gift; unbelievers do not escape duty and instead impose desire-driven, unjust demands on one another.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r2.anchor: Hâsılı لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا tebşîrin ümmet-i Muhammededir.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r3.claim: Every community’s law is a divinely imposed burden: believers receive a straight law as mercy, while unbelievers receive a crooked one as the effect of justice and wrath; what counts as justice differs with their spiritual condition, and God turns hearts, so the plea asks for steadfastness in Islam.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r3.anchor: mü’minlerinki müstakīm ve eser-i rahmet, kâfirlerinki gayr-i müstakīm ve eser-i adl ü gazabdır.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r4.claim: “Pardon us” asks God to erase the effects of sins. People pledge sincere obedience but still fall short, cannot fully spend the God-given capacity and will in His path, and therefore ask through grace rather than earned merit; though deeds remain in divine knowledge, God can remove their consequences.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r4.anchor: Fakat Sen kemâl-i kudretinle onların bize müteveccih olan

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r5.claim: He explains forgiveness as covering and concealing people’s faults, suppressing their blemishes, and not exposing them publicly.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r5.anchor: bize mağfiret de et, ayıplarımızı ilm-i ilâhînde gizle, ört, bastır, eller içinde bizi rüsvây eyleme.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r6.claim: The request for mercy asks God to bestow blessings on the petitioners.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r7.claim: Mawlana means our patron, owner and master, guardian of our affairs, and helper; Elmalılı links it to the declaration that God is the protector of those who believe.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r7.anchor: Sen bizim mevlâmız, sâhib ü mâlikimiz, veliyy-i umûrumuz, nâsırımızsın.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r8.claim: The believers ask for material and spiritual victory over unbelievers in defending the truth and raising God’s word.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r8.anchor: maddeten, mânen müdafa‘a-i hak ve i‘lâ-yı kelimede bizi gālib ve muzaffer eyle.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r9.speaker: الله
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r9.claim: Elmalılı says Muslim and Tirmidhi report that when the Prophet prayed with these petitions, God answered, “So I have done.”
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r9.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz bu dualarla dua ettiği zaman taraf-ı ilâhîden “peki yaptım” buyurulduğu Müslim ve Tirmizî’de rivayet edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r10.claim: Elmalılı says the forthcoming Sura of Al-i Imran begins as a response to this prayer for victory.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r10.anchor: bu nusret duasına bir cevap olarak başlayacaktır.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r11.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r11.claim: A Prophetic report from Ibn Masud, included in the Kutub al-Sitta, says whoever recites the last two verses of al-Baqara at night will find them sufficient.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r11.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan rivayet olunan bir hadîs-i nebevîde buyurulmuştur ki “her kim geceleyin Sûretü’l-Bakara’dan iki âyeti okursa ona kifayet eder.”

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r12.speaker: Ebû Zer
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r12.claim: Abu Dharr’s report, cited by Hakim and Bayhaqi, says the Prophet received the surah’s final two verses from a treasure beneath the Throne and urged people to learn and teach them as prayer, Qur’an, and supplication.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r12.anchor: Ebû Zer’den tahrîc ettikleri diğer bir hadîs-i şerîfte de Fahr-ı Risâlet buyurmuştur ki: “Allah teâlâ Sûre-i Bakara’yı iki âyetle hitâma erdirdi

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r13.speaker: Ömer ve Ali
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r13.claim: Both Umar and Ali are reported to have said that they knew no sensible person who went to sleep without reciting these final verses of al-Baqara.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r13.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer ile Hazret-i Ali radıyallahu ‘anhümâ’dan mervîdir ki her biri “âkil bir adam görmezdim ki Sûre-i Bakara’nın âhirindeki bu âyetleri okumadan uyusun

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r14.speaker: Ebû Meysere
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r14.claim: Abu Maysara reports that Gabriel taught the Prophet to say “amen” at the end of Sura al-Baqara.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r14.anchor: “Cibrîl Resûlullah’a Sûre-i Bakara’nın âhirinde ‘âmîn’ telkin etti” diye de Ebû Meysere’den mervîdir.

ELMALILI:2:286#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r15.claim: Elmalılı closes by praying that God grant worshippers a great share of the promised response when they understand these supplications and follow what they require.
ELMALILI:2:286#4/r15.anchor: bu duaların mânalarını fehm ve muktezâsına ittibâ‘ile vaad ettiği feyz-i icâbetinden büyük büyük nasiblerle kâmyâb buyursun.

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r12.claim: In perfect mercy, God sets people's charge at their capacity and far below that limit, out of gentleness and grace.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r12.anchor: لكمال رحمته بهم وقفهم على حد وسعهم ودون ذلك بكثير ، كل ذلك رفق منه وفضل

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r13.claim: The soul receives what it earns of good deeds.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r13.anchor: { لها ما كسبت } . من الخيرات . { وعليها ما اكتسبت }

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r14.claim: What the soul acquires of evil lies against it, and repentance rescues it from that burden.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r14.anchor: وعليها ما اكتسبت } . ما تكسبه من التوبة التي تنجي من كسب

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r15.claim: Earlier communities voiced needs through an intermediary, asking Moses to pray, while this community is directly told to call upon God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r15.anchor: كان إذا وقعت حاجة كلموه بلسان الواسطة . قالوا : { يا موسى ادع لنا ربك }

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r16.claim: Unlike earlier communities, this community is directly commanded: “Your Lord says, call upon Me, and I will answer you.”
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r16.anchor: وهذه الأمة قال لهم : { وقال ربكم ادعونى أستجب لكم }

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r17.claim: Earlier peoples needed time to pass before repentance was accepted; for this community remorse itself is repentance.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r17.anchor: وكانت الأمم ( السالفة ) إذا أذنبوا احتاجوا إلى مضي مدة لقبول التوبة

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r18.claim: Earlier peoples asked for an idol like others, but this community is distinguished by the radiance of unity and countless special merits.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r18.anchor: وهذه الأمة اختصت بإشراق أنوار توحيدهم ، وخصائصهم أكثر من أن يأتي عليه الشرح

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r19.claim: “Pardon us” concerns the present, while “forgive us” concerns the future.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r19.anchor: في الحال . { واغفر لنا } . في المآل

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r20.claim: They ask for mercy and victory in every state because they have no protector besides God; victory also means overcoming whatever distracts them from Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r20.anchor: في جميع الأحوال إذ ليس لنا أحد سواك ، فأنت مولانا فاجعل النصرة لنا على ما يشغلنا عنك

QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r21.claim: In answer to their plea, God replaced earlier peoples' destruction with forgiveness, their transformation with good deeds, and stones with mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v1p128/r21.anchor: ولما قالوا : { ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا } خسف الله ذنوبهم بدل خسف المتقدمين

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r1.claim: The sūra’s ending complements its opening: after the opening’s account of faithful belief and good works, the conclusion confirms the standing of the Prophet and believers and teaches later Muslims how to relate to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r1.anchor: Sûrenin başıyla sonu âdeta bir levhanın iki parçası gibi birbirini tamamlamaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r2.claim: The early emigrants left everything for Medina and the Helpers welcomed them; the ending tells these early Muslims their standing with God as a reward and offers later followers a lesson in religious life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r2.anchor: O’nun rızâsı için her şeylerini geride bırakarak Medine’ye hicret etmiş muhacirlerle onlara her şeyleriyle kucak açmış ensar vardı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r4.claim: The closing supplication teaches that sincere servants have inadvertent lapses which the Lord may forgive, and that Islam’s final, complete religion is founded on ease rather than burdensome worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r4.anchor: iyi niyetli kulların istemeden meydana gelen kusurlarını yüce mevlânın bağışlayacağına işaret etmekte, Hz. Peygamber’in ümmetine gelen en son ve kâmil dinin başta gelen özelliklerinden biri olan “kolaylık” temel kuralını dile getirmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r5.claim: Reciting these verses and carefully displaying them as calligraphic panels became a way the Muslim community embodied their significance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r5.anchor: ümmetin geleneğinde de hem özellikle okunarak hem de levhalaştırılıp itina ile duvarlara asılarak bu özellik hayata geçirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r6.claim: Against theologians who deem an impossible divine burden permissible to protect unrestricted power and will, the author reads the verse as confirming that a wise God does not impose what exceeds capacity, in keeping with justice and a rational basis for accountability.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r6.anchor: “Câiz değildir, hakîm olan Allah böyle bir yükümlülük getirmez” diyenleri bu âyet teyit etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r7.speaker: Cebriyye ekolü
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r7.claim: The Jabriyya deny that people possess a will or power of their own in the acts and behaviors they perform.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r7.anchor: “İnsanların ortaya koydukları fiillerde ve davranışlarda kendilerine mahsus irade ve kudretleri yoktur” diyen Cebriyye ekolü

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r8.speaker: Mu‘tezile mezhebi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r8.claim: The Muʿtazila say human acts independently result from human will and power, and that a person creates their act from nothing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r8.anchor: “Bu fiiller ve davranışlar, bağımsız olarak insanın irade ve kudretinin eseridir, fiilini yoktan var eden (îcâd) kuldur” diyen Mu‘tezile mezhebi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r9.speaker: İmam Eş‘arî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r9.claim: Al-Ashʿarī holds that the human will and power accompany God’s in the act’s occurrence but have no effect.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r9.anchor: “Kulun fiili meydana gelirken Allah’ın irade ve kudreti yanında –etkisi bulunmaksızın– kulunki de vardır” diyen İmam Eş‘arî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r10.speaker: Mâtürîdî mezhebi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r10.claim: The author presents the Māturīdī school as drawing support from this verse while opposing the other schools’ accounts of human action.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r10.anchor: bütün bu ekollerin karşısında yer alan Mâtürîdî mezhebi, diğer deliller yanında bu âyetten ışık ve güç almaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r11.speaker: Mâtürîdî mezhebi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r11.claim: God creates humans’ universal will and power, usable for good or evil; their particular willing and power is its direction toward one, resolved act, called kasb, which affects the act’s moral quality rather than its creation, grounding responsibility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r11.anchor: Küllî irade ve kudretin, hayır ve şerden birine sarfedilmesi ise cüz’î niteliklidir; yani cüz’î kudret, cüz’î iradedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r12.claim: The author identifies kesb as the verse’s explicit term for human contribution to action, meaning to acquire, earn, or deserve; the aphorism says the servant earns while God creates.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r12.anchor: Türkçesi “elde etmek, kazanmak, hak etmek” demek olan “kesb”dir. Eskiden sıkça tekrarlanan “Kul kâsibdir, Allah da hâlıktır”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r13.speaker: hadis
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r13.claim: A hadith cited above gives glad tidings that God forgives the Muslim community’s lapses caused by forgetting or error, affirming that this supplication was accepted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r13.anchor: bir hadis, Muhammed ümmetinin unutma ve yanılma sebebiyle meydana gelen kusurlarının Allah tarafından bağışlandığı müjdesini veriyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r14.claim: The Old Testament, still practically valid for Christianity, has strict rules and restrictions on eating, drinking, and purification; Islam’s duties fit human nature and are manageable, with dispensations for personal hardship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r14.anchor: Hıristiyanlık için de amelî geçerliliği bulunan Eski Ahid’de yeme, içme, temizlenme gibi konularda oldukça zor dinî kurallar, yasaklama ve sınırlamalar vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r15.claim: Although believers might expect humanity to embrace this accessible religion, testing through reason, will, the self, and Satan obstructs many; because the thankful are few, believers need God’s help beyond their own effort.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r15.anchor: Bu çokluk karşısında müminler, kendi güç ve gayretleri yanında ve ondan daha çok yüce Allah’ın yardımına sığınmak durumundadırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r16.speaker: hadis
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r16.claim: Many sound hadiths describe the merit of the sūra’s final two verses; one says they suffice at night for whoever recites them, cited from Bukhārī and Shawkānī.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:285/r16.anchor: “Bakara sûresinin sonunda iki âyet vardır ki bir gecede okuyana onlar yeter” meâlindeki hadis bunlardandır

BURHAN:v1p182/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p182/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p182/r3.claim: The closing of al-Baqara is another example of a sura ending made of supplication.
BURHAN:v1p182/r3.anchor: وكالدعاء الذى اشتملت عليه الآيتان من آخر سورة البقرة

BURHAN:v3p225/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p225/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p225/r8.claim: The author cites the verse's concise statement of capacity, responsibility, and earned reward as an example of eloquent concision.
BURHAN:v3p225/r8.anchor: وقوله ﴿ لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت ﴾

BURHAN:v4p163/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p163/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p163/r1.claim: The verb akhadha has several senses, including usurpation, as in the report about taking even a handspan of land.
BURHAN:v4p163/r1.anchor: تجىء بمعنى غصب ومنه من أخذ قيد شبر من أرض طوق من سبع أرضين

BURHAN:v4p163/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p163/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p163/r2.claim: Akhadha and its derivatives can mean punish or seize in retribution, as in the cited accounts of God taking unjust peoples and the prayer not to be called to account.
BURHAN:v4p163/r2.anchor: وبمعنى عاقب كقوله تعالى ﴿ وكذلك أخذ ربك

BURHAN:v4p163/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p163/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p163/r3.claim: The construction akhadha yafʿalu can mean beginning to do something, like jaʿala yafʿalu and karuba yafʿalu.
BURHAN:v4p163/r3.anchor: وتجىء للمقاربة قالوا أخذ يفعل كذا كما قالوا جعل يقول وكرب يقول

BURHAN:v4p353/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p353/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v4p353/r4.claim: Some call prohibitive la a request particle so the label includes supplication as well as prohibition; here la is a prayer asking God not to hold the speakers accountable.
BURHAN:v4p353/r4.anchor: وترد للدعاء نحو ﴿ لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ﴾ 5 ولذلك

ITQAN:v3p286/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p286/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p286/r4.claim: The end of al-Baqara closes with supplication.
ITQAN:v3p286/r4.anchor: وكالدعاء الذي اشتملت عليه الآيتان من آخر سورة البقرة

ITQAN:v1p284/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p284/r5.speaker: أبو ميسرة
ITQAN:v1p284/r5.claim: Abu Maysara reports that Gabriel taught the Prophet to say “Amen” at the end of al-Baqara.
ITQAN:v1p284/r5.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد عن أبي ميسرة أن جبريل لقن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند خاتمة البقرة آمين

ITQAN:v1p114/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p114/r1.claim: Among the material granted to Muhammad but not to any earlier prophet are al-Fatiha, Ayat al-Kursi, and the conclusion of al-Baqara.
ITQAN:v1p114/r1.anchor: من الثاني الفاتحة وآية الكرسي وخاتمة البقرة كما تقدم في الأحاديث قريبا

ITQAN:v1p114/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p114/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p114/r2.claim: A report in Muslim says an angel brought the Prophet good news of two lights not given to a prophet before him: al-Fatiha and the final verses of al-Baqara.
ITQAN:v1p114/r2.anchor: وروى مسلم عن ابن عباس أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ملك فقال أبشر بنورين قد أوتيتهما لم يؤتهما نبي قبلك

ITQAN:v1p114/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p114/r3.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
ITQAN:v1p114/r3.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits a report from Uqba ibn Amir urging recitation of the last two verses of al-Baqara, which God selected for Muhammad.
ITQAN:v1p114/r3.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني عن عقبة بن عامر قال ترددوا في الآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة ﴿ آمن الرسول ﴾ إلى خاتمتها

ITQAN:v1p114/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p114/r4.speaker: كعب
ITQAN:v1p114/r4.claim: Ka'b says Muhammad received four verses not given to Moses: the passage beginning لله ما في السماوات and ending al-Baqara, plus Ayat al-Kursi; Moses instead received a supplication.
ITQAN:v1p114/r4.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد في فضائله عن كعب قال إن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم أعطي أربع آيات لم يعطهن موسى

ITQAN:v2p500/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p500/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p500/r4.claim: The coordinating and answer uses of lā do not occur in the Qur’an.
ITQAN:v2p500/r4.anchor: ثالثها ورابعها أن تكون عاطفة أو جوابية ولم يقعا في القرآن

ITQAN:v2p500/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p500/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p500/r8.claim: Prohibitive lā is used with a present verb, makes it jussive, and places the action in the future; it may express either prohibition or supplication.
ITQAN:v2p500/r8.anchor: فتختص بالمضارع وتقتضي جزمه واستقباله سواء كان نهيا

ITQAN:v4p491/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p491/r5.speaker: من قال
