ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r2.anchor: وفي البحر وهو المروي عن الحسن أن ذلك على تقدير الأمر أي قولوا في دعائكم ذلك فهو تعليم منه تعالى لعباده كيفية الدعاء والطلب منه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r3.claim: Muʾākhadha means punishment; the form fāʿala can carry the simple sense of fāʿala/afaʿala rather than reciprocal action.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r3.anchor: والمؤاخذة المعاقبة وفاعل هنا بمعنى فعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r4.claim: An alternative takes the reciprocal form literally: God holds the sinner accountable while the sinner, having no rescuer but God, appeals to Him as though demanding release; Al-Alusi calls this unsound without strained interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r4.anchor: وقيل : المفاعلة على بابها لأن الله تعالى يؤاخذ المذنب بالعقوبة والمذنب كأنه يؤاخذ ربه بالمطالبة بالعفو

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r5.claim: One view takes forgetting as abandoning obligations and error as committing prohibitions, even deliberately, since sins are errors opposed to correctness.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r5.anchor: الأول أن المراد من الأول الترك ومنه قوله : ولم أك عند الجود للجود قاليا ولا كنت يوم الروع للطعن ناسيا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r6.claim: A second view means the prior negligence and inattention that usually cause forgetting or mistakes, and asks pardon for that antecedent shortcoming.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r6.anchor: الثاني أن المراد منهما ما هما مسببان عنه من التفريط والإغفال إذ قلما يتفقان إلا عن تقصير سابق فالمعنى لا تؤاخذنا بذلك التقصير

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r7.claim: A third view means actual forgetfulness and error: they could rationally bring punishment, like poison can kill when taken inadvertently, but God promised to overlook them as grace.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r7.anchor: الثالث أن المراد بهما أنفسهما من حيث ترتبهما على ما ذكر أو مطلقا إذ لا امتناع في المؤاخذة بهما عقلا فإن المعاصي كالسموم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r8.speaker: الطبراني
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r8.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits a hadith that al-Nawawi grades ḥasan: the Prophet says his community is exempted for error, forgetfulness, and coercion.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r8.anchor: فيما أخرجه الطبرانى وقال النووى حديث حسن : رفع عن أمتى الخطأ والنسيان وما أكرهوا عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r9.speaker: المحققين من أهل السنة والمعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r9.claim: An objection says the third view conflicts with the rational impossibility of charging beyond capacity accepted by leading Sunnis and Muʿtazilites, since exemption would not then be a continuing favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r9.anchor: وأورد على هذا بأنه لا يتم على مذهب المحققين من أهل السنة والمعتزلة من أن التكليف بغير المقدور غير جائز عقلا منه تعالى إذ لا يكون ترك المؤاخذة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r10.claim: Iṣr is a weighty burden that confines its bearer; here it means difficult obligations.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r10.anchor: أى عبثا ثقيلا يأسر صاحبه أى يحبسه مكانه + والمراد به التكاليف الشاقة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes iṣr as a sin for which there is no repentance, so the supplication asks protection from committing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r11.anchor: وقيل : الاصر الذنب الذى لا توبة له فالمعنى اعصمنا من اقترافه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r12.claim: Aṣāran is also read in the plural, and one reading doubles the tāʾ in tuḥammil.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r12.anchor: وقرئ آصارا على الجمع وقرأ أنى ولا تحمل بالتشديد للمبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r13.claim: The comparison is either an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning a burden like the one imposed earlier, or an adjective of iṣr itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r13.anchor: في حيز النصب على أنه صفة لمصدر محذوف أي حملا مثل حملك إياه على من قبلنا أو على أنه صفة لإصرا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r14.claim: Examples of Israelite burdens include killing oneself in repentance or retaliation, cutting impurity from clothing (some say the body), and giving a quarter of wealth as alms.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70/r14.anchor: وهو ما كلفه بنو إسرائيل من قتل النفس فى التوبة أو فى القصاص لانه كان لا يجوز غيره فى شريعتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r1.claim: This asks relief from punishments that cannot be borne and that follow from prior burdens; describing punishment as loading is figurative, based on its consequences.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r1.anchor: استعفاء عن العقوبات التى لا تطاق بعد الاستعفاء عما يؤدى إليها والتعبير عن إنزال ذلك بالتحميل مجازيا باعتبار ما يؤدي إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r2.claim: Another view makes the request broader than the preceding one: the burden is pictured as impossible to bear for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r2.anchor: وجوز أن يكون طلبا لما هو أعم من الأول لتخصيصه بالتشبيه إلا أنه صور فيه الإصر بصورة ما لا يستطاع مبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r3.claim: A further view treats this as asking to avoid literally impossible obligations and argues that the request proves such obligations are possible; Al-Alusi judges the argument weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : هو استغناء عن التكليف بما لا تفى به القدر البشرية حقيقة فتكون الآية دليلا على جواز التكليف بما لا يطاق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r4.claim: The doubled form here serves only to make the verb take a second object, not to intensify or multiply the action.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r4.anchor: والتشديد ههنا لمجرد تعدية الفعل لمفعول ثان دون التكثير

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r5.claim: To pardon is to erase the traces of sins by withholding punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r5.anchor: وأعف عنا ( أى امح آثار ذنوبنا بترك العقوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r6.claim: To forgive is to conceal what is ugly and disclose what is beautiful.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r6.anchor: واغفر لنا ( بستر القبيح وإظهار الجميل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r7.claim: Mercy is gracious concern for the servants that brings increase.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r7.anchor: وارحمنا ( وتعطف علينا بما يوجب المزيد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r8.claim: An alternative assigns pardon to deeds, forgiveness to words, and mercy to the weighing of the scales.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : ( اعف عنا ) منالأفعال ( واغفر لتا ) من الأقوال ( وارحمنا ) بثقل الميزان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r9.claim: Another alternative places pardon at death, forgiveness in the darkness of graves, and mercy amid the terrors of resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : ( واعف عنا ) فى سكرات الموت ( واغفر لنا ) فى ظلمة القبور ( وارحمنا ) فى أهوال يوم النشور

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan explains the sequence: pardon answers the plea not to punish for error, forgiveness the plea not to impose burdens, and mercy the plea not to impose the unbearable; hence no repeated rabbana.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو حيان : ولم يأت فى هذه الجمل الثلاث بلفظ ( ربنا ) لأنها نتائج ما تقدم من الجمل التى افتتحت بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r11.claim: Mawlānā means our owner and master, or the one who manages our affairs; it is a verbal noun used for an agent.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r11.anchor: أنت مولنا ( أى مالكنا وسيدنا وجوز أن يكون بمعنى متولى الأمر وأصله مصدر أريد به الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r12.claim: When mawlā and sayyid are both used, Arabic usage puts mawlā first; al-Khansāʾ's verse is cited as evidence, though Al-Alusi has reservations about the criticism of the reverse order.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r12.anchor: وإذا ذكر المولى والسيد وجب فى الاستعمال تقديم المولى فيقال : مولانا وسيدنا كما فى قول الخنساء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r13.claim: The clause may be understood as an instruction to say: You are our patron.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r13.anchor: قيل : والجملة على معنى القول أى قولوا أنت مولانا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r14.claim: The requested victory is against enemy combatants or, more broadly, all unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r14.anchor: أنت مولانا ( فانصرنا على القوم الكفرين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r15.claim: The fāʾ signals causation: because God is their patron and manager, they ask Him to grant victory, like asking generosity from a generous person.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p70#2/r15.anchor: أى قولوا أنت مولانا ( فانصرنا على القوم الكفرين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r9.claim: The soul is charged only with what its disposition can contain without constriction: spiritual manifestations.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r9.anchor: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها ) إلا ما يسعها ولا يضيق به طوقها واستعدادها من التجليات

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r10.claim: What the soul earns is goodness, perfection, and unveiling, whether gained through effort or spontaneously.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r10.anchor: لها ما كسبت ) من الخير والكمالات والكشوف سواء كان ذلك باعتمال أو بغير اعتمال

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r11.claim: What weighs against the soul is the evil toward which it deliberately turns.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r11.anchor: وعليها ما اكتسبت ) وتوجهت إليه بالقصد من السوء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r12.claim: Forgetting is forgetting the covenant through inclination toward the darkness of nature.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r12.anchor: ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا ) عهدك بميلنا إلى ظلمة الطبيعة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r13.claim: Error means acting in a way unfit for the divine presence.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r13.anchor: أو أخطأنا ) بالعمل على غير الوجه اللائق لحضرتك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r14.claim: The burden is the load of attributes and acts that imprison hearts and keep them from witnessing God.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r14.anchor: ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا ) وهو عبء الصفات والافعال الحابسة للقلوب من معاينة القلوب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r15.claim: Those before are people fixated on outward acts or inward attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r15.anchor: منا حملته على الذين من قبلنا ) من المحتجين بظواهر الافعال أو بواطن الصفات

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r16.claim: The unbearable burden is abandonment and deprivation from union and witnessing divine beauty while veiled by majesty.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r16.anchor: ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به ) من ثقل الهجران والحرمان عن وصالك ومشاهدة جمالك بحجب جلالك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r17.claim: They ask pardon for sins of acts and attributes that veil them from God and deprive them of intimacy and delight.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r17.anchor: واعف عنا ) سيآت أفعالنا وصفاتنا فانها سيآت حجبتنا عنك وحرمتنا برد وصلك ولذة رضوانك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r18.claim: They ask forgiveness for the sin of their own existence, which is the greatest sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r18.anchor: واغفر لنا ) ذنوب وجودنا فانه أكبر الكبائر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r19.claim: Mercy is the bestowed existence that follows annihilation.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r20.claim: God is their master and manager because they are His manifestations and effects of His power.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r20.anchor: أنت مولانا ) أى سيدنا ومتولى أمورنا لأنا مظاهرك وآثار قدرتك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r21.claim: The unbelievers signify commanding souls, their attributes, and the armies of satanic imaginations that veil people from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r21.anchor: فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين ) من قوى نفوسنا الامارة وصفاتها وجنود شياطين أوهامنا المحجوبين عنك الحاجبين إيانا لكفرهم وظلمتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r22.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r22.claim: Muslim and al-Tirmidhi report from Ibn Abbas that after the Prophet recited these verses upon their revelation, he was told after each clause: I have done so.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r22.anchor: أخرج مسلم والترمذى من حدث ابن عباس لما نزلت هذه الآية فقرأها صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قيل له عقيب كل كلمة قد فعلت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r23.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r23.claim: Abu Saʿid and al-Bayhaqi transmit from al-Dahhak that Gabriel brought the verse with angels and told the Prophet after each clause, I grant you that, until he finished.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r23.anchor: وأخرج أبو سعيد ولبيهقى عن الضحاك أن جبريل لما جاء بهذه الآية ومعه ما شاء الله تعالى من الملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r24.speaker: أبو ميسرة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r24.claim: Abu ʿUbayd reports from Abu Maysara that Gabriel prompted the Prophet to say āmin at the end of al-Baqara.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r24.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد عن أبى ميسرة أن جبريل لقن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عند خاتمة البقرة آمين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r25.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r25.claim: The six canonical collections transmit from Ibn Masʿud that whoever recites the final two verses of al-Baqara at night, they suffice him.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r25.anchor: عن ابن مسعود عن النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : من قرأ الأيتين من آخر سورة البقرة فى ليلة كفتاه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r26.speaker: شداد بن أوس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r26.claim: Al-Tabarani, with a good chain, reports from Shaddad ibn Aws that God wrote a book two thousand years before creating heaven and earth, and the final two verses protect a home from Satan for three nights.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r26.anchor: وأخرج الطبرانى بسند جيد عن شداد بن أوس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : إن الله تعالى كتب كتابا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r27.speaker: ابن مسعود الأنصاري
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r27.claim: Ibn ʿAdi reports from Ibn Masʿud al-Ansari that two verses from the treasures of Paradise were written by God before creation; reciting them after the night prayer suffices for night worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r27.anchor: وأخرج ابن عدى عن ابن مسعود الانصارى أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : أنزل الله تعالى آيتين من كنوز الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r28.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r28.claim: Al-Hakim, who authenticates it, and al-Bayhaqi report from Abu Dharr that the final verses were granted from beneath the Throne and should be taught to wives and children as prayer, Qur'an, and supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r28.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه والبيهقى فى الشعب عن أبى ذرأن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : إن الله ختم سورة البقرة بآيتين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r29.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r29.claim: Abu ʿUbayd transmits from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir that the verses are Qur'an and supplication, bring entry into Paradise, and please the Merciful.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r29.anchor: وفي رواية أبي عبيد عن محمد بن المنكدر أنهن قرآن وأنهن دعاء وأنهن يدخلن الجنة وأنهن يرضين الرحمن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r30.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r30.claim: Musaddad transmits from ʿUmar, and al-Darimi from ʿAli, that neither thought a sensible person would sleep without reciting these final verses of al-Baqara.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p71/r30.anchor: عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه والدارمى عن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه كلاهما قال : ما كنت أرى أحدا يعقل ينام حتى يقرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r1.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r1.claim: Some investigators connect al-Baqara's fire prepared for unbelievers and opening mention of believers and unbelievers with Al ʿImran's concluding paradise prepared for the righteous, making the sūras like one sūra.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r1.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض المحققين من وجوه التلازم بين الصورتين أنه قال فى البقرة فى صفة النار : ( أعدت للكافرين )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r2.claim: Al ʿImran's close, commanding God-consciousness for success, matches al-Baqara's opening description of the God-conscious as successful.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r2.anchor: خاتمة هذه مناسبة لفاتحة تلك لان الأولى افتتحت بذكر المتقين وأنهم المفلحون وختمت هذه بقوله تعالى : ( واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r3.claim: Al-Baqara opens by describing belief in what was revealed to Muhammad and earlier prophets; Al ʿImran closes by affirming that some People of the Book believe in both revelations.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r3.anchor: وختمت آل عمران بقوله تعالى : ( وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل اليكم وما أنزل اليهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r4.claim: The Jews' claim that God was poor for asking a loan in al-Baqara is answered by Al ʿImran's declaration that God heard those who called Him poor, strengthening the sūra link.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r4.anchor: وقد ورد أن اليهود قالوا لما نزل ( من ذا الذى يقرض الله ) الآية : يا محمد افتقر ربك بسأل عباده القرض

ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r5.claim: Al-Baqara's account of Abraham asking for a messenger among his descendants is echoed by Al ʿImran's statement that God favored believers by sending a messenger from among them.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p73/r5.anchor: ومثله أنه وقع فى البقرة حكاية قول إبراهيم : ( ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم ) الآية وهنا ( لقد من الله على المؤمنين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p354/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p354/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p354/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when the verse about hidden thoughts was revealed, it distressed the Companions, who said they could bear prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity but not this. The Prophet told them to answer as believers: “We hear and obey; forgive us.” God then revealed the believers' affirmation and replaced the former ruling with the declaration that no soul is charged beyond its capacity, followed by their petitions for pardon and help; the Prophet answered “yes” to each.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p354/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: لما أنزل الله على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r13.claim: The verse answers an implied request not to be burdened beyond capacity; wusʿ means what a person can bear without hardship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r13.anchor: ظاهر الآية قضاء الحاجة، وفيها إضمار السؤال كأنه قال: وقالوا لا تكلفنا إلا وسعنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, and most exegetes take wusʿ to refer to the inner thoughts mentioned in the preceding verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r14.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه وعطاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r15.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the ruling specifically concerns believers: God has made their religious obligations easy and only requires what they can do, as affirmed by 2:185 and 22:78.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r15.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال: هم المؤمنون خاصة، وسع عليهم أمر دينهم ولم يكلفهم فيه إلا ما يستطيعون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r16.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r16.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna glosses wusʿ as ease, not a burden beyond ability; the author calls this a good view because wusʿ is what lies below the limit of full capacity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p356/r16.anchor: وسئل سفيان بن عيينة عن قوله عز وجل {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} قال: إلا يسرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r1.claim: What a person earns of good is for that person as reward and recompense.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r1.anchor: ما عملت من الخير، لها أجره وثوابه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r2.claim: What a person acquires of evil is against that person, carrying its burden.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r3.claim: The plea asks God not to punish the believers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi reads forgetfulness as actual forgetting: Israelites who forgot or erred were punished at once, sometimes by losing foods; believers were taught to ask for no such reckoning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي كانت بنو إسرائيل إذا نسوا شيئا مما أمروا به أو أخطأوا عجلت لهم العقوبة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes forgetting to mean neglecting or abandoning God, as in the verse saying they forgot God and He forgot them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r5.anchor: وقيل هو من النسيان الذي هو الترك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r6.claim: One view says the word for erring can mean acting deliberately, supported by its use for a grave intentional act elsewhere.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r7.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r7.claim: ʿAta interprets the plea as covering ignorance and deliberate action.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r7.anchor: قال عطاء: إن نسينا أو أخطأنا يعني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r8.speaker: الأكثرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r8.claim: Most interpreters take error as ignorance or inadvertence: deliberate sin is not simply absolved, but left to God’s will, whereas error is forgiven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r8.anchor: وجعله الأكثرون من الخطإ الذي هو الجهل والسهو، لأن ما كان عمدا من الذنب فغير معفو عنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r9.claim: The Prophet said that error, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from his community.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p357/r9.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r1.claim: Mujahid, ʿAta, Qatada, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, and others say the burden is a severe covenant the Israelites could not fulfill and were punished for breaking; the wording is supported by the covenant verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r1.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد وعطاء وقتادة والسدي والكلبي وجماعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r2.speaker: عثمان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r2.claim: A second view, attributed to ʿUthman, ʿAta, Malik, Abu ʿUbayda, and others, asks that the law not be made as severe as it was for earlier Jews: fifty prayers, a quarter of wealth in alms, cutting away impurity from clothes, and sins displayed on the door; the author links this to the verse about removing burdens.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى قول عثمان وعطاء ومالك بن أنس وأبي عبيدة وجماعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r3.claim: Another explanation calls the burden a sin for which there is no repentance and takes the plea to ask protection from such a sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r3.anchor: وقيل: الإصر ذنب لا توبة له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358/r4.claim: The word’s underlying sense is restraint and binding firmly.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r1.claim: The petition asks not to be charged with deeds beyond their capacity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r1.anchor: أي لا تكلفنا من الأعمال ما لا نطيقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r2.claim: An unnamed view takes the unbearable burden to mean inner speech and whispering.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r3.speaker: مكحول
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r3.claim: Makḥul identifies the burden as intense sexual desire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r3.anchor: حكي عن مكحول أنه قال: هو الغلمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim says the burden is love.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r5.speaker: محمد بن عبد الوهاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhab identifies it as passionate love.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r5.anchor: وعن محمد بن عبد الوهاب قال: العشق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it means transformation into apes and swine.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: هو مسخ القردة والخنازير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r7.claim: An unnamed explanation identifies the burden as the gloating of enemies.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r8.claim: Another unnamed explanation identifies it as separation and estrangement.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r9.claim: The request is that God overlook and erase their sins.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r10.claim: The request is that God cover their sins and not expose them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r11.claim: They cannot attain good action except through obedience granted by God, nor leave disobedience except through His mercy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r11.anchor: فإننا لا ننال العمل إلا بطاعتك، ولا نترك معصيتك إلا برحمتك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r12.claim: God is their helper, protector, and patron.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r13.claim: The final plea asks God to grant victory over the disbelieving people.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, in a report from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says God answered the closing pleas with forgiveness, pardon, mercy, and victory.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r14.anchor: روى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r15.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r15.claim: Muʿadh ibn Jabal would say amen when he completed Surat al-Baqara.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r15.anchor: وكان معاذ بن جبل إذا ختم سورة البقرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r16.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r16.claim: ʿAbd Allah reports that during the night journey the Prophet reached the lote tree in the sixth heaven, received the five prayers and closing verses of al-Baqara, and was granted forgiveness for members of his community who did not associate partners with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p358#2/r16.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: لما أسري برسول الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r1.claim: God burdens a soul only with what its ability can contain, by grace and mercy; alternatively, He gives less than its utmost capacity, making the duty manageable and easy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r1.anchor: إلا ما تسعه قدرتها فضلا ورحمة، أو ما دون مدى طاقتها بحيث يتسع فيه طوقها ويتيسر عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r2.claim: This supports the nonoccurrence of an impossible duty, but does not prove that such a duty is impossible in principle; compare 2:185.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r2.anchor: يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r3.claim: A soul receives the good it has earned, while bearing the evil it has acquired; neither another’s obedience nor disobedience benefits or harms it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r3.anchor: من خير. { وعليها ما اكتسبت } من شر لا ينتفع بطاعتها ولا يتضرر بمعاصيها غيرها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r4.claim: The verse uses the lighter earning verb for good and the effortful form for evil because evil is desired by the soul and pursued more energetically, unlike good.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r4.anchor: وتخصيص الكسب بالخير والاكتساب بالشر لأن الاكتساب فيه احتمال والشر تشتهيه النفس وتنجذب إليه فكانت أجد في تحصيله وأعمل بخلاف الخير

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r5.claim: The prayer may ask pardon for negligence that caused forgetting or error, or for forgetting and error themselves; they do not rationally preclude accountability, like mistakenly taking poison can still cause death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r5.anchor: لا تؤاخذنا بما أدى بنا إلى نسيان أو خطأ من تفريط وقلة مبالاة، أو بأنفسهما إذ لا تمتنع المؤاخذة بهما عقلا فإن الذنوب كالسموم فكما أن تناولها يؤدي إلى الهلاك وإن كان خطأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r6.claim: A sin may lead to punishment even without resolve.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r6.anchor: فكما أن تناولها يؤدي إلى الهلاك وإن كان خطأ فتعاطي الذنوب لا يبعد أن يفضي إلى العقاب وإن لم تكن عزيمة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r7.claim: God promised to overlook such sins through grace, so the prayer acknowledges and perpetuates that favor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r7.anchor: لكنه تعالى وعد التجاوز عنه رحمة وفضلا فيجوز أن يدعو الإنسان به استدامة واعتدادا بالنعمة فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r8.claim: The Prophet’s saying that error and forgetfulness have been lifted from his community supports the promised pardon.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286/r8.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك مفهوم قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r1.claim: An iṣr is a heavy burden that restrains its bearer in place; here it means difficult obligations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r1.anchor: عبأ ثقيلا يأصر صاحبه، أي يحبسه في مكانه. يريد به التكاليف الشاقة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r2.claim: A reading doubles the tāʾ in tuḥammil to add emphasis.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r3.claim: The comparison may mean a burden like the one imposed on us, like that imposed on earlier people, or describe the iṣr itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r3.anchor: حملا مثل حملك إياه على { من قبلنا } ، أو مثل الذي حملته إياهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r4.claim: The earlier people’s burdens may be Israelite duties—killing one another, cutting away impurity, fifty daily prayers, and giving a quarter of wealth as alms—or their hardships and ordeals.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r4.anchor: والمراد به ما كلف به بنو إسرائيل من قتل الأنفس، وقطع موضع النجاسة، وخمسين صلاة في اليوم والليلة، وصرف ربع المال للزكاة. أو ما أصابهم من الشدائد والمحن

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r5.claim: The plea concerns tribulation and punishment, or duties beyond human capacity; its wording indicates that imposing an impossible duty is possible, since the prayer seeks escape from it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r5.anchor: من البلاء والعقوبة، أو من التكاليف التي لا تفي بها الطاقة البشرية وهو يدل على جواز التكليف بما لا يطاق وإلا لما سئل التخلص منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r6.claim: The intensive form here makes the verb take a second object.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r6.anchor: والتشديد ههنا لتعدية الفعل إلى المفعول الثاني

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r8.claim: “Forgive us” means conceal our faults and do not expose us through punishment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r9.claim: “Have mercy on us” means show tenderness and favor.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r10.anchor: { أنت مولنا } سيدنا. { فانصرنا على القوم الكفرين }

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r11.claim: The plea follows from a master’s duty to aid his clients against enemies; alternatively, “the unbelieving people” means unbelievers generally.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r11.anchor: فإن من حق المولى أن ينصر مواليه على الأعداء، أو المراد به عامة الكفرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r12.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r12.claim: A report says that when the Prophet made these supplications, he was told “I have done so” after each one.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r12.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لما دعا بهذه الدعوات قيل له عند كل كلمة فعلت

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r13.claim: The Prophet reported that two verses from the treasures of Paradise were written by the Merciful’s hand two thousand years before creation; reciting them after the last night prayer suffices in place of night vigil.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r13.anchor:
وعنه عليه السلام
" أنزل الله تعالى آيتين

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r14.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r14.claim: The Prophet said that whoever recites the last two verses of Sūrat al-Baqara at night, they suffice him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r14.anchor:
وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام
" من قرأ الآيتين

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r15.claim: This report counters an objection to calling it Sūrat al-Baqara: the Prophet called it the sūra in which the cow is mentioned, a fortress of the Qur’an whose study is blessed, whose neglect is regretted, and which sorcerers cannot master; he explained “the impotent” as sorcerers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:286#2/r15.anchor:
كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام
" السورة التي تذكر فيها البقرة فسطاط القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r1.claim: After the command to say that they hear, obey, and seek forgiveness, the people recited it; revelation then came with the Messenger’s faith and the final supplication, replacing the earlier burden through the plea not to be taken for forgetting or error.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r1.anchor: فلما اقترأها القوم وذلت بها ألسنتهم أنزل الله في إثرها { آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r2.claim: In al-Baghawī’s alternate narration from Ibn ʿAbbās, God answered “I have done so” and continued answering yes after each supplication through the end of the sura.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r2.anchor: قال البغوي : وفي رواية عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : قد فعلت

BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r3.claim: Biqāʿī says the revelation sequence establishes the coherence of the closing verses.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p552#2/r3.anchor: فقد تبين من هذا تناسب هذه الآيات

BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r1.claim: Al-Ḥarālī connects the closing assurance to the believers’ request for the straight path: the sura describes its followers, Jews as those under wrath, and Christians as astray, warning seekers to avoid their errors and submit to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r1.anchor: إلى آخر السورة قيل لهم : عليكم بالكتاب - إجابة لسؤالهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r2.claim: God rewards their faith by lifting the burdens, hardship, and accountability for mistakes and forgetfulness that marked the earlier community.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r2.anchor: وأنه أثابهم على إيمانهم رفع الإصر والمشقة والمؤاخذة بالخطأ والنسيان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r3.claim: Capacity is what a soul can bear and perform without incapacity: an intrinsically possible act within the person’s choice.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r3.anchor: أي ما تسعه وتطيقه ولا تعجز عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r4.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes actual assignment from what God may command: an act such as sleep, or a possible act known not to occur, is not assigned here even though such a command is conceptually permissible.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r4.anchor: سواء كان مما لا مدخل للإنسان في اختياره كالنوم أو كان له مدخل فيه وقد تعلق العلم الأزلي بعدم وقوعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r5.claim: The assurance is part of their supplication, praising God and asking Him to fulfill the Prophet’s promise; they fear being charged for unchosen inner whisperings they cannot prevent.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r5.anchor: وهذا الكلام من جملة دعائهم على وجه الثناء طلبا للوفاء بما أخبرهم به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم عنه سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r6.claim: The shift from direct address to speaking of God in the third person is a deferential appeal to His majesty and to His patience, mercy, and compassion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r6.anchor: ولعل العدول عن الخطاب إلى الغيبة بذكر الاسم الأعظم من باب التملق بأن له من صفات العظمة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r7.claim: Alternatively, God may be answering their “we hear and obey” by assuring them that uncommitted thoughts will not be counted, resolving the hardship of 2:284 unlike Israel’s disobedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p556/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك من قول الله سبحانه وتعالى جزاء لهم على قولهم { سمعنا وأطعنا }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r1.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the unaugmented verb denotes the least degree of earning, so even intending a good deed without doing it earns a good deed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r1.anchor: قال الحرالي : وصيغة فعل مجردة تعرب عن أدنى الكسب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r2.claim: The augmented iftiʿāl form for evil signals effortful engagement: sin is recorded only with firm resolve, and a person who intends evil but does not act is not charged.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r2.anchor: فشرط في الشر صيغة الافتعال الدالة على الاعتمال إشارة إلى أن من طبع النفس الميل إلى الهوى بكليتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r3.claim: A mere unfulfilled intention to sin is not counted against a person; different wording elsewhere may reflect the needs of its particular context.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r3.anchor: فلذلك من هم بسيئة فلم يعملها لم تكتب عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r4.claim: The supplications proceed from lighter requests to heavier ones, teaching that God did not punish forgetfulness or error, impose burdens, demand the impossible, or withhold pardon and mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r4.anchor: ولما بشرهم بذلك عرفهم مواقع نعمه في دعاء رتبه على الأخف فالأخف

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r5.claim: They ask God not to treat them like an adversary interrogating a litigant over every small and large matter.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r5.anchor: أي لا تفعل معنا فعل من يناظر خصما فهو يناقشه على كل صغير وكبير

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r6.claim: Forgetting means doing what was forbidden without remembering; error means doing it while remembering but without intending evil.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines error as an unintended departure from the proper limit despite intending or wishing to be right.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r7.anchor: قال الحرالي : والخطأ هو الزلل عن الحد عن غير تعمد بل مع عزم الإصابة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī takes God’s placing this plea on the servants’ tongues as a sign that He accepts it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r8.anchor: وفي إجرائه من كلام الله سبحانه وتعالى على لسان عباده قبوله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r9.claim: Repeating “our Lord” at the start of each request recalls the greatness of the occasion and God’s nurturing, kindness, and mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r9.anchor: وإعادة ربنا في صدر كل جملة من هذا الطراز كما تقدمت الإشارة إليه في التذكير بعظم المقام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r10.claim: Although God may impose whatever He wills and is not answerable for His acts, the believers ask Him not to place a heavy burden on them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r10.anchor: فإن له أن يكلف بما يشاء مع تحميل ما تعظم مشقته من التكاليف فإنه لا يسأل عما يفعل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r11.claim: Al-Ḥarālī explains iṣr as a weighty covenant whose bearing entails severe hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r11.anchor: قال الحرالي : هو العهد الثقيل أي الذي في تحمله أشد المشقة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r12.claim: The plea recalls that earlier communities received laws that could break their backs, making the present community’s lighter law a reason for gratitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r12.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه كان حمل على من سبق من الأحكام ما يهد الأركان تأكيدا لما يحمل على الشكر على تخفيف ذلك عنا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r13.claim: Biqāʿī traces iṣr to a root meaning to bend or incline; a heavy branch bends under its weight, explaining the word’s sense of burden.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r14.claim: As an example of earlier burdens, the second book of the Torah prescribes sprinkling sacrificial blood on the altar’s corners.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p557/r14.anchor: منها ما في السفر الثاني من التوراة في القربان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r1.claim: Biqāʿī cites the command that the Gospel community judge by God’s revelation in the Gospel while discussing the burdens imposed on earlier communities.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r1.anchor: وليحكم أهل الإنجيل بما أنزل الله فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r2.claim: Having affirmed that earlier burdens were just, believers acknowledge God’s sovereign right to impose even more, then ask Him not to load them beyond capacity; form II evokes the labor of such a burden.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r2.anchor: المالك التام الملك والملك المنفرد بالملك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r3.claim: Ṭāqa means ability or capacity; the request asks not to be made to bear what they cannot manage.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r4.claim: They ask God to remove the punishment for all sins, then not to mention those sins at all; pardon addresses bodily punishment and forgiveness spiritual torment.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r4.anchor: أي ارفع عنا عقاب الذنوب كلها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says mercy raises the pardoned and forgiven sinner to the same share of mercy as one who never sinned.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r5.anchor: ولما كان قد يلحق من يعفى عنه ويغفر له قصور في الرتبة عن منال الحظ من الرحمة ألحق تعالى المعفو عنه المغفور له بالمرحوم ابتداء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r6.claim: Biqāʿī explains mawlā as the enduring guardian who maintains care for those who entrust Him with what they cannot accomplish themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r6.anchor: والمولى هو الولي اللازم الولاية القائم بها الدائم عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r7.claim: Mawlā also means the one who brings guardianship to fruition through closeness and turning toward the ward; the petition seeks bodily reward in paradise and spiritual delight in vision.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r7.anchor: وكان حقيقته الفاعل لثمرة الولاية وهي القرب والإقبال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r8.claim: After asking for pardon, forgiveness, and mercy, believers seek the fruit of divine guardianship: victory through speech and arms.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r8.anchor: الدعاء بثمرة الولاية فقال : { فانصرنا } باللسان والسنان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r9.claim: Mentioning the opposing people’s strength urges sincere reliance on God, while calling them kāfirūn identifies those concealing the clear proofs described at the sura’s opening.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r9.anchor: أي الساترين للأدلة الدالة لهم على ربهم المذكورين أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r10.claim: Biqāʿī says the ending implies that fighting the disbelievers is obligatory and that they are the most hostile enemies.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p559/r10.anchor: فتضمن ذلك وجوب قتالهم وأنهم أعدى الأعداء

DURR-FULL:v2p127/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p127/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p127/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that 2:284 deeply distressed the Companions; the Prophet told them to hear and obey, then 2:285–286 came, and God affirmed each petition in 2:286 with “I have done so.”
DURR-FULL:v2p127/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله}

DURR-FULL:v2p128/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the Companions shared Ibn ʿUmar’s distress; God then revealed 2:286, removing liability for inner whispering beyond their capacity and leaving each person accountable for acquired speech and deeds.
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: يغفر الله لأبي عبد الرحمن لعمري لقد وجد المسلمون منها حين أنزلت مثل ما وجد عبد الله بن عمر

DURR-FULL:v2p128/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r2.claim: Salim reports that Ibn ʿUmar wept over 2:284; Ibn ʿAbbas says the Companions reacted similarly and that the following verse abrogated it.
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r2.anchor: فبلغ صنيعه ابن عباس فقال: يرحم الله أبا عبد الرحمن لقد صنع أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين أنزلت

DURR-FULL:v2p128/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r5.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r5.claim: ʿAli says the Companions were distressed that thoughts might be judged; this verse then abrogated the earlier accounting for thoughts.
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r5.anchor: عن علي قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} ) الآية أحزنتنا قلنا

DURR-FULL:v2p128/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud says accounting preceded the revelation of “each soul has what it earned,” which abrogated the earlier verse.
DURR-FULL:v2p128/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في الآية قال: كانت المحاسبة قبل أن تنزل (لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت)

DURR-FULL:v2p132/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p132/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p132/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God eased religious duties for believers, linking this to no hardship in religion (22:78), God’s desire for ease (2:185), and fearing God as much as possible (64:16).
DURR-FULL:v2p132/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها} قال: هم المؤمنون وسع الله عليهم أمر دينهم

DURR-FULL:v2p132/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p132/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p132/r13.claim: The Prophet tells ʿImran ibn Husayn, who had hemorrhoids, to pray standing, then sitting if unable, then on one side if unable to sit.
DURR-FULL:v2p132/r13.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين قال: كانت لي بواسير فسألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة فقال صل قائما

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses what accrues to a soul for or against it as its deeds.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت} قال: من العمل

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r2.claim: When this verse descended, believers worried about resisting involuntary thoughts; Gabriel answered that they cannot prevent such whisperings.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت ضج المؤمنون منها ضجة

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains wusʿ as a soul's capacity.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {إلا وسعها} قال: إلا طاقتها

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses wusʿ as what a person can bear.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك {إلا وسعها} قال: إلا ما تطيق

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r5.claim: The Prophet said God pardons his community's inward whisperings so long as they do not act on or speak them.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تجاوز عن أمتي

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r6.claim: The Prophet said God pardons his community's errors, forgetfulness, and coercion; al-Hasan affirmed this is expressed in the Quranic plea.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r6.anchor: عن أم الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله تجاوز لأمتي عن ثلاث

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r7.claim: The Prophet said God pardons his community for mistakes, forgetfulness, and actions done under compulsion.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله تجاوز لي عن أمتي

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r8.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r8.claim: The Prophet said God pardons his community for mistakes, forgetfulness, and actions done under compulsion.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r8.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تجاوز لي عن أمتي

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r9.speaker: ثوبان
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r9.claim: The Prophet said God pardons his community for mistakes, forgetfulness, and actions done under compulsion.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r9.anchor: عن ثوبان قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تجاوز لي عن أمتي

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r10.claim: The Prophet said God pardons his community for mistakes, forgetfulness, and actions done under compulsion.
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r10.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تجاوز لي عن أمتي

DURR-FULL:v2p133/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r11.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
DURR-FULL:v2p133/r11.claim: The Prophet said God has lifted from his community mistakes, forgetfulness, and actions done under compulsion.

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r1.speaker: أبو بكرة
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r1.claim: The Prophet said God lifted from this community mistakes, forgetfulness, and things they are forced to do.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r1.anchor: عن أبي بكرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رفع الله عن هذه الأمة

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r2.claim: Al-Hasan transmits from the Prophet that this community is excused for errors, forgetfulness, and compulsion.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r2.anchor: عن الحسن عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال تجوز لهذه الأمة الخطأ والنسيان

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r3.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi attributes to the Prophet the report that God pardons three things: error, forgetfulness, and coercion.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تجاوز لأمتي عن ثلاث

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r4.claim: Al-Hasan reports that God excuses a person for what he errs in, forgets, is compelled to do, or is overcome by.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r4.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تجاوز الله لابن آدم عما أخطأ

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r5.claim: When the plea against being taken to task for forgetting or erring was revealed, Gabriel told Muhammad that God had granted it.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r5.anchor: عن السدي قال: إن هذه الآية حين نزلت {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا} قال له جبريل

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses isr as a covenant or binding charge.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إصرا} قال: عهدا

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r7.claim: Mujahid also explains isr as a covenant.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} قال: عهدا

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq that isr is the covenant imposed on the Jews, whose breach led to transformation into apes and swine; Abu Talib's verse attests the Arabic usage.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj reads isr as an unbearable covenant imposed on Jews and Christians who failed it and were destroyed; he identifies the unbearable burden with transformation into apes and swine.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} قال: عهدا ألا نطيقه ولا نستطيع القيام به

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r10.claim: Qatada contrasts the harsh restrictions imposed on earlier communities with the easing, facility, and well-being given this community.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r10.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا} قال: كم من تشديد

DURR-FULL:v2p134/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r11.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r11.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah interprets the plea as asking not to be transformed into apes and swine.
DURR-FULL:v2p134/r11.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} قال: لا تمسخنا قردة وخنازير

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r1.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r1.claim: Al-Rabiʿ explains isr as the severe burden imposed on the People of the Book.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r1.anchor: عن الربيع في قوله {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} يقول: التشديد الذي شدد به

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن حسنة
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r2.claim: The Prophet reports that Israelites cut away urine with scissors when it touched them, illustrating a former legal hardship.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r2.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن حسنة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن بني إسرائيل كانوا إذا أصابهم البول

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r3.speaker: أبو موسى
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r3.claim: Abu Musa says Israelites used shears to cut away the place touched by urine.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r3.anchor: عن أبي موسى قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل إذا أصاب أحدهم البول يتبعه بالمقراضين

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r4.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r4.claim: A Jewish woman told Aisha that grave punishment comes from urine and that it is cut from skin and clothes; after Aisha relayed this, the Prophet confirmed it.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r4.anchor: عن عائشة قالت دخلت على امرأة من اليهود فقالت: إن عذاب القبر من البول

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the plea against isr to mean asking not to bear a sin for which there is no repentance or expiation.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في الآية قال: لا تحمل علينا ذنبا ليس فيه توبة ولا كفارة

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r6.speaker: الفضيل
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r6.claim: Al-Fudayl says an Israelite sinner had to kill himself as repentance, and that this severity was lifted from this community.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r6.anchor: عن الفضيل في قوله {ولا تحمل علينا إصرا} قال: كان الرجل من بني إسرائيل إذا أذنب

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r7.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak reads the plea as asking not to be assigned acts beyond one's ability.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك {ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} قال: لا تحملنا من الأعمال

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r8.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the unbearable load with the stringent prohibitions and fetters imposed on earlier people.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r8.anchor: عن السدي {ما لا طاقة لنا به} من التغليظ والأغلال التي كانت عليهم من التحريم

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r9.speaker: سلام بن سابور
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r9.claim: Salam ibn Sabur glosses the phrase as sexual desire.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r9.anchor: عن سلام بن سابور {ما لا طاقة لنا به} قال: الغلمة

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r10.speaker: مكحول
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r10.claim: Makhul interprets the unbearable matters as exile, sexual desire, and erection.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r10.anchor: عن مكحول {ما لا طاقة لنا به} قال: الغربة والغلمة والانعاظ

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd distinguishes pardon for falling short in commands, forgiveness for violating prohibitions, and mercy as necessary to fulfill commands and avoid prohibitions; no one is saved except through mercy.
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r11.anchor: عن ابن زيد {واعف عنا} إن قصرنا عن شيء مما أمرتنا به {واغفر لنا}

DURR-FULL:v2p135/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r12.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r12.claim: Gabriel brought the concluding supplications with a company of angels, and after each phrase God answered, 'That is yours.'
DURR-FULL:v2p135/r12.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: جاء بها جبريل ومعه من الملائكة ما شاء الله

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r1.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r1.claim: Gabriel recited the end of al-Baqara; after Muhammad memorized and recited it, God affirmed each letter as granted to him.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك قال أقرأ جبريل النبي آخر سورة البقرة فلما حفظها قال: اقرأها

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r2.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r2.claim: As Gabriel recited the pleas, the Prophet responded 'Amen, Lord of the worlds' after each one.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r2.anchor: عن عطاء قال: لما نزلت هذه الآيات {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا}

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r3.claim: Abu Dharr reports that these petitions were granted specifically to the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r3.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: هي للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Prophet asked God for these petitions and received them specifically for himself.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك في هذه الآية قال: كان عليه الصلاة والسلام فسألها نبي الله ربه

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r5.speaker: أبو ميسرة
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r5.claim: Abu Maysara says Gabriel taught the Prophet to say 'Amen' at the end of al-Baqara.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r5.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة أن جبريل لقن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند خاتمة البقرة: آمين

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r6.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r6.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal would say 'Amen' after reciting the closing plea for victory over the unbelievers.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r6.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل أنه كان إذا فرغ من قراءة هذه السورة {وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين}

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r7.speaker: جبير بن نغير
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r7.claim: Jubayr ibn Nufayr would say 'Amen, amen' when reciting al-Baqara's ending.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r7.anchor: عن جبير بن نغير أنه كان إذا قرأ خاتمة البقرة يقول: آمين آمين

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r8.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r8.claim: Hudhayfa says that after the Prophet recited al-Baqara in prayer, he praised God as Lord and said 'To You belongs praise' seven or ten times.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r8.anchor: عن حذيفة قال صليت خلف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ سورة البقرة

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r9.claim: The Prophet said that whoever recites the final two verses of al-Baqara at night will find them sufficient.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من قرأ الآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة في ليلة

DURR-FULL:v2p136/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r10.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r10.claim: The Prophet said God wrote a book two thousand years before creating heaven and earth, revealed two of its verses to close al-Baqara, and Satan does not approach a house where they are recited for three nights.
DURR-FULL:v2p136/r10.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله كتب كتابا قبل أن يخلق السماوات والأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God eased believers' religion, linking this to no hardship (22:78), willing ease (2:185), and fear as much as possible (64:16).
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله ، لا يكلف الله نفسا الا وسعها قال : هم المؤمنون ، وسع الله عليهم امر دينهم فقال الله ما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r2.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r2.claim: Sufyān applies the capacity limit to spending: only what one can afford.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r2.anchor: عن سفيان لا يكلف الله نفسا الا وسعها قال في شأن النفقة الا ما استطاعت

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan applies the verse to an unpayable vow: a person is not charged beyond capacity.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r3.anchor: فقال الحسن لا يكلف الله نفسا الا وسعها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r4.speaker: عامر الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbī glosses capacity as what the soul has done for itself.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r4.anchor: عن عامر الشعبي لا يكلف الله نفسا الا وسعها الا ما عملت لها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r5.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says people were not charged with work they could not bear; others are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r5.anchor: عن موسى بن عبيدة ، عن خالد بن زيد ، عن محمد بن كعب القرظي لا يكلف الله نفسا الا وسعها قال : فلم يكلفوا من العمل ما لم يطيقوا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r6.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r6.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote the same explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r6.anchor: عن معمر ، ان عمر بن عبد العزيز كتب : لا يكلف الله نفسا الا وسعها مثله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r7.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r7.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says a man unable to provide for family owes his wife only what he has.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r7.anchor: ومثله عن عطاء في الرجل ، لا يجد ما ينفق على اهله ، ليس لها الا ما وجد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r8.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r8.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī interprets the capacity limit as performance of obligatory duties.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r8.anchor: عن سفيان الثوري ، في قوله : لا يكلف الله نفسا الا وسعها قال اداء الفرائض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains what the soul earned as deeds it performed.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p577/r9.anchor: حدثني الزهري حدثنا سعيد بن مرجانة ، قال : قال ابن عباس : فانزل الله عز وجل : لا يكلف الله نفسا الا وسعها لها ما كسبت من العمل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r1.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb glosses what the soul earns for itself as good deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي لها ما كسبت من خير

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبدالله
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda b. ʿAbd Allāh says 2:284 was abrogated by the following verse, which assigns each soul its earned good and bad deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r2.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة بن عبدالله ، في قول الله : و ان تبدوا ما في انفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله الاية ، نسختها الاية

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the liability clause as referring to what a person has done.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فانزل الله و عليها ما اكتسبت من العمل .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب الرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r4.claim: The excerpt also attributes the opaque gloss بياض to Muḥammad b. Kaʿb for the liability clause, as printed.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب الرظي و عليها ما اكتسبت بياض

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r5.claim: The Prophet says God has waived three things for his community: error, forgetfulness, and coercion.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r5.anchor: عن أم الدراء ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ان الله تجاوز لامتي عن ثلاث ، عن الخطا و النسيان و الاستكراه :

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r6.claim: After Abū Bakr al-Hudhali told him the report, al-Ḥasan affirmed it and cited this prayer as Qur'anic evidence.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r6.anchor: فذكرت ذلك للحسن فقال : اجل ، ما تقرا بذلك قرانا ؟ ربنا لا تؤاخذنا ان نسينا أو اخطانا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports God's answer: I will not hold you accountable.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : ربنا لا تؤاخذنا ان نسينا أو اخطانا قال : لا اؤاخذكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r8.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the affirmative answer نعم to this plea.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ربنا لا تؤاخذنا ان نسينا أو اخطانا قال : نعم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r9.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr likewise gives God's answer as I will not hold you accountable.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p578/r9.anchor: عن سعيد لا تؤاخذنا ان نسينا أو اخطانا قال : لا اواخذكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the plea as God's answer that He will not impose the burden on them; Saʿīd b. Jubayr also reports this gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r1.anchor: قال ابن جبير ، عن ابن عباس ، في قول الله : و لا تحمل علينا اصرا قال : و لا احمل عليكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī understand iṣr as a covenant or binding commitment.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : و لا تحمل علينا اصرا قال : عهدا . وروى عن مجاهد و السدى ، نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r3.speaker: الحسن، الضحاك، مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Muqātil b. Ḥayyān give the related gloss mīthāq, a binding covenant.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r3.anchor: وروى عن الحسن و الضحاك و مقاتل بن حيان ، قالوا : ميثاقا .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r4.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ explains the iṣr as the severity God imposed on earlier People of the Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r4.anchor: عن الربيع ، قوله : و لا تحمل علينا اصرا كما حملته علي الذين من قبلنا يقول : التشديد الذي شددته

IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the answer نعم to the request not to impose the former burden.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ولا تحمل علينا اصرا كما حملته علي الذين من قبلنا قال : نعم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r6.claim: In a dialogue, Abū Hurayra asks Ibn ʿAbbās whether adultery and theft are therefore permitted; Ibn ʿAbbās says no, only Israel's special burden was lifted.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r6.anchor: قال : أبو هريرة ، لابن عباس : ما علينا من حرج ان تزنى أو ان تسرق ؟ قال : بلى . ولكن الاصر

IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r7.speaker: الفضيل
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r7.claim: Al-Fuḍayl says an Israelite who sinned was told to repent by killing himself, a burden removed from this community.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r7.anchor: قال الفضيل ، في قوله : و لا تحمل علينا اصرا كما حملته علي الذين من قبلنا قال : كان الرجل من بني اسرائيل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r8.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r8.claim: Muqātil b. Ḥayyān identifies those burdened before as the Jews and Christians, whom God destroyed.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p579/r8.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، قوله : كما حملته علي الذين من قبلنا كما حملته علي اليهود و النصارى فاهلكتهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the affirmative answer نعم to this plea.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة و لا تحملنا ما لاطاقة لنا به قال : نعم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك، محمد بن كعب، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muḥammad b. Kaʿb, and al-Suddī report God's answer as: I have done so.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r2.anchor: و روى ابن عباس و الضحاك و محمد بن كعب و السدى ، قال : يقوله الله عز و جل : قد فعلت

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r3.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr gives God's answer as: I will not impose it on you.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : لا احمله عليكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r4.claim: Muqātil interprets the unbearable burden as punishment that could turn people into apes and swine and punish them as earlier peoples were; Gabriel says the plea was granted, as Ibn Jurayj also reports.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r4.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قول الله : و لا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به من العذاب ، فتجعلنا كما جعلتهم قردة و خنازير

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r5.speaker: مكحول
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r5.claim: Makhūl glosses the burden as estrangement and intense sexual desire.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r5.anchor: عن مكحول ، في قوله : ربنا و لاتحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به قال : الغربة و الغلمة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r6.speaker: مكحول
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r6.claim: Makhūl gives a second gloss: erection.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r6.anchor: عن أبيه ، عن مكحول ، قال : الانعاظ .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r7.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the unbearable burden with the severe restrictions and prohibitions imposed on the Israelites.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r7.anchor: عن السدى قوله : و لا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به من التغليظ و الاغلال التي كانت عليهم من التحريم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports God's answer to the plea for pardon as: I have pardoned you.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قول الله تعالى

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة، محمد بن كعب، سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r9.claim: Abū Hurayra, Muḥammad b. Kaʿb, and Saʿīd b. Jubayr are also reported to give this answer of pardon.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r9.anchor: روى عن أبي هريرة و محمد بن كعب و سعيد بن جبير ، نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r10.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r10.claim: Muqātil b. Ḥayyān gives an alternative gloss: keep us safe from that.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r10.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قول الله : و اعف عنا قال : عافنا من ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports God's answer to the plea for forgiveness as: I have forgiven you.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قول الله تعالى

IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r12.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة، سعيد بن جبير، السدي، مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r12.claim: Abū Hurayra, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, al-Suddī, and Muqātil b. Ḥayyān are also reported to give this answer of forgiveness.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p580/r12.anchor: روى عن أبي هريرة و سعيد بن جبير والسدى و مقاتل بن حيان ، نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits God's affirmative response نعم to the plea for mercy and acknowledgment of His guardianship.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة فانزل الله : و ارحمنا انت مولانا قال : نعم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، ابن عباس، عطاء الخراساني، مقاتل بن حيان، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r2.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says God's answer is that He has shown mercy; Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, Muqātil, and al-Suddī are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : و ارحمنا قال قد رحمتكم . وروى عن ابن عباس و عطاء الخراساني و مقاتل بن حيان و السدى

IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports God's answer as: you have been given victory over the disbelievers.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : فانصرنا علي القوم الكافرين قال : قد نصرتم علي القوم الكافرين .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة، سعيد بن جبير، محمد بن كعب، الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, Muḥammad b. Kaʿb, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk are also reported to give the answer that victory was granted.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p582/r4.anchor: وروى عن أبي هريرة و سعيد بن جبير ومحمد بن كعب و الضحاك ، نحو ذلك .

IBNHIBBAN:v1p350/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v1p350/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNHIBBAN:v1p350/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that 2:284 distressed the Companions; the Prophet told them to affirm hearing and obedience, then God revealed 2:285 and 2:286, answering ‘yes’ to each plea in 2:286.
IBNHIBBAN:v1p350/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: لما نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية {لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا

IBNHIBBAN:5069/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:5069/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNHIBBAN:5069/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says 2:284 unsettled the Companions; the Prophet told them to affirm hearing, obedience, and surrender, after which God put faith in their hearts and answered the pleas not to be taken for forgetfulness or to bear the burden imposed on earlier peoples.
IBNHIBBAN:5069/r1.anchor: عن بن عباس قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} [البقرة: 284]

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur's preferred reading takes the assurance as God's own parenthetical speech among the believers' quoted words, displaying the fruit of faith and obedience and promising no undue religious hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r1.anchor: الأظهر أنه من كلام الله تعالى ، لا من حكاية كلام الرسول والمؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r2.speaker: author
