IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r2.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet and believers may be speaking, explaining their assent as understanding that only thoughts with voluntary outward effects or settled conviction incur account; Ibn Ashur says the following clause makes this unlikely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من كلام الرسول والمؤمنين ، كأنه تعليل لقولهم سمعنا وأطعنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة، ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r3.claim: In a Muslim report from Abu Hurayra and Ibn Abbas, companions feared the accountability verse, the Prophet told them to hear, obey, and submit, God strengthened their faith, and then this verse was revealed to lift the burden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r3.anchor: وهذا مروي في ( صحيح مسلم ) عن أبي هريرة وابن عباس أنه قال : لما نزلت { وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r4.claim: Calling this abrogation follows early scholars' terminology; Ibn Ashur says it is clarification and specification, since adjacent verses may have been revealed at different times and believers could have feared hardship in the interval.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p134/r4.anchor: وإطلاق النسخ على هذا اصطلاح للمتقدمين ، والمراد البيان والتخصيص لأن الذي تطمئن له النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r1.claim: The verse rules out religious obligations beyond customary human ability, without making claims about capacity under the hidden decree; Ibn Ashur uses it against the Jabriyya.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية تقتضي عدم وقوع التكليف بما لا يطاق في الشريعة ، بحسب المتعارف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r2.claim: The clause is circumstantial from nafs and explains capacity: good benefits the soul and evil harms it, marked respectively by li and ʿala.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r2.anchor: وقوله : { لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت } حال من ( نفسا ) لبيان كيفية الوسع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r3.claim: Kasaba and iktasaba are synonymous in Arabic here; the latter is not literally a verb of compliance, and the forms vary to avoid repetition, as Dhu al-Rumma illustrates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r3.anchor: كما فعل ذو الرمة في قوله : ومطعمم الصيد هبال لبغيته ألفى أباه بذاك الكسب مكتسبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r4.claim: Al-Nabigha's paired forms hamalat and ihtamalat likewise exemplify stylistic variation rather than a fixed good-versus-evil distinction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r4.anchor: وقول النابغة : فحملت برة واحتملت فجار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r5.claim: Choosing the form that can imply compliance for evil suggests Satan commands and the soul obeys, disfavoring sins; using kasaba for good suggests God guides people to it by innate disposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r5.anchor: وقد تكون ، في اختيار الفعل الذي أصله دال على المطاوعة ، إشارة إلى أن الشرور يأمر بها الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r6.claim: Al-Kashshaf says iktasaba signals exertion because the soul desires evil and works to obtain it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r6.anchor: ووقع في ( الكشاف ) أن فعل المطاوعة لدلالته على الاعتمال ، وكان الشر مشتهى للنفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r7.claim: Some exegetes distinguish kasb as acquiring good from iktisab as acquiring evil, but Ibn Ashur rejects this as inaccurate and cites Quranic usage of kasaba for evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r7.anchor: فمن أجل ذلك ظن بعض المفسرين أن الكسب هو اجتناء الخير ، والاكتساب هو اجتناء الشر ، وهو خلاف التحقيق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r8.claim: It is also said that iktasaba denotes effort when paired with kasaba, though the Quran never uses iktasabat for good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p137/r8.anchor: وقد قيل : إن اكتسب إذا اجتمع مع كسب خص بالعمل الذي فيه تكلف . لكن لم يرد التعبير باكتسبت في جانب فعل الخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r1.claim: The supplication may be quoted from the believers after their assent in 2:285 as they turn to seek recompense and intimate conversation with God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذا الدعاء محكيا من قول المؤمنين : الذين قالوا : { سمعنا وأطعنا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r2.claim: Placing the prayer at the end completes the notice that the sura is ending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r2.anchor: واختيار حكاية هذا عنهم في آخر السورة تكملة للإيذان بانتهائها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, God may be teaching the believers this prayer, as He taught the praise in al-Fatiha, after establishing that He does not impose beyond capacity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تلقينا من جانب الله تعالى إياهم : بأن يقولوا هذا الدعاء ، مثل ما لقنوا التحميد في سورة الفاتحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r4.claim: The prayer seeks continued relief from burdens beyond capacity, so it will not be withdrawn in anger as earlier permitted foods were withheld from the Jews.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r4.anchor: والمراد من الدعاء به طلب الدوام على ذلك لئلا ينسخ ذلك من جراء غضب الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r5.claim: Muakhadha derives from taking in the sense of punishment, and the reciprocal form intensifies the plea not to punish for forgetfulness or error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r5.anchor: والمؤاخذة مشتقة من الأخذ بمعنى العقوبة ، كقوله : { وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r6.claim: Forgetfulness and error mean the resulting deed or omission that God does not approve.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r6.anchor: والمراد ما يترتب على النسيان والخطأ من فعل أو ترك لا يرضيان الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r7.claim: A report recorded by Ibn Majah says error, forgetfulness, and compulsion were lifted from the Prophet's community; it also circulates with وضع, al-Nawawi graded it hasan, and Ahmad rejected it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r7.anchor: وقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه ) وفي رواية : ( وضع ) رواه ابن ماجه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r8.claim: The report's meaning is sound for exemption from religious address, but liability for destruction and compensation remains; therefore the prayer can still ask not to be punished for an error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r8.anchor: ومعناه صحيح في غير ما يرجع إلى الخطاب الوضع . فالمعنى رفع الله عنهم المؤاخذة فبقيت المؤاخذة بالإتلاف والغرامات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r9.claim: Believers prayed this before learning that God had lifted such accountability, so there is no need to follow al-Kashshaf's reading of forgetfulness and error as negligence that causes them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p139#2/r9.anchor: فهذه دعوة من المؤمنين دعوها قبل أن يعلموا أن الله رفع عنهم ذلك بقوله : { لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r1.claim: Repeating the address to God between coordinated clauses, though unnecessary, displays humility and supplication.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r1.anchor: فصل بين الجملتين المتعاطفتين ، بإعادة النداء ، مع أنه مستغنى عنه : لأن مخاطبة المنادى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r2.claim: Carrying is a metaphor for imposing a severe duty that weighs on the soul, preparing the image of a burden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r2.anchor: والحمل مجاز في التكليف بأمر شديد يثقل على النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r3.claim: Isr originally means what is used to bind and fasten things; it later denotes a solemn covenant difficult to fulfill and then a burdensome obligation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r3.anchor: وأصل معنى الإصر ما يؤصر به أي يربط ، وتعقد به الأشياء ، ويقال له : الإصار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r4.speaker: الزجاج، الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Zamakhshari explain isr here and in 7:157 as something burdensome to perform and obey; Ibn Ashur says that sense is intended here and that حمل reinforces the burden metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r4.anchor: وبذلك فسره الزجاج والزمخشري هنا وفي قوله ، في سورة الأعراف ( 157 ) : ويضع عنهم إصرهم وهو المقصود هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets isr as a covenant the community could not fulfill, whose breach would bring punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p140/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : { ولا تحمل علينا إصرا } عهدا لا نفي به ، ونعذب بتركه ونقضه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r1.claim: The phrase qualifies isr as a religious burden like difficult rules imposed on earlier peoples, such as Israel's forty years in the wilderness and the rare features of the cow they had to slaughter; these disciplined disobedience and disregard for their messengers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r1.anchor: مثل ما كلف به بعض الأمم الماضية من الأحكام الشاقة مثل أمر بني إسرائيل بتيه أربعين سنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r2.claim: Muhammad's description as one who removes their burdens supports this reading of the prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r2.anchor: قال تعالى في صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ويضع عنهم إصرهم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r3.claim: The unbearable load here means punishments people cannot endure, with the doubled verb form serving a causative function.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r3.anchor: أي ما لا نستطيع حمله من العقوبات . والتضعيف فيه للتعدية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r4.claim: Some distinguish the first prayer as relief from earlier peoples' punishments and the second as relief from severe obligations; Ibn Ashur treats both prayers like the plea not to be taken to task.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r4.anchor: وقيل : هذا دعاء بمعافاتهم من التكاليف الشديدة ، والذي قبله دعاء بمعافاتهم من العقوبات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r5.claim: Ṭāqa derives from iṭāqa, with the hamza dropped for ease, as in jāba/ijāba and ṭāʿa/iṭāʿa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141/r5.anchor: والطاقة في الأصل الإطاقة خففت بحذف الهمزة كما قالوا : جابة وإجابة وطاعة وإطاعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r1.claim: The closing pleas omit another ربنا because it has already been repeated three times, and Arabs avoid repeating a word more than three times except for emphasis or alarm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r1.anchor: إما لأنه تكرر ثلاث مرات ، والعرب تكره تكرير اللفظ أكثر من ثلاث مرات إلا في مقام التهويل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, pardon, forgiveness, and mercy generalize the preceding specific requests and are their foundations, making this one encompassing prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r2.anchor: فإن العفو أصل لعدم المؤاخذة ، والمغفرة أصل لرفع المشقة والرحمة أصل لعدم العقوبة الدنيوية والأخروية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r3.claim: The clause أنت مولانا is set apart as the reason for the preceding requests and as a premise for the following one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r3.anchor: وقوله : { أنت مولانا } فصله لأنه كالعلة للدعوات الماضية : أي دعوناك ورجونا منك ذلك لأنك مولانا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r4.claim: The appeal to God's patronage rests on a patron's duty to treat dependents gently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p141#2/r4.anchor: ومن شأن المولى الرفق بالمملوك ، وليكون هذا أيضا كالمقدمة للدعوة الآتية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r1.claim: The فاء derives the plea for victory from God's role as patron, since a patron is expected to aid those under his care.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r1.anchor: جيء فيه بالفاء للتفريع عن كونه مولى ، لأن شأن المولى أن ينصر مولاه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r2.speaker: مرة بن عداء الفقعسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur cites Murra ibn Adāʾ al-Faqʿasi's poem lamenting patrons who abandon their client as the days turn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r2.anchor: في قول مرة بن عداء الفقعسي :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r3.claim: The request's derivation from God's established guardianship over believers strengthens its insistence and recalls 2:257.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r3.anchor: قال تعالى : { الله ولي الذين آمنوا } ( البقرة : 257 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r4.claim: At Uhud, after Abu Sufyan boasted of al-Uzza, the Prophet instructed the Muslims to answer that God is their patron and their opponents have no patron.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r4.anchor: وفي حديث يوم أحد لما قال أبو سفيان : ( لنا العزى ولا عزى لكم ) قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أجيبوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r5.claim: Victory gathers worldly and otherworldly good: it brings security and flourishing, makes the faith prevail, prevents persecution, and draws people into Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r5.anchor: ووجه الاهتمام بهذه الدعوة أنها جامعة لخيري الدنيا والآخرة ؛ لأنهم إذا نصروا على العدو ، فقد طاب عيشهم وظهر دينهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r6.speaker: أبو مسعود الأنصاري البدري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r6.claim: A report in the Sahih says the Prophet taught that reciting the last two verses of al-Baqara at night suffices the reciter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r6.anchor: وفي ( الصحيح ) ، عن أبي مسعود الأنصاري البدري : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( من قرأ الآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة ، في ليلة ، كفتاه )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r7.claim: The sufficiency may mean the two verses replace night prayer, or that they provide blessing and protection from devils and harms; Ibn Ashur suggests both meanings are intended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p142/r7.anchor: قيل معناه كفتاه عن قيام الليل ، فيكون معنى من قرأ من صلى بهما ، وقيل معناه كفتاه بركة وتعوذا من الشياطين والمضار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r2.claim: Souls that seek good and salvation must expose themselves to one of the two paths after reflection; each bears what it has earned.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r2.anchor: فما على الأنفس المريدة الخير والنجاة إلا التعرض لأحد المهيعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r1.claim: The verse states God assigns no act of heart or body beyond capacity, comprehension, and constitution, relieving anxiety about passing thoughts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r1.anchor: خبر جزم نص على أنه لا يكلف العباد من وقت نزول الآية عبادة من أعمال القلوب والجوارح إلا وهي في وسع المكلف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r2.claim: Those denying rational possibility of impossible duties read the verse as saying God neither does nor has imposed one; Ibn Atiyya says this is not explicit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r2.anchor: وتأول من ينكر جواز تكليف ما لا يطاق هذه الآية بمعنى أنه لا يكلف ولا كلف وليس ذلك بنص في الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r3.claim: This accords with verses saying God intends ease, places no hardship in religion, and requires mindfulness as far as possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r3.anchor: وهذا المعنى الذي ذكرناه في هذه الآية يجري مع معنى قوله تعالى يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري وجماعة من المتكلمين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r4.claim: Al-Ashari and other theologians hold that imposing an impossible duty is rationally possible, not religiously forbidden, and signals certain punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r4.anchor: فقال أبو الحسن الأشعري وجماعة من المتكلمين تكليف ما لا يطاق جائز عقلا ولا يحرم ذلك شيئا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya compares this assignment to a hadith's command that a sculptor make a hair.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r5.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وينظر إلى هذا تكليف المصور أن يعقد شعيرة حسب الحديث.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r6.claim: One group says impossible duty occurred in Abu Lahab's case: he was foretold as doomed to disbelief while commanded to believe.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r6.anchor: فقالت فرقة وقع في نازلة أبي لهب لأنه حكم عليه بتب اليدين وصلي النار،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r7.claim: Another group says no impossible duty occurred; the threat that Abu Lahab enters the Fire means if he persists in disbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p392#3/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة لم يقع قط، وقوله تعالى: سيصلى نارا [المسد: 3]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r1.claim: Impossibility may be logical, customary, physically fatal, or due to being occupied with another task; the last is figurative usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r1.anchor: وما لا يطاق ينقسم أقساما: فمنه المحال عقلا كالجمع بين الضدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r2.claim: Takallafa takes two objects, with one omitted here, understood as worship or another thing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r2.anchor: ويكلف يتعدى إلى مفعولين أحدهما محذوف تقديره «عبادة» أو شيئا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r3.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads wus'aha with open waw and kasra on the sin; Ibn Atiyya calls this a metathesis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «إلا وسعها» بفتح الواو وكسر السين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r4.speaker: السدي وجماعة من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r4.claim: Al-Suddi and other exegetes say what one earns for oneself is good deeds and what lies against one is bad deeds; thoughts are not acquired.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r4.anchor: وعليها ما اكتسبت يريد من السيئات، قاله السدي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r5.claim: Good deeds belong to the person because they bring joy and are counted as property; evil deeds are burdens and debts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r5.anchor: وجاءت العبارة في الحسنات ب لها من حيث هي مما يفرح الإنسان بكسبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r6.claim: The repeated root with different verb forms beautifies the style, as in the contrast between fa-mahhil and amhil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r6.anchor: وكرر فعل الكسب فخالف بين التصريف حسنا لنمط الكلام.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r7.claim: Good deeds follow God's path without strain, while sins require the effort of crossing His prohibition; Ibn Atiyya prefers this as the reason for differing forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r7.anchor: والذي يظهر لي في هذا أن الحسنات هي مما يكسب دون تكلف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r8.speaker: المهدوي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r8.claim: Al-Mahdawi and others say no one is held accountable for another's sin; Ibn Atiyya says the principle is true but not established by this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r8.anchor: وقال المهدوي وغيره: وقيل معنى الآية لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب أحد.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r9.claim: Rabbana la tu'akhidhna means: say this in your supplication.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p393/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ربنا لا تؤاخذنا معناه قولوا في دعائكم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r1.speaker: الطبري وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r1.claim: Al-Tabari and others take forgetting as neglecting obedience and error as intentional sin; involuntary forgetfulness and error are already excused.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r1.anchor: فذهب الطبري وغيره إلى أنه النسيان بمعنى الترك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r2.claim: Many scholars, including Ibn Atiyya, hold that the prayer concerns involuntary forgetfulness and unintentional error; he calls this correct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r2.anchor: وذهب كثير من العلماء إلى أن الدعاء في هذه الآية إنما هو في النسيان الغالب والخطأ غير المقصود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r3.claim: Qatada says he was told the Prophet stated that God excused his community for forgetfulness and error.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r3.anchor: قال قتادة في تفسير الآية بلغني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says that after believers recited the prayer at its revelation, Gabriel told the Prophet God had granted it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r4.anchor: وقال السدي لما نزلت هذه الآية فقالوها قال جبريل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r5.claim: Believers feared the reckoning in 2:284 and seek protection from forgetfulness and error beyond human control; on this reading an impossible duty is possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r5.anchor: وذلك أن المؤمنين لما كشف عنهم ما خافوه في قوله تعالى: يحاسبكم به الله [البقرة: 284]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r6.speaker: الطبري والزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r6.claim: Al-Tabari and al-Zajjaj deny impossible duties: forgetting means omitted duties, error intentional disobedience, and the burden Israelite obligations and punishments.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r6.anchor: ومذهب الطبري والزجاج أن تكليف ما لا يطاق غير جائز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r7.speaker: الطبري والزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r7.claim: For these authors the burden included killing themselves, cutting their bodies, bodily punishment for sins, and difficult covenants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r7.anchor: والإصر هي العبادات الثقيلة كتكاليف بني إسرائيل من قتل أنفسهم وقرض أبدانهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r8.claim: Akhṭa'a can describe intentional action as well as genuine mistake or deliberated action.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r8.anchor: وأما لفظة «أخطأ» فقد تجيء في القصد ومع الاجتهاد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r9.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وابن عباس والسدي وابن جريج والربيع وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r9.claim: These exegetes explain isr as a firm covenant or solemn pact.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: الإصر العهد والميثاق الغليظ. وقاله مجاهد وابن عباس والسدي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r10.speaker: عطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r10.claim: Ata interprets the burden as transformation into apes and swine.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء: الإصر المسخ قردة وخنازير.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd also explains isr as a sin for which there is neither expiation nor repentance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r11.anchor: وقال ابن زيد أيضا: الإصر الذنب لا كفارة فيه ولا توبة منه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r1.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r1.claim: Malik defines isr as a weighty, difficult matter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r1.anchor: الإصر: الأمر الغليظ الصعب. قال القاضي أبو محمد:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya links these senses to the root for something binding, such as a cord tying loads.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r2.anchor: والإصرة في اللغة الأمر الرابط من ذمام أو قرابة أو عهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r3.speaker: عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r3.claim: A reading transmitted from Asim has isran with damma on the hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r3.anchor: وروي عن عاصم أنه قرأ أصرا بضم الهمزة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r4.claim: Those who came before are the Jews; al-Dahhak adds the Christians.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r4.anchor: ولا خلاف أن الذين من قبلنا يراد به اليهود. قال الضحاك: والنصارى،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r5.claim: Qatada asks not to be burdened with the same harshness as those before us.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r5.anchor: فقال قتادة لا تشدد علينا كما شددت على من كان قبلنا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd understand the plea as asking not to be burdened with acts beyond capacity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: لا تحملنا من الأعمال ما لا نطيق، وقال نحوه ابن زيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets it as asking God not to transform believers into apes and swine.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: لا تمسخنا قردة وخنازير،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r8.speaker: سلام بن سابور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r8.claim: Salam ibn Sabur says the unbearable thing is sexual desire; al-Naqqash transmits this from Mujahid, Ata, and Mak'hul.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r8.anchor: وقال سلام بن سابور: الذي لا طاقة لنا به الغلمة، وحكاه النقاش عن مجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r9.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r9.claim: Abu al-Darda seeks refuge from sexual desire for which there is no means of satisfaction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r9.anchor: وروي أن أبا الدرداء كان يقول في دعائه: وأعوذ بك من غلمة ليس لها عدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r10.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the unbearable burden as prohibitions and fetters imposed on the Israelites.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r10.anchor: وقال السدي: هو التغليظ والأغلال التي كانت على بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r11.claim: Pardon concerns what believers committed and disclosed; forgiveness asks God to conceal what He knows; mercy asks for freely initiated favor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r11.anchor: واعف عنا أي فيما واقعناه وانكشف واغفر لنا أي استر علينا ما علمت منا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r12.claim: The petitions are distinct approaches to prayer, though all seek entry into Paradise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r12.anchor: فهي مناح للدعاء متباينة وإن كان الغرض المراد بكل واحد منها واحدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r13.claim: Calling God our mawla praises Him, draws the supplicant near, and thanks Him; mawla derives from wali and denotes guardianship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r13.anchor: وأنت مولانا مدح في ضمنه تقرب إليه وشكر على نعمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r14.claim: Victory over unbelievers enables the law to stand, the Muslim word to prevail, and the way to obedience to remain open.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r14.anchor: ثم ختمت الدعوة بطلب النصر على الكافرين الذي هو ملاك قيام الشرع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r15.speaker: جبريل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r15.claim: Gabriel teaches Muhammad the petitions one by one and answers that God has granted each through the end of the sura.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r15.anchor: وروي أن جبريل عليه السلام أتى محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r16.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r16.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal is reported to say amin after reciting the sura.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r16.anchor: وروي عن معاذ بن جبل أنه كان إذا فرغ من قراءة هذه السورة قال آمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Muadh's practice may be a Prophetic report, or sound analogy with al-Fatiha because both contain supplication.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r1.anchor: هذا يظن به أنه رواه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فإن كان ذلك فكمال،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r2.speaker: أبو مسعود عقبة بن عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r2.claim: Abu Masud Uqba ibn Amr transmits that reciting the last two verses at night suffices in place of night prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r2.anchor: وروى أبو مسعود عقبة بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: من قرأ الآيتين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r3.claim: Ali says he doubts anyone who understands Islam would sleep without reciting the two verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: ما أظن أحدا عقل وأدرك الإسلام ينام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r4.claim: The Prophet says he received the final verses from a treasure beneath the Throne, a gift no one before him received.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r4.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أوتيت هؤلاء الآيات من آخر سورة البقرة

MUSLIM:329/r3.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:329/r3.speaker: الله تعالى
MUSLIM:329/r3.claim: In Abu Hurayra’s account, Allah answers yes to the petitions in 2:286: pardon for forgetfulness and error, relief from burdens and incapacity, forgiveness, mercy, and aid.
MUSLIM:329/r3.anchor: ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا‏}‏ قال نعم

MUSLIM:329/r4.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:329/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSLIM:329/r4.claim: The report explicitly says Allah abrogated the earlier passage about accounting for inner thoughts and then revealed the assurance that He burdens no soul beyond its capacity.
MUSLIM:329/r4.anchor: فلما فعلوا ذلك نسخها الله تعالى

MUSLIM:330/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:330/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
MUSLIM:330/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning about hidden thoughts deeply troubled the believers; the Prophet told them to hear, obey, and submit, and Allah placed faith in their hearts before revealing 2:286.
MUSLIM:330/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال لما نزلت هذه الآية

MUSLIM:330/r2.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:330/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
MUSLIM:330/r2.claim: Allah answers “I have done so” to the believers’ prayers for protection from error and burdens, and for forgiveness, mercy, and His guardianship.
MUSLIM:330/r2.anchor: ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r1.anchor: الوسع الطاقة قاله ابن عباس وقتادة ومعناه لا يكلفها ما لا قدرة لها عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r2.claim: The verse means God does not impose what a person cannot do, since that would be impossible, like requiring a paralytic to run or a blind person to see.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r2.anchor: لا يكلفها ما لا قدرة لها عليه لاستحالته كتكليف الزمن السعي والأعمى النظر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r3.claim: It is possible to impose a task a person cannot fulfill because of absent means, such as faith on someone eternally known not to believe; this verse concerns impossibility in itself.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r4.claim: The prayer later in the verse asks not to be burdened with what cannot be borne; if impossible obligations could never be imposed, that request would be pointless.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari instead understands the request as asking not to be given a burdensome task, though it could be performed with strain; Arabs say they cannot bear looking at someone they actually can look at.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r6.anchor: المعنى لا تحملنا ما يثقل علينا أداؤه وان كنا مطيقين له على تجشم وتحمل مكروه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that what accrues to a person is obedience and what accrues against them is disobedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس لها ما كسبت من طاعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر النقاش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r2.claim: Al-Naqqash says the wording “for her” points to good and “against her” points to evil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر النقاش فقوله لها دليل على الخير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r3.claim: One view distinguishes kasabat for a single occurrence and iktasabat for repeated acts over time.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r3.anchor: وقد ذهب قوم إلى أن كسبت لمرة ومرات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r4.claim: Another view treats kasabat and iktasabat as two forms with the same meaning, as in 86:17.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r4.anchor: وهما عند آخرين لغتان بمعنى واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r5.claim: This prayer is God's instruction to people to say these words.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r5.anchor: هذا تعليم من الله للخلق أن يقولوا ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari takes forgetting here as deliberate neglect, since involuntary forgetfulness is already exempt from sin; he likewise takes error here as intentional, though the word can also mean inadvertence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بالنسيان هاهنا الترك مع العمد لأن النسيان الذي هو بمعنى الغفلة قد أمنت الآثام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الضحاك، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r7.claim: One interpretation of iṣr is a covenant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r7.anchor: وفي الإصر قولان أحدهما أنه العهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation is a burden: a request not to impose the heavy obligations imposed on the Children of Israel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r8.anchor: الثاني الثقل أي لا تثقل علينا من الفروض ما ثقلته على بني اسرائيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r1.speaker: الضحاك، السدي، ابن زيد، الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r1.claim: The first of five views understands this as asking not to be given deeds that are difficult and arduous.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r1.anchor: قاله الضحاك والسدي وابن زيد والجمهور والثاني أنه المحبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r2.speaker: الثوري عن منصور عن إبراهيم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r2.claim: A second view takes the unbearable thing to be love.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه المحبة رواه الثوري عن منصور عن إبراهيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r3.speaker: مكحول
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r3.claim: A third view identifies it as sexual desire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r3.anchor: والثالث الغلمة قاله مكحول والرابع حديث النفس ووساوسها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r4.claim: A fourth view identifies it as inner thoughts and their whisperings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r4.anchor: والرابع حديث النفس ووساوسها والخامس عذاب النار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r5.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r5.claim: The fifth view takes it as the punishment of Hell.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r6.claim: Anta mawlānā means “You are our protector.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r6.anchor: ﴾ أي أنت ولينا ﴿ فانصرنا ﴾ أي أعنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r7.anchor: وكان معاذ إذا فرغ من هذه السورة قال آمين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r8.speaker: معاذ
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r8.claim: Muʿadh used to say “Amen” after finishing this surah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r8.anchor: وكان معاذ إذا فرغ من هذه السورة قال آمين

MUSNAD-AHMAD:2070/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2070/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2070/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that 2:284 troubled believers; the Prophet told them to answer ‘We hear and obey,’ and God then revealed the closing passage of al-Baqara, including 2:286.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2070/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: {إن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r1.claim: When 2:284 alarmed the Companions as beyond their capacity, the Prophet instructed them to say ‘We hear and obey’; after they accepted, God revealed 2:285–286 and replaced the burden with the limit of each soul's capacity.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: لما نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r3.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r3.claim: The report glosses the capacity verse as assigning the soul the good it earns and charging it with the evil it acquires.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r3.anchor: فصار له ما كسب من خير، وعليه ما اكتسب (3) من شر

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r4.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r4.speaker: العلاء
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r4.claim: Al-Ala transmits affirmative answers to the petitions against forgetfulness, burdens, and inability, then quotes the final request for pardon, mercy, and help.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9344/r4.anchor: فسر العلاء هذا: {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا} [البقرة: 286] ، قال: نعم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r1.speaker: أبو مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says that whoever recites the two closing verses of al-Baqara at night will find them sufficient; Ibn Kathir cites several transmission routes and gives no grading here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي مسعود، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من قرأ بالآيتين"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r2.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying that he received the closing verses of al-Baqara from a treasure beneath the Throne, a gift given to no prophet before him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أعطيت خواتيم سورة البقرة من كنز تحت العرش، لم يعطهن نبي قبلي"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that during the Night Journey, at the Sidrat al-Muntaha in the sixth heaven, the Prophet received the five prayers, the closing verses of al-Baqara, and forgiveness for non-polytheists from his community even for grave sins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p733#2/r3.anchor: عن مرة، عن عبد الله، قال: لما أسري برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انتهي به إلى سدرة المنتهى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r1.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r1.claim: The Prophet tells Uqba ibn Amir to recite the final two verses of al-Baqara, saying they were given from beneath the Throne; Ibn Kathir calls the chain hasan, though the major collections do not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r1.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "اقرأ الآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة فإني أعطيتهما من تحت العرش"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r2.speaker: حذيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r2.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet saying that his community was favored with these verses from a treasure beneath the Throne, given to no one before or after him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "فضلنا على الناس بثلاث، أوتيت هؤلاء الآيات من آخر سورة البقرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r3.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r3.claim: Ali says that no person who understands Islam should go to sleep without reciting the closing verses, a treasure granted to the Prophet from beneath the Throne.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r3.anchor: عن علي قال: لا أرى أحدا عقل الإسلام ينام حتى يقرأ خواتيم سورة البقرة، فإنها كنز أعطيه نبيكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r4.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r4.claim: In another transmission Ali adds Ayat al-Kursi to the nightly recitation of the closing verses, describing both as a treasure beneath the Throne.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r4.anchor: عن علي قال: ما أرى أحدا يعقل، بلغه الإسلام، ينام حتى يقرأ آية الكرسي وخواتيم سورة البقرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r5.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r5.claim: The Prophet says God wrote a book two thousand years before creating the heavens and earth, sent down from it the two verses ending al-Baqara, and that a house where they are recited is not approached by Satan for three nights. Al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb; al-Hakim calls it sahih by Muslim's standard, though they did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p734/r5.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الله كتب كتابا قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض بألفي عام، أنزل منه آيتين ختم بهما (4) سورة البقرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet laughed when reciting the closing verses and Ayat al-Kursi, saying they are from the Merciful's treasure beneath the Throne; reciting 4:123 and 53:39–41 instead made him grieve and submit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ آخر سورة البقرة وآية الكرسي ضحك، وقال: "إنهما من كنز الرحمن تحت العرش"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r2.speaker: معقل بن يسار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r2.claim: The Prophet says he was given the Opening of the Book and the closing verses of al-Baqara from beneath the Throne, while the Mufassal was given as an extra voluntary portion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r2.anchor: عن معقل بن يسار، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أعطيت فاتحة الكتاب، وخواتيم سورة البقرة من تحت العرش، والمفصل نافلة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Gabriel brought news of two lights never given to an earlier prophet: al-Fatiha and the closing verses of al-Baqara; every letter recited from them brings a gift.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده جبريل؛ إذ سمع نقيضا فوقه، فرفع جبريل بصره إلى السماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r4.speaker: رجل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r4.claim: In a report in al-Darimi, the Prophet names Ayat al-Kursi as the greatest verse and says he would choose the end of al-Baqara for his community because it contains every good of this world and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p735/r4.anchor: حدثنا صفوان، حدثنا أيفع بن عبد الله الكلاعي (2) قال: قال رجل: يا رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p736#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p736#2/r5.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p736#2/r5.claim: Jabir reports that after this verse was revealed, Gabriel told the Prophet that God had praised him and his community and invited him to ask; the Prophet then asked for the closing supplication beginning, 'God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.'
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p736#2/r5.anchor: عن حكيم عن جابر قال: لما نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه والمؤمنون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r1.claim: God never imposes on a person more than they can bear; this expresses His kindness, mercy, and beneficence toward creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r1.anchor: أي: لا يكلف أحدا فوق طاقته،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this the abrogating verse that lifts the Companions’ fear about 2:284’s accountability for hidden thoughts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r2.anchor: وهذه هي الناسخة الرافعة لما كان أشفق منه الصحابة، في قوله: {وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r3.claim: God may reckon and question, but punishes only what a person can repel; involuntary inner whispers are not charged, and aversion to evil whispers is faith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r3.anchor: أي: هو وإن حاسب وسأل لكن لا يعذب إلا بما يملك (2) الشخص دفعه، فأما ما لا يمكن دفعه من وسوسة النفس وحديثها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r4.claim: What a person earns is good and what is charged against them is evil, in deeds that fall within moral obligation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r4.anchor: {لها ما كسبت} أي: من خير، {وعليها ما اكتسبت} أي: من شر، وذلك في الأعمال التي تدخل تحت التكليف،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r5.claim: God teaches His servants to ask Him and has undertaken to answer; forgetting means omitting a duty or doing a forbidden act forgetfully, while error is missing the legally correct action through ignorance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r5.anchor: ثم قال (3) تعالى مرشدا عباده إلى سؤاله، وقد تكفل لهم بالإجابة، كما أرشدهم وعلمهم أن يقولوا:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r6.claim: Forgetfulness can mean leaving an obligation or committing a prohibition unintentionally; error means missing the sound legal form out of ignorance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r6.anchor: أي: إن تركنا فرضا على جهة النسيان، أو فعلنا حراما كذلك، {أو أخطأنا} أي: الصواب في العمل، جهلا منا بوجهه الشرعي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r7.claim: In a report cited from Sahih Muslim, the Prophet says God answered this plea, Yes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r7.anchor: وقد تقدم في صحيح مسلم لحديث أبي هريرة: "قال الله: نعم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r8.claim: In the report from Ibn Abbas cited here, God answers, I have done so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r8.anchor: ولحديث (5) ابن عباس قال الله: "قد فعلت".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r9.claim: A Prophetic report transmitted through Ibn Abbas says God lifted mistake, forgetfulness, and coercion from the community; Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban narrate it, but Ahmad and Abu Hatim faulted it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله وضع (7) عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان، وما استكرهوا عليه".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r10.speaker: أم الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r10.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Umm al-Darda that the Prophet said God overlooks three for his community: error, forgetfulness, and coercion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r10.anchor: عن أم الدرداء، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الله تجاوز لأمتي عن ثلاث: عن الخطأ، والنسيان، والاستكراه"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r11.claim: After Abu Bakr al-Hudhali mentioned the report to Hasan, Hasan agreed and cited this Qur’anic plea as its basis.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p737/r11.anchor: قال أبو بكر: فذكرت ذلك للحسن، فقال: أجل، أما تقرأ بذلك قرآنا: {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r1.claim: The plea asks not to be burdened with arduous duties, even if bearable, like the shackles imposed on earlier peoples; Muhammad’s merciful law removes such burdens through its easy, tolerant religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r1.anchor: أي: لا تكلفنا من الأعمال الشاقة وإن أطقناها، كما شرعته للأمم الماضية قبلنا من الأغلال والآصار التي كانت عليهم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r2.claim: In a report from Sahih Muslim, the Prophet says God answered this plea, Yes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r2.anchor: وقد ثبت في صحيح مسلم، عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "قال الله: نعم".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the answer to this plea as God saying, I have done so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "قال الله: قد فعلت".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r4.claim: A Prophetic report says he was sent with the upright, easy religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r4.anchor: وجاء الحديث من طرق، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "بعثت بالحنيفية السمحة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r5.claim: The plea covers unbearable obligations, calamities, and trials: believers ask not to be tested with what they cannot bear.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r5.anchor: أي: من التكليف والمصائب والبلاء، لا تبتلينا بما لا قبل لنا به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r6.speaker: مكحول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r6.claim: Makḥul glosses the unbearable burden as estrangement and intense sexual desire; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits the gloss, followed by the divine answer, Yes, or in another report, I have done so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738/r6.anchor: وقد قال مكحول في قوله: {ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} قال: الغربة والغلمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r1.claim: Pardon concerns shortcomings between the servant and God; forgiveness concerns failings toward other people, whom God is asked not to expose to the servant’s ugly deeds; mercy asks protection from future sin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {واعف عنا} أي: فيما بيننا وبينك مما تعلمه من تقصيرنا وزللنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r2.claim: A sinner needs God to pardon him, conceal his faults from people, and preserve him from falling into the same kind of sin again.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r2.anchor: أن يعفو الله عنه فيما بينه وبينه، وأن يستره عن عباده فلا يفضحه به بينهم، وأن يعصمه فلا يوقعه في نظيره.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r3.claim: The earlier transmitted answer to these pleas is that God said Yes; another report has Him say, I have done so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r3.anchor: وقد تقدم في الحديث أن الله قال: نعم. وفي الحديث الآخر: "قال الله: قد فعلت".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r4.claim: Mawlana means our protector and helper; believers trust and rely on God, with no power or strength except through Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r4.anchor: أي: أنت ولينا وناصرنا، وعليك توكلنا، وأنت المستعان، وعليك التكلان، ولا حول ولا قوة لنا إلا بك (3)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r5.claim: The disbelievers reject God’s religion, oneness, and Messenger, worship others, and associate created beings with God; the plea asks victory and the final outcome over them in this world and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r5.anchor: أي: الذين جحدوا دينك، وأنكروا وحدانيتك، ورسالة نبيك، وعبدوا غيرك، وأشركوا معك من عبادك، فانصرنا عليهم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r6.claim: The answer is again reported as God saying Yes, or as in Muslim’s report from Ibn Abbas, I have done so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r6.anchor: قال الله: نعم. وفي الحديث الذي رواه مسلم، عن ابن عباس: "قال الله: قد فعلت".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r7.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jarir reports that Muadh said Amin when finishing the sura; Waki reports a route through an unnamed man from Muadh saying he said Amin on completing al-Baqara.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p738#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن جرير: حدثني المثنى بن إبراهيم، حدثنا أبو نعيم، حدثنا سفيان، عن أبي إسحاق، أن معاذا، رضي الله عنه، كان إذا فرغ من هذه السورة

JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r1.speaker: القراء
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r1.claim: All readers agree on the noun reading with ḍamma on wāw and sukūn on sīn.
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r1.anchor: أجمعت القراء على (وسعها) بضم الواو وسكون السين

JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r2.speaker: إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r2.claim: Ibrahim ibn Abi ʿAbla reads the word with fatḥa on wāw and kasra on sīn as a verb; the common reading is a verbal noun.
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة: وسعها بفتح الواو وكسر السين على الفعل، يعني لا تكلف نفسا إلا وسعها أمره، والأول على المصدر

JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r3.claim: Akhaṭaʾa can refer to sin or something other than sin, while khaṭiʾa is used only for sin.
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r3.anchor: يقال: أخطأ في الإثم وغير الإثم، وخطئ في الإثم لا غير

JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r4.claim: Isr can mean a heavy burden or a binding covenant.

JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r7.claim: Hasan supplies an omitted imperative: “and say, Our Lord.”
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r7.anchor: في قوله: ربنا محذوف، واختلفوا فيه، فقيل: تقديره: وقولوا ربنا، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, the prayer is quoted speech—“they say, Our Lord”—with rabbana as a vocative meaning “O our Lord.”
JISHUMI:v2p1088#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: تقديره على الحكاية، أي: يقولون ربنا، و(ربنا) منصوب على النداء، وتقديره: يا ربنا

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r1.claim: God has not imposed commands and prohibitions beyond people’s capacity, removing their excuse.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r1.anchor: ثم بين تعالى أنه فيما أمر ونهى لم يكلفهم إلا ما وسعهم، وأنه أزاح علتهم

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r2.claim: The statement may continue the believers’ speech: “We hear and obey; You have burdened us only with what we can bear”; the following prayer is part of their quoted words.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r2.anchor: قيل: يحتمل أنه من كلام الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والمؤمنين عطفا على ما تقدم، وحكاية عنهم، وتقديره: قالوا سمعنا وأطعنا، فإنك ما كلفتنا إلا ما في وسعنا

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r3.claim: Alternatively, it begins a new divine statement to the Messenger and believers, clarifying that earlier commands and prohibitions did not exceed capacity.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ابتداء خبر من الله تعالى لرسوله والمؤمنين حيث تقدم من الأوامر والنواهي ما تقدم، فبين أنه لم يكلف إلا ما في الوسع، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r4.claim: Here taklīf means commanding or prohibiting a soul only to the extent it can perform; the easy is what is not hard.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r4.anchor: والمعنى: لا يكلف أي لا يأمر ولا ينهى نفسا إلا وسعهما إلا ما هم به مستطيعون، واليسير: السهل دون العسير

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r5.claim: Each soul receives the reward for what it has earned through good and righteous deeds.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r5.anchor: لها ما كسبت أي لكل نفس جزاء ما كسبت، أي لكل نفس جزاء ما عملت من الخير والعمل الصالح

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r6.claim: Each soul bears the burden for the sins it has committed.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r6.anchor: (وعليها ما اكتسبت) يعني وزر ما عملت من المعاصي

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r7.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r7.claim: Al-Asamm reads “if we forget” as ordinary absent-minded forgetfulness; the author rejects this because accidental forgetfulness is not charged or punishable.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r7.anchor: قيل: هو النسيان الذي هو السهو، عن الأصم، وهذا لا يصح؛ لأنه لا يكلفهم مع السهو، ولا يجوز أن يؤاخذ به

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r8.claim: Another reading of “we forgot” is that people abandoned something because of doubt or bad interpretation, like the verse saying they forgot God and He forgot them.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r8.anchor: وقيل: (نسينا) تركنا لشبهة أو سوء تأويل كقوله: (نسوا الله فنسيهم)

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r9.claim: The phrase may also ask God not to hold them accountable if they are exposed to forgetfulness.

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r10.claim: “Or we err” may mean committing a sin because of an ambiguity.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r10.anchor: أو أخطأنا أي عملنا خطيئة بشبهة

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r11.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r11.claim: Al-Asamm takes error to mean an unintentional act.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r11.anchor: وقيل: إن أخطأنا: فعلنا من غير عمد، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r12.claim: The author rejects the claim that this prayer is invalid because unintentional error is excused: it remains proper to pray even for what is already waived.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r12.anchor: ويصح أن يدعو وإن وضع عنه

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r13.speaker: عطاء
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r13.claim: ʿAta interprets the prayer as asking not to be held to account for ignorance or deliberate action.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r13.anchor: وقيل: (إن نسينا أو أخطأنا) إن جهلنا أو تعمدنا، عن عطاء

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك والربيع والسدي
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r14.claim: They interpret isr as a covenant too difficult to fulfill.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r14.anchor: ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا قيل: عهدا نعجز عن القيام به، عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك والربيع والسدي

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r15.speaker: عطاء وعمر ومالك
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r15.claim: An alternative takes isr as a heavy burden, asking that commands not be made too strict.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r15.anchor: وقيل: ثقلا يعني لا تشدد الأمر علينا، عن عطاء وعمر ومالك

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r16.claim: The earlier people are the Jews, who faced severe obligations.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r16.anchor: كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا من الشدائد يعني اليهود

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r17.speaker: قتادة والضحاك والسدي وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r17.claim: They interpret this as burdensome commands, such as the Israelites’ order to kill themselves; “I cannot bear speaking to him” means the speech is burdensome.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r17.anchor: قيل: ما يثقل علينا مثل ما كلف بنو إسرائيل أن يقتلوا أنفسهم، كقولهم: ما أطيق كلام فلان، أي يثقل عن قتادة والضحاك والسدي وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r18.claim: Another interpretation asks not to be burdened with punishment beyond our strength.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r18.anchor: وقيل: ما لا طاقة لنا به من العذاب

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r19.claim: One interpretation asks God to erase sins and cover them.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r19.anchor: واعف عنا واغفر لنا قيل: اعف عن ذنوبنا واغفر لنا استرها

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r20.claim: Another interpretation distinguishes pardon for minor sins from forgiveness of major ones.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r20.anchor: وقيل: اعف عن الصغائر، واغفر لنا الكبائر

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r21.claim: God’s mercy is provision in this world and Paradise in the next.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r21.anchor: وارحمنا في الدنيا بالرزق، وفي إلآخرة بالجنة

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r22.claim: Mawlā here means our guardian and protector, the one with greatest claim over us.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r22.anchor: أنت مولانا أي أنت ولينا وحافظنا وأولى بنا

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r23.claim: One view asks for help against disbelievers through subjugation.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r23.anchor: فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين أي أعنا عليهم قيل: بالقهر

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r24.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r24.claim: Another view understands the requested help as argument and victory.

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r25.speaker: معاذ
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r25.claim: Muʿadh is reported to say “Amen” when he finishes reciting the end of Surat al-Baqara.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r25.anchor: وعن معاذ أنه كان إذا ختم سورة البقرة قال: آمين

JISHUMI:v2p1089/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r26.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r26.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that the closing verses of al-Baqara are Qur’an and supplication, and please the Merciful; no grading is stated.
JISHUMI:v2p1089/r26.anchor: وعن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: في آخر سورة البقرة آيات إنهن قرآن وإنهن دعاء وإنهن يرضين الرحمن

JISHUMI:v2p1090/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r1.claim: The request not to be held accountable refutes determinism about human acts, since the request presupposes that people act.
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r1.anchor: تدل الآية على بطلان مذهب الجبر في المخلوق؛ لأن قوله: لا تؤاخذنا لا يصح إلا ولهم فعل

JISHUMI:v2p1090/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r2.claim: The statement that God burdens a soul only within its capacity refutes the determinists’ account of ability.
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r2.anchor: وتدل على بطلان قولهم في الاستطاعة بقوله: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها

JISHUMI:v2p1090/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r3.claim: The account of the believers’ faith in this prayer establishes the duty to follow the believers’ example.
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r3.anchor: ويدل على وجوب الاقتداء بالمؤمنين فيما حكى عنهم من الإيمان

JISHUMI:v2p1090/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r4.claim: Their request for help against disbelievers likewise shows that they have agency.
JISHUMI:v2p1090/r4.anchor: ويدل قوله: فانصرنا على أن لهم فعلا؛ لذلك سألوا النصرة

TIRMIDHI:2992/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:2992/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TIRMIDHI:2992/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the revelation in 2:284 distressed the believers; the Prophet told them to answer that they heard and obeyed, God placed faith in their hearts, and revelation then came down through 2:286.
TIRMIDHI:2992/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال لما نزلت هذه الآية

TIRMIDHI:2992/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:2992/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
TIRMIDHI:2992/r2.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās’s report, God answers the requests not to punish forgetfulness or error, impose the former peoples’ burden, or demand the unbearable, and to pardon, forgive, and show mercy, with “I have done so.”
TIRMIDHI:2992/r2.anchor: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلاَّ وُسْعَهَا

TIRMIDHI:2992/r3.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:2992/r3.speaker: أبو عيسى
TIRMIDHI:2992/r3.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report hasan and notes another route from Ibn ʿAbbās, as well as a related report from Abū Hurayra.
TIRMIDHI:2992/r3.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث حسن وقد روي هذا من غير هذا الوجه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r1.claim: Wusʿ is what a person can bear without strain or distress; God assigns only what fits capacity and is manageable, below the limit of exertion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r1.anchor: الوسع ما يسع الانسان ولا يضيق عليه ولا يحرج فيه أي لا يكلفها الا ما يتسع فيه طوقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r2.claim: This declares God’s justice and mercy; people could physically pray more than five times, fast longer than a month, or perform pilgrimage more than once.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r3.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r3.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAblah reads the word with fatḥa on the wāw.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ( وسعها ) بالفتح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r4.claim: Good deeds benefit the soul and evil deeds harm it; no one bears another’s sin or receives reward for another’s obedience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r4.anchor: ينفعها ما كسبت من خير ويضرها ما اكتسبت من شر لا يؤاخذ بذنبها غيرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r5.claim: The intensified form for evil signals effort: the soul desires and is drawn toward evil, so works harder to acquire it; good uses the unmarked form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r5.anchor: في الاكتساب اعتمال فلما كان الشر مما تشتهيه النفس وهي منجذبة اليه وامارة به كانت في تحصيله اعمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r6.claim: The prayer asks that they not be taken to task for forgetfulness or error if either occurs through them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r6.anchor: أي لا تؤاخذنا بالنسيان أو الخطأ ان فرط منا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r7.claim: Although forgetfulness and error are excused, they are named to mean the negligence and inattention that can cause them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359/r7.anchor: ذكر النسيان والخطأ والمراد بهما ما هما مسببان عنه من التفريط والاغفال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r1.claim: The passage about Moses’ companion says Satan caused him to forget; Satan cannot directly cause forgetting but whispers, leading to the negligence that causes it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r1.anchor: والشيطان لا يقدر على فعل النسيان وإنما يوسوس فتكون وسوسته سببا للتفريط

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r2.claim: Because the God-fearing only lapse through forgetfulness or error, naming these in prayer disavows culpable causes and acknowledges their protection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r2.anchor: فما كانت تفرط منهم فرطة الا على وجه النسيان والخطأ فكان وصفهم بالدعاء بذلك ايذانا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r3.claim: A person may pray for continued preservation of a blessing already received, both to sustain it and acknowledge it as a blessing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز ان يدعو الانسان بما علم أنه حاصل له قبل الدعاء من فضل الله لاستدامته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r4.claim: Iṣr is a heavy load that pins its bearer in place; metaphorically it means onerous obligations such as killing oneself or cutting away contaminated skin or clothing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r4.anchor: والإصر العبء الذي يأصر حامله أي يحبسه مكانه لا يستقل به لثقله استعير للتكليف الشاق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r5.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r5.claim: The word is also read in the plural, “āṣāran”; Ubayy’s reading adds a shadda to “do not place.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p359#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء ( آصارا ) على الجمع وفي قراءة أبي ( ولا تحمل ) علينا بالتشديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r1.claim: The shadda in this phrase intensifies the act of imposing a burden; the other form changes the verb from one object to two.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r1.anchor: قلت هذه للمبالغة في حمل عليه وتلك لنقل حمله من مفعول واحد إلى مفعولين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r2.claim: The prayer asks to be spared punishments imposed on earlier peoples, then punishment for failing to preserve difficult duties imposed on them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r2.anchor: من العقوبات النازلة بمن قبلنا طلبوا الإعفاء عن التكليفات الشاقة التى كلفها من قبلهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means duties so difficult they can scarcely be performed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد به الشاق الذي لا يكاد يستطاع من التكاليف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r4.claim: The second request repeats the first in meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r4.anchor: وهذا تكرير لقوله ) ﴿ ولا تحمل علينا إصرا ﴾

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r5.claim: “Our mawlā” may mean our master, since we are His servants; our helper; or the one who manages our affairs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r5.anchor: سيدنا ونحن عبيدك أو ناصرنا أو متولي امورنا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r6.claim: They ask for victory because a master should aid his servants, because this is God’s customary way, or because managing their affairs is His concern.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r6.anchor: فمن حق المولى ان ينصر عبيده أو فإن ذلك عادتك أو فإن ذلك من امورنا التي عليك توليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet recited these supplications, he was told after each one, “It has been done.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r7.anchor:
وعن ابن عباس
155 ( أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دعا بهذه الدعوات قيل له عند كل كلمة قد فعلت )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r8.claim: The Prophet said that reciting al-Baqara’s final two verses at night suffices the reciter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r8.anchor:
وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام
156 ( من قرأ الآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة في ليلة كفتاه )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r9.claim: The Prophet said he was given al-Baqara’s closing verses from a treasure beneath the Throne, a gift no prior prophet received.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r9.anchor:
وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام
157 ( أوتيت خواتيم سورة البقرة من كنز تحت العرش لم يؤتهن نبي قبلي )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r10.claim: A report says two verses from Paradise’s treasures were written by the Merciful before creation two thousand years earlier; reciting them after the night prayer suffices instead of night vigil.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r10.anchor:
وعنه عليه السلام
158 ( أنزل الله آيتين من كنوز الجنة كتبهما الرحمن بيده قبل ان يخلق الخلق بألفي سنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r11.claim: It is acceptable to say “I read al-Baqara” as shorthand for the surah; prophetic reports and Companion usage attest this, like naming other surahs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r11.anchor: فإن قلت هل يجوز ان يقال قرأت سورة البقرة أو قرأت البقرة قلت لا بأس بذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r12.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r12.claim: Ali says al-Baqara’s closing verses are a treasure beneath the Throne.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r12.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه ( خواتيم سورة البقرة من كنز تحت العرش )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r13.claim: Ibn Masʿud swore at the stoning site that this was the stoning of the person to whom al-Baqara was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r13.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنهما انه رمى الجمرة ثم قال ( من ههنا والذي لا اله غيره رمي الذي انزلت عليه سورة البقرة )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r14.claim: Saying “I read al-Baqara” plainly means the surah, just as one says “the surah of al-Zukhruf,” al-Mumtahana, or al-Mujadila.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p360/r14.anchor: واذا قيل قرأت البقرة لم يشكل ان المراد سورة البقرة كقوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p361/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p361/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p361/r1.claim: An unnamed authority disliked one way of referring to the sūra and said one should call it the sūra in which al-Baqara is mentioned.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p361/r1.anchor: وعن بعضهم انه كره ذلك وقال يقال قرأت السورة التي تذكر فيه البقرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p361/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p361/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p361/r2.claim: The Prophet calls al-Baqara the Qurʾān’s fustāṭ, urges learning it for its blessing, warns that neglect is regret, and says sorcerers cannot master it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p361/r2.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم 159 ( السورة التي تذكر فيها البقرة فسطاط القرآن فتعلموها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Companions feared accountability for inner thoughts, after which the capacity verse was revealed; Ibn Masud also held this abrogation view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r2.anchor: عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة قال : انزل الله { وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Companions were told to hear, obey, and submit after 2:284; when they did, faith entered their hearts and the final verses' petitions followed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم } دخل قلوبهم منها شيء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r19.claim: The clause is read either as God's promise of gracious treatment or as the Prophet and believers praising God for not overburdening anyone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r19.anchor: وفيه وجهان : أحدهما : وعد من الله ورسوله وللمؤمنين بالتفصل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r20.claim: What a person earns is good deeds, while what is against them is sins.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r21.claim: The forms may differ only in wording while sharing a meaning, or kasabat may be reserved for good and iktasabat for evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r21.anchor: وفي كسبت واكتسبت وجهان : أحدهما : أن لفظهما مختلف ومعناهما واحد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r22.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r22.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse instructs believers to say this prayer to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r22.anchor: قال الحسن : معناه : قولوا ربنا لا تؤاخذنا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r23.claim: Nasiya can mean deliberately neglecting God's command or simply leaving it; Qutrub cites 'they forgot God, so He forgot them' for the latter sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r23.anchor: والنسيان : بمعنى الترك كقوله تعالى : ^ ( نسوا الله فنسيهم ) ^ [ التوبة : 67 ]

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r24.claim: Mistakes may mean sins interpreted under ambiguities or sins deliberately committed despite being wrong.
