MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r24.anchor: فيه تأويلان : أحدهما : ما تأولوه من المعاصي بالشبهات . والثاني : ما عمدوه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r25.claim: Linguists distinguish akhta'a, which can apply to sinful or non-sinful error, from khati'a, which always entails sin; a cited verse of poetry illustrates the distinction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p361/r25.anchor: فقالوا : ' أخطأ ' يكون على جهة الإثم وغير الإثم ، وخطىء : لا يكون إلا على جهة الإثم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada interpret the burden as a covenant too difficult to fulfill.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r1.anchor: أحدها : إصرا أي عهدا نعجز عن القيام به ، قاله ابن عباس ، ومجاهد ، وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r2.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r2.claim: Ata interprets the burden as being transformed into apes and swine.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r2.anchor: الثاني : أي لا تمسخنا قردة وخنازير ، وهذا قول عطاء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the burden to mean a sin for which there is neither repentance nor expiation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنه الذنب الذي ليس فيه توبة ولا كفارة ، قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r4.speaker: مالك، الربيع، النابغة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r4.claim: Malik and al-Rabi interpret isr as a great burden; al-Nabigha's poetry supports the sense of carrying a burden for others.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r4.anchor: قال النابغة : يا مانع الضيم أن يغشى سراتهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r5.claim: The people before them are the Israelites, who were charged with killing themselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r5.anchor: يعني بني إسرائيل فيما حملوه من قتل أنفسهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r6.claim: One view takes the unbearable burden as obligations imposed on the Israelites.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r6.anchor: أحدهما : ما لا طاقة لنا به مما كلفه بنو إسرائيل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r7.claim: The other view understands the unbearable burden as punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r7.anchor: الثاني : ما لا طاقة لنا به من العذاب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r8.claim: Mawlana means either our master and owner or our protector and helper.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that as the Prophet recited the successive petitions, God answered that He had forgiven, excused, shown mercy, and granted victory in response to each.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r10.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r10.claim: Uqba ibn Amir al-Juhani reports that the Prophet urged recitation of the final two verses of al-Baqara, which God gave him from beneath the Throne.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r10.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ' اقرؤوا هاتين الآيتين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r11.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r11.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports the Prophet calling al-Baqara a pavilion of the Qur'an and urging its study: learning it is blessed, abandoning it regrettable, and sorcerers cannot withstand it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p364/r11.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : السورة التي تذكر فيها البقرة فسطاطا القرآن

MUQATIL:2:286/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:286/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:286/r1.claim: God requires a person to do only what that person is capable of doing.
MUQATIL:2:286/r1.anchor: يقول: لا يكلفها من العمل إلا ما أطاقت

MUQATIL:2:286/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:286/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:286/r2.claim: A person receives the good they earn and bears the sin they commit.
MUQATIL:2:286/r2.anchor: من الخير وما عملت أو تظلمت به

MUQATIL:2:286/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:286/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:286/r3.claim: Gabriel taught Muhammad this plea: do not punish us for ignorance or error that made us leave God’s command; God answered, “That is granted to you.”
MUQATIL:2:286/r3.anchor: يقول: إن جهلنا عن شىء أو أخطأنا، فتركنا أمرك

MUQATIL:2:286/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:286/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:286/r4.claim: Iṣr means a covenant; the plea asks not to burden this community as God burdened Israel, forbidding camel meat, sheep fat, and all cloven-hoofed animals because of their sins, and making them apes and pigs.
MUQATIL:2:286/r4.anchor: ما كان حرم عليهم من لحوم الإبل، وشحوم الغنم، ولحوم كل ذى ظفر

MUQATIL:2:286/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:286/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:286/r5.claim: “Pardon us” asks God to pardon, and “forgive us” asks Him to overlook all their sins.
MUQATIL:2:286/r5.anchor: يقول: واعف عنا من ذلك، { واغفر لنا } ، يقول: وتجاوز عنا

MUQATIL:2:286/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:286/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:286/r6.claim: God is their protector; they ask victory over disbelievers of Mecca and elsewhere until Resurrection. God grants the requests, intercedes for the community, and exempts it for error, forgetfulness, and coercion, a favor withheld from earlier nations.
MUQATIL:2:286/r6.anchor: يعنى كفار مكة وغيرها إلى يوم القيامة، قال الله تعالى: ذلك لك

BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r1.claim: The opening clause is God's own statement, not part of the believers' prayer.
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r1.anchor: إخبار من الله تعالى وليس من كلام المؤمنين

BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r2.claim: After 2:284 alarmed the Companions, they knelt before the Prophet, fearing they could not bear accounting for inner thoughts. He warned against answering like earlier scriptural communities; they affirmed obedience and sought forgiveness. After 2:285 was revealed, 2:286 eased the burden: the account concerns deliberate resolve to do evil, not unavoidable passing thoughts.
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r2.anchor: روي أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r3.claim: Taklīf imposes a burden; wusʿ is what a person can accommodate without hardship. God, through favor and mercy to this community, assigns only what fits their capacity, as in 2:185.
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r3.anchor: والوسع ما يسع الإنسان ولا يضيق عليه

BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r4.claim: This shows that God has not actually imposed an impossible burden, not that such imposition is intrinsically impossible: its occurrence would make God's statement false, while an unrestricted negation does not establish impossibility.
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r4.anchor: وهذا يدل على عدم وقوع التكليف بالمحال لا على امتناعه

BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r5.claim: The soul alone receives the reward for all the good it has earned and bears the punishment for all the evil it has acquired; no one else independently shares either account.
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r5.anchor: من الخير الذي كلفت فعله لا لغيرها استقلالا أو اشتراكا

BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r6.claim: The verse uses the more effortful form اكتسبت for evil because the desired act involves striving, unlike good; the iftiʿāl form conveys exertion.
BURSEVI:v1p365#2/r6.anchor: وإيراد الاكتساب في جانب الشر لأن الشر فيه اعتمال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r1.claim: The opening statement may be reported as part of the preceding prayer or begin a new sentence.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r1.anchor: ﴿ لا يكلف الله نفسا ﴾ محكى عنهم أو مستأنف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r2.speaker: شرح التأويلات
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r2.claim: Obligation is limited to acts a person can perform, since responsibility concerns deeds within one’s ability.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r2.anchor: إلا طاقتها وقدرتها لأن التكليف لا يرد إلا بفعل يقدر عليه المكلف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r3.claim: Capacity is what one can bear without constraint or embarrassment, short of the utmost exertion; people could pray, fast, or make pilgrimage more than required.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r3.anchor: الوسع ما يسع الإنسان ولا يضيق عليه ولا يحرج فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r4.claim: Good is called kasb and evil iktisab because the iftiʿāl form suggests recoil: the soul recoils from evil and exerts itself for good.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r4.anchor: وخص الخير بالكسب والشر بالاكتساب لأن الافتعال للانكماش

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r5.claim: The prayer implies that God could hold people accountable for forgetfulness or error, contrary to the Muʿtazila, since these can be avoided in some measure; otherwise the request is pointless.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r5.anchor: ودل هذا على جواز المؤاخذة فى النسيان والخطأ خلافا للمعتزلة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r6.claim: Isr is a heavy load that pins its bearer in place; metaphorically it denotes hard obligations such as killing oneself or cutting impurity from skin or clothing.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r6.anchor: عبأ يأصر حامله أى يحبسه مكانه لثقله استعير للتكليف الشاق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r7.claim: The people burdened with such earlier obligations are the Jews.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r7.anchor: استعير للتكليف الشاق من نحو قتل الأنفس وقطع موضع النجاسة من الجلد والثوب وغير ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r8.claim: This request concerns protection from punishments that befell earlier peoples.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r9.claim: The requests are not redundant: pardon erases major sins, while forgiveness covers minor sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r9.anchor: وليس بتكرار فالأول للكبائر والثاني للصغائر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r10.claim: An alternative gloss assigns pardon, forgiveness, and mercy protection respectively from metamorphosis, being swallowed by the earth, and drowning.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r10.anchor: الأول من المسخ والثاني من الخسف والثالث من الغرق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r11.claim: Mercy may mean making the scales of our deeds heavy despite our having no good deeds to offer.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r12.claim: Mawlā can mean our master, helper, or the one who manages our affairs.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r12.anchor: سيدنا ونحن عبيدك أو ناصرنا أو متولى أمورنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r13.claim: The request for victory follows because a master is expected to aid his servants.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r13.anchor: فمن حق المولى أن ينصر عبيده فى الحديث

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r14.claim: A report says reciting the closing verses beginning «Āmana al-rasūl» at night suffices the reciter.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r14.anchor: من قرأ آمن الرسول إلى آخره فى ليلة كفتاه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r15.claim: Another report says reciting those two verses after the final night prayer substitutes for night vigil.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r15.anchor: من قرأهما بعد العشاء الآخرة أجزأتاه عن قيام الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r16.speaker: على
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r16.claim: ʿAlī is cited as saying that the closing verses of al-Baqara are a treasure from beneath the Throne.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r16.anchor: لما روى عن على رضى الله عنه خواتيم سورة البقرة من كنز تحت العرش

NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r17.claim: Some disapproved of saying «I read al-Baqara» and preferred «I read the sūra in which al-Baqara is mentioned».
NASAFI-FULL:v1p140/r17.anchor: وقال بعضهم يكره ذلك بل يقال قرأت السورة التى تذكر فيها البقرة

BURSEVI:v1p366/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p366/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p366/r1.claim: The plea seeks pardon for negligence and carelessness that lead to forgetfulness or error, since such causes fall within human responsibility.
BURSEVI:v1p366/r1.anchor: بما صدر عنا من الأمور المؤدية إلى النسيان أو الخطأ من تفريط وقلة مبالاة

BURSEVI:v1p366/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p366/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p366/r2.claim: The request implies that accountability for forgetfulness and error is possible because avoiding them is possible in some measure; otherwise the prayer would be meaningless.
BURSEVI:v1p366/r2.anchor: فإن التحرز عنهما في الجملة ممكن ولولا جواز المؤاخذة في النسيان والخطأ لم يكن للسؤال معنى

BURSEVI:v1p366/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p366/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p366/r3.claim: The Prophet says this community is exempted from liability for error, forgetfulness, and coercion; earlier communities were liable for the first two.
BURSEVI:v1p366/r3.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه"

BURSEVI:v1p366/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p366/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p366/r4.claim: Iṣr denotes a heavy load that pins its bearer in place, and here means burdensome religious duties.
BURSEVI:v1p366/r4.anchor: والإصر العبء الثقيل الذي يأصر صاحبه أي : يحبسه مكانه

BURSEVI:v1p366/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p366/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p366/r5.claim: Israelites faced severe duties: self-killing in repentance, cutting mistaken limbs and impurity, fifty daily prayers, mosque-only prayer, fasting restrictions, forbidden good things, quarter-wealth alms, and written records of nightly sins.
BURSEVI:v1p366/r5.anchor: وهو ما كلفه بنو إسرائيل من قتل النفس في توبة وقطع الأعضاء الخاطئة وقطع موضع النجاسة

BURSEVI:v1p366/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p366/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p366/r6.claim: God spared this community comparable strictures and earlier peoples' punishments; the Prophet describes his mission as the easy, tolerant upright way and says his community is spared sinking, metamorphosis, and drowning.
BURSEVI:v1p366/r6.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم "بعثت بالحنيفة السهلة السمحة"

BURSEVI:v1p366/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p366/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p366/r7.claim: This asks deliverance from unbearable punishments, after asking to avoid the onerous duties whose neglect could bring them; punishment is described as a load because those duties lead to it.
BURSEVI:v1p366/r7.anchor: واستعفاء من العقوبات التي لا تطاق بعد الاستعفاء مما يؤدي إليها من التكاليف الشاقة

BURSEVI:v1p367/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r1.speaker: التيسير
BURSEVI:v1p367/r1.claim: The request means not to impose duties that are difficult to sustain continually; it does not ask for the literally impossible, which cannot occur.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r1.anchor: قال في "التيسير" أي : لا تكلفنا ما يشق علينا الدوام عليه

BURSEVI:v1p367/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p367/r2.claim: Pardon means removing the traces of sins; forgiveness means concealing faults so the believer is not exposed before people.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r2.anchor: أي : آثار ذنوبنا {واغفر لنا} واستر عيوبنا ولا تفضحنا

BURSEVI:v1p367/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r3.speaker: التيسير
BURSEVI:v1p367/r3.claim: The two requests are not repetitive: pardon leaves the person unpunished and erases the sin, while forgiveness hides it from view; one may pardon while still mentioning and exposing a deed.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r3.anchor: قال في "التيسير" وليس بتكرار. فإن الأول تركه حتى لا يؤاخذ به

BURSEVI:v1p367/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p367/r4.claim: Believers ask both that God overlook their sins and conceal them, so their state is not publicly exposed.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r4.anchor: والمؤمنون أمروا أن يسألوا التجاوز عنها وإخفاءها حتى لا يظهر حالهم لأحد

BURSEVI:v1p367/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p367/r5.claim: Pardon and forgiveness precede the request for mercy because clearing away faults comes before adorning the servant with favor.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r5.anchor: لما أن التخلية سابقة على التحلية

BURSEVI:v1p367/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p367/r6.claim: Mawlānā can mean our master while we are His servants, our helper, or the one who manages our affairs.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r6.anchor: سيدنا ونحن عبيدك أو ناصرنا أو متولي أمورنا

BURSEVI:v1p367/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p367/r7.claim: The plea asks God to help against disbelievers and repel their harm, as a guardian should defend those in his care; victory may come through conquest, argument, or defense.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r7.anchor: أي : أعنا عليهم وادفع عنا شرهم فإن من حق المولى أن ينصر عبيده

BURSEVI:v1p367/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p367/r8.claim: The request for victory also seeks protection from devils, since they belong among the disbelieving enemies.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r8.anchor: والنصرة على الكفار تكون بالظفر وتكون بالحجة وتكون بالدفع

BURSEVI:v1p367/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p367/r9.claim: In the Miʿrāj report, at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary in the sixth heaven, the Prophet received the five prayers, the closing verses of al-Baqara, and forgiveness for any follower who avoids associating partners with God.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r9.anchor: فأعطى رسول الله عليه السلام ثلاثا أعطى الصلوات الخمس وأعطى خواتيم سورة البقرة

BURSEVI:v1p367/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p367/r10.claim: During the Miʿrāj, the Prophet recited the believers' response to 2:285 and then asked the petitions of this verse; God answered that error, forgetfulness, and coercion were lifted and granted the remaining requests.
BURSEVI:v1p367/r10.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في خبر المعراج : "قربني الله وأدناني إلى سند العرش

BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r1.claim: A report says two verses from Paradise's treasures were written by the Merciful's hand two thousand years before creation, and reciting them after the final evening prayer suffices for night vigil.
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r1.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم "أنزل الله آيتين من كنوز الجنة

BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites the final two verses of al-Baqara will be sufficed, either for night prayer or for the reckoning on Judgment Day.
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r2.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم "من قرأ آيتين من آخر سورة البقرة كفتاه"

BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r3.claim: Bursevi uses the Prophet's designation of al-Baqara as the Quran's tent to refute disapproval of calling it Surat al-Baqara.
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r3.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "السورة التي تذكر فيها البقرة فسطاط القرآن"

BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r4.claim: The Prophet urges learning al-Baqara as a blessing, says abandoning it brings regret and sorcerers cannot master it, and the report links a house without its recitation for three nights with Satan's approach.
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r4.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "السحرة" أي : لا تستطيع البطلة أن تسحر قارئها

BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r5.speaker: معاذ
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r5.claim: Muʿādh used to say amen whenever he completed Surat al-Baqara.
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r5.anchor: وكان معاذ إذا ختم سورة البقرة يقول آمين

BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r6.speaker: أبو الأسلم الديلمي
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r6.claim: Al-Daylami reports Muʿādh's capture of a date-stealing jinn; the Prophet foretold its return, and on its second capture it claimed that reciting al-Baqara's ending keeps devils out of a house that night.
BURSEVI:v1p367#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي الأسلم الديلمي قلت لمعاذ بن جبل : أخبرني عن قصة الشيطان حين أخذته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r8.claim: Wusʿ means capacity, and may also mean less than one’s full capacity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r8.anchor: يعني طاقتها ويقال: إلا دون طاقتها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r9.claim: Good deeds accrue to a person and evil deeds count against them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r9.anchor: { لها ما كسبت } من الخير { وعليها ما اكتسبت } من الشر،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r10.speaker: جبريل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r10.claim: In the Miʿraj narrative, the Prophet asks pardon for forgetfulness or error; Gabriel says this has been granted and these are lifted from the community.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r10.anchor: فقال جبريل عند ذلك: سل تعطه، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: { ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r11.claim: The account glosses “if we forgot” as ignorance and “or erred” as deliberate action, while also offering the reading of acting through forgetfulness and error.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r11.anchor: يعني إن جهلنا { أو أخطأنا } يعني إن تعمدنا، ويقال: إن عملنا بالنسيان والخطأ.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r12.claim: The Miʿraj account glosses iṣr as a burden: earlier peoples had wholesome things forbidden for wrongdoing, sins written on their doors, and fifty prayers imposed before relief.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286/r12.anchor: يعني ثقلا { كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا } وهو أنه حرم عليهم الطيبات بظلمهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r1.claim: The request means not to burden people with work they cannot bear and thereby punish them, or with work they could do but could not sustain because of its hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r1.anchor: يقول: لا تثقلنا من العمل ما لا نطيق فتعذبنا، ويقال: ما تشق علينا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r2.claim: One gloss takes pardon, forgiveness, and mercy as protection from the past nations’ punishments of metamorphosis, sinking, and pelting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r2.anchor: ويقال: { واعف عنا } من المسخ { واغفر لنا } من الخسف { وارحمنا } من القذف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r3.claim: Mawlana means our protector and guardian.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r3.anchor: ثم قال: { أنت مولانا } يعني ولينا وحافظنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r4.claim: The prayer for victory was answered.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r4.anchor: { فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين } فاستجيبت دعوته.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r5.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r5.claim: The Prophet said he was granted victory through terror cast over enemies as far as a month’s journey.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r6.claim: A report says sincere raiders who leave home beating drums cast fear among unbelievers for a month, whether or not the enemy knows they have departed; the verses were revealed after the Prophet returned.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r6.anchor: ويقال إن الغزاة: إذا خرجوا من ديارهم بالنية الخالصة وضربوا بالطبل وقع الرعب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r9.claim: The account says 2:285 then praised the obedient believers, and God revealed 2:286 with “yes” affirmations to each request through the end of the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#2/r9.anchor: فلما فعلوا ذلك نسخها الله، فأنزل الله عز وجل: { لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#3/r1.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#3/r1.claim: Muslim transmits the answer to the prayer through Abu Hurayra; scholars say the report’s “I have done so” and “yes” show transmission by meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#3/r1.anchor: أخرجه مسلم عن أبي هريرة. قال علماؤنا: قوله في الرواية الأولى «قد فعلت» وهنا قال: «نعم»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r16.claim: Taklīf is an order that entails difficulty; Jawhari glosses takallaftu as undertaking a burdensome matter, and wusʿ as capacity or means.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r16.anchor: التكليف هو الأمر بما يشق عليه. وتكلفت الأمر تجشمته حكاه الجوهري. والوسع: الطاقة والجدة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r17.claim: This categorical statement says no bodily or inward act is imposed beyond a person’s capacity, understanding, and constitution, relieving the Muslims’ anxiety about thoughts.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r17.anchor: وهذا خبر جزم. نص الله تعالى على أنه لا يكلف العباد من وقت نزول الآية عبادة من أعمال القلب أو الجوارح إلا وهي في وسع المكلف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r18.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r18.claim: Abu Hurayra recalls following Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib while hungry; finding only a trace of clarified butter at home, Jaʿfar shared it with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#4/r18.anchor: وفي معنى هذه الآية ما حكاه أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: ما وددت أن أحدا ولدتني أمه إلا جعفر بن أبي طالب،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra’s quoted couplet says God burdens no soul beyond its capacity and a hand gives only what it has.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r1.anchor: ما كلف الله نفسا فوق طاقتها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري وجماعة من المتكلمين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r2.claim: Al-Ashari and a group of theologians hold that imposing the impossible is rationally possible, as a sign that the person will be punished, without compromising doctrine.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r2.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الأشعري وجماعة من المتكلمين: تكليف ما لا يطاق جائز عقلا،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r3.claim: The scholars agree that impossible obligations do not occur in revealed law, and this verse signals their absence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r3.anchor: بعد اتفاقهم على أنه ليس واقعا في الشرع، وأن هذه الآية آذنت بعدمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r4.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r4.claim: One group says the impossible occurred in Abu Lahab’s case: he was commanded to accept a whole law that included the prediction he would never believe.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r4.anchor: فقالت فرقة: وقع في نازلة أبي لهب، لأنه كلفه بالإيمان بجملة الشريعة،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r5.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r5.claim: Another group says impossible obligation never occurred; a consensus is reported on this position.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة: لم يقع قط. وقد حكى الإجماع على ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads “he shall burn” as conditional on Abu Lahab dying in the predicted state.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r6.anchor: سيصلى نارا [المسد: 3] معناه إن وافى حكاه ابن عطية.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r7.claim: Yukallifu takes two objects, with one omitted: the estimate is “an act of worship” or “something.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r7.anchor: «ويكلف» يتعدى إلى مفعولين أحدهما محذوف تقديره عبادة أو شيئا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r8.claim: Revelation includes weighty duties such as one facing ten and emigration, but God eased this community rather than imposing the painful burdens placed on earlier peoples.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r8.anchor: فالله سبحانه بلطفه وإنعامه علينا وإن كان قد كلفنا بما يشق ويثقل كثبوت الواحد للعشرة،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r9.speaker: السدي وجماعة المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r9.claim: Al-Suddi and, according to Ibn Atiyya, the exegetes agree that what a person earns for themselves is good deeds and what is against them is evil deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r9.anchor: يريد من الحسنات والسيئات. قاله السدي. وجماعة المفسرين لا خلاف بينهم في ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r10.claim: Passing thoughts and similar things are not a person’s acquired deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r10.anchor: والخواطر ونحوها ليست من كسب الإنسان.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r11.claim: Good is “for” a person as a joyful possession, while evil is “against” them as a heavy liability, like having property and owing debt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r11.anchor: وجاءت العبارة في الحسنات ب «لها» من حيث هي مما يفرح المرء بكسبه ويسر بها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r12.claim: The verb kasaba is repeated with different morphology to suit the pleasing pattern of the speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#5/r12.anchor: وكرر فعل الكسب فخالف بين التصريف حسنا لنمط الكلام كما قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says good deeds come without strain along God’s path, while evil requires forcefully breaching His prohibition; the two verb forms suit that distinction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويظهر لي في هذا أن الحسنات هي مما تكتسب دون تكلف، إذ كاسبها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r2.claim: The verse supports the scholars’ use of kasb and iktisab for human acts; the author rejects attributing creation to people as an innovating excess.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r2.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على صحة إطلاق أئمتنا على أفعال العباد كسبا واكتسابا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r3.claim: When the imams call a human an actor, that attribution is purely metaphorical.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r3.anchor: ومن أطلق من أئمتنا ذلك على العبد، وأنه فاعل فبالمجاز المحض.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r4.speaker: المهدوي وغيره وابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r4.claim: Al-Mahdawi and others offer the sense that no one is charged with another’s sin; Ibn Atiyya accepts the principle but says this verse is not its proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r4.anchor: وقال المهدوي وغيره: وقيل معنى الآية لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب أحد. قال ابن عطية: وهذا صحيح في نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r5.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r5.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari argues that killing by a heavy object, strangling, or drowning entails retaliation or blood money on the killer, not the killer’s kin; a father’s exemption does not free a co-killer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r5.anchor: قال الكيا الطبري: قوله تعالى: { لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت } يستدل به على أن من قتل غيره بمثقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the verse supports retaliation against a co-killer with a father, against Abu Hanifa, and against a co-killer with an accidental killer, against al-Shafiʿi and Abu Hanifa.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r6.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي: «ذكر علماؤنا هذه الآية في أن القود واجب على شريك الأب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r7.claim: The prayer asks that sin committed through forgetfulness or error be pardoned, as in the Prophetic report that these are lifted from the community.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r7.anchor: المعنى: أعف عن إثم ما يقع منا على هذين الوجهين أو أحدهما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r8.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r8.claim: The Prophet said that error, forgetfulness, and what people are coerced into have been lifted from his community; the author says this certainly lifts sin, while legal effects differ by case.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r8.anchor: كقوله عليه السلام: " رفع عن أمتى الخطأ والنسيان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r9.claim: Effects of error or forgetfulness vary: financial liabilities, blood money, and obligatory prayers remain; retaliation and an utterance of unbelief lapse; fasting while forgetful and an inadvertent broken oath are disputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r9.anchor: والصحيح أن ذلك يختلف بحسب الوقائع، فقسم لا يسقط باتفاق كالغرامات والديات والصلوات المفروضات.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r10.speaker: مالك والربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r10.claim: Malik and al-Rabiʿ define iṣr as a severe, difficult command.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r10.anchor: قال مالك والربيع: الإصر الأمر الغليظ الصعب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says iṣr is hard labor and the burdens placed on the Israelites, such as rules about urine.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r11.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: الإصر شدة العمل، وما غلظ على بني إسرائيل من البول ونحوه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r12.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets iṣr as weighty, stringent obligations, close to Malik and al-Rabiʿ’s view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r12.anchor: قال الضحاك: كانوا يحملون أمورا شدادا وهذا نحو قول مالك والربيع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r13.speaker: النابغة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r13.claim: Al-Nabigha’s line about bearing the iṣr for people is cited as poetic evidence for the sense of a burden.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#6/r13.anchor: وهذا نحو قول مالك والربيع ومنه قول النابغة:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r1.speaker: عطاء وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r1.claim: Ata and Ibn Zayd interpret iṣr as metamorphosis into apes and pigs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r1.anchor: عطاء: الإصر المسخ قردة وخنازير وقاله ابن زيد أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd also says iṣr means a sin for which there is neither repentance nor expiation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r2.anchor: وعنه أيضا أنه الذنب الذي ليس فيه توبة ولا كفارة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r3.claim: Iṣr can mean covenant, as in the covenant taken in another verse, as well as narrowness, sin, or burden.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r3.anchor: والإصر في اللغة العهد ومنه قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r4.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r4.claim: The word can also mean a rope binding loads; aṣara means to confine, and Jawhari gives maʾṣir/maʾṣar and plural maʾāṣir, noting common mispronunciation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r4.anchor: والإصار: الحبل الذي تربط به الأحمال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r5.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r5.claim: Ibn Khuwayzimandad says the verse’s apparent sense can rebut claims that a religious duty is unduly burdensome, in line with no hardship in religion and the report that religion is easy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r5.anchor: قال ابن خويزمنداد: ويمكن أن يستدل بهذا الظاهر في كل عبادة ادعى الخصم تثقيلها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r6.speaker: الكيا الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r6.claim: Al-Kiya al-Tabari likewise uses the verse to deny hardship and constriction incompatible with the tolerant, upright religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r6.anchor: ونحوه قال الكيا الطبري قال: يحتج به في نفي الحرج والضيق المنافي ظاهره للحنيفية السمحة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r7.claim: Qatada interprets the prayer as asking not to be burdened as harshly as earlier peoples were.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: معناه لا تشدد علينا كما شددت على من كان قبلنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r8.speaker: الضحاك وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd say the prayer asks not to be burdened with deeds people cannot bear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r8.anchor: الضحاك: لا تحملنا من الأعمال ما لا نطيق وقال نحوه ابن زيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets it as asking not to be transformed into apes and pigs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r9.anchor: ابن جريج: لا تمسخنا قردة ولا خنازير.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r10.speaker: سلام بن سابور ومجاهد وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r10.claim: Salam ibn Sabur says the unbearable thing is sexual urge; al-Naqqash also transmits this interpretation from Mujahid and Ata.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r10.anchor: وقال سلام بن سابور: الذي لا طاقة لنا به: الغلمة وحكاه النقاش عن مجاهد وعطاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r11.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r11.claim: Abu al-Darda used to pray for refuge from sexual urge without the means to satisfy it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r11.anchor: وروي أن أبا الدرداء كان يقول في دعائه: وأعوذ بك من غلمة ليس لها عدة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r12.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r12.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the unbearable burden as the severity and shackles imposed on the Israelites.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r12.anchor: وقال السدي: هو التغليظ والأغلال التي كانت على بني إسرائيل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r13.claim: ʿAfw means leaving a sin without punishing its doer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r13.anchor: عفوت عن ذنبه إذا تركته ولم تعاقبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r14.claim: Forgiveness means covering sins; ghafr is concealment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r14.anchor: { واغفر لنا } أي استر على ذنوبنا. والغفر: الستر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r15.claim: Mercy here is a favor that God initiates for people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r15.anchor: { وارحمنا } أي تفضل برحمة مبتدئا منك علينا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r16.claim: Mawlana means our protector and helper.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r17.claim: The prayer’s wording teaches people how to supplicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r17.anchor: وخرج هذا مخرج التعليم للخلق كيف يدعون.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r18.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r18.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal reportedly said “Amen” after reciting this sura; Ibn Atiyya says this may be a report from the Prophet, or a sound analogy with al-Fatiha’s supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r18.anchor: روي عن معاذ بن جبل أنه كان إذا فرغ من قراءة هذه السورة قال: آمين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r19.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r19.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib said he doubted that anyone who understands and has grasped Islam would sleep before reading the final two verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#7/r19.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: ما أظن أحدا عقل وأدرك الإسلام ينام حتى يقرأهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r1.speaker: أبو مسعود الأنصاري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r1.claim: Muslim transmits from Abu Masud al-Ansari that the Prophet said whoever recites the final two verses of al-Baqara at night, they suffice him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r1.anchor: من قرأ هاتين الآيتين من آخر سورة «البقرة» في ليلة كفتاه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r2.claim: One explanation is that the verses suffice for night prayer; Ibn Umar reports that reading them twice after the evening prayer fulfills that role.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r2.anchor: قيل: من قيام الليل كما روي عن ابن عمر قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r3.claim: Another explanation is that the verses suffice against Satan’s harm, so he has no power over the reader.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r3.anchor: وقيل: كفتاه من شر الشيطان فلا يكون له عليه سلطان.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r4.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r4.claim: Al-Dani transmits from Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman that a book was written before creation and three closing verses from it were revealed; reciting them at home keeps Satan away for three nights.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r4.anchor: وأسند أبو عمرو الداني عن حذيفة بن اليمان قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r5.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r5.claim: The Prophet said these closing verses came from a treasure beneath the Throne and were not given to any prophet before him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r5.anchor: أوتيت هذه الآيات من آخر سورة البقرة من كنز تحت العرش لم يؤتهن نبي قبلي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls this report sound and links these verses’ descent with the angel’s descent with al-Fatiha.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:285-286#8/r6.anchor: وهذا صحيح وقد تقدم في الفاتحة نزول الملك بها مع الفاتحة.

RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says the opening clause may be God's own statement or a continuation of the believers' words following their confession and prayer in 2:285.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون ابتداء خبر من الله ويحتمل أن يكون حكاية عن الرسول والمؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r2.claim: If the believers speak the clause, it follows their “we hear and obey”: since God mercifully requires only what is within capacity, they must respond with obedience as servants.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r2.anchor: فكأنهم قالوا : كيف لا نسمع ولا نطيع

RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r3.claim: If God speaks the clause, it answers the believers' plea for forgiveness: after their obedience and request for pardon over deliberate shortcomings, He reassures them about inadvertent lapses.

RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r4.claim: The verb is used in the construction “I burdened him with a thing, so he undertook it”; taklīf is its verbal noun.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r4.anchor: يقال : كلفته الشيء فتكلف ، والكلف اسم منه

RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r5.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats wusʿ as a noun, like wajd and juhd.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r5.anchor: قال الفراء : هو اسم كالوجد والجهد

RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r6.claim: Others define capacity as what a person can bear without constriction or hardship, below the utmost degree of exertion.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121/r6.anchor: الوسع ما يسع الإنسان ولا يضيق عليه ولا يحرج فيه

RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r1.claim: The Muʿtazila cite this verse and 22:78, 4:28, and the promise of ease to argue that God does not impose what a person cannot do.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r1.anchor: المعتزلة عولوا على هذه الآية في أنه تعالى لا يكلف العبد ما لا يطيقه

RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r2.claim: Their first premise is that people create their own acts: if God created the commanded act, the person could neither produce it again nor resist God's power; if God did not, the person could not bring it about.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r2.anchor: الأول : أن العبد موجد لأفعال نفسه ، فإنه لو كان موجدها هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r3.claim: Their second premise is that ability precedes the act; otherwise an unbeliever commanded to believe would not be able to do so, making the command impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r3.anchor: والثاني : أن الاستطاعة قبل الفعل وإلا لكان الكافر المأمور بالإيمان لم يكن قادرا على الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī's Ashʿarite colleagues say rational proofs establish that impossible commands do occur, so this verse must be interpreted.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4.anchor: أما الأصحاب فقالوا : دلت الدلائل العقلية على وقوع التكليف على هذا الوجه

RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5.claim: The first rational argument invokes God's eternal knowledge that one who dies in unbelief will never believe; that foreknown nonbelief is incompatible with belief, making the command appear to require a contradiction and likewise raising the problem of compulsion.
RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5.anchor: من مات على الكفر ينبىء موته على الكفر أن الله تعالى كان عالما في الأزل بأنه يموت على الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r1.claim: The second argument says acts depend on motives created by God; if motives instead came from the person, an infinite regress follows, while a determining motive makes the alternative impossible, yet the unbeliever is commanded to believe.
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r1.anchor: لأن قدرة العبد لما كانت صالح للفعل والترك

RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r2.claim: The third argument says a command issued when motives are equal requires contradictory equality and preference; if one motive prevails, the preferred is necessary and the other impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r2.anchor: فإن كان الأول فهو تكليف ما لا يطاق ، لأن الاستواء يناقض الرجحان

RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r3.claim: The fourth argument says Abū Lahab was commanded to believe even though God had announced that he would not believe, so he was required to believe that he would not believe.
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r3.anchor: أنه تعالى كلف أبا لهب الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r4.claim: The fifth argument says people do not know the detailed count of movements and rests in an act such as moving a finger; since they did not intend that precise count, they do not create it, and an undetermined preference is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r4.anchor: العبد غير عالم بتفاصيل فعله ، لأن من حرك أصبعه لم يعرف عدد الأحيان التي حرك أصبعه فيها

RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī deems the rational proofs decisive: when they conflict with an apparent scriptural meaning, one must preserve the proofs and interpret the apparent text, or undermine rational grounds for monotheism, prophecy, and scripture.
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r5.anchor: لم يبق إلا أن يقطع بصحة الدلائل العقلية ، ويحمل الظاهر السمعي على التأويل

RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī notes that the same interpretive method is routinely used by the Muʿtazila against anthropomorphic readings; thus the verse certainly admits interpretation even if its precise interpretation is left unspecified.
RAZI-FULL:v7p122/r6.anchor: وهذا الكلام هو الذي تعول المعتزلة عليه أبدا في دفع الظواهر التي تمسك بها أهل التشبيه

RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r1.claim: A second answer defines command as notice that action brings reward and omission brings punishment; where an act is impossible, the statement is not a real command but notice of punishment and one's creation for Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r1.anchor: لا معنى للتكليف في الأمر والنهي إلا الإعلام بأنه متى فعل كذا فإنه يثاب

RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r2.speaker: طائفة من قدماء أهل الجبر
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r2.claim: A group of early determinists says people are commanded while it remains unknown whether God knows they will die unbelievers; after such a death, one learns the obstacle was present and the condition for obligation had been absent during life.
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r2.anchor: وهذا قول طائفة من قدماء أهل الجبر

RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r3.claim: A fourth answer says the clause is spoken by the believers and therefore does not prove God's rule; al-Rāzī calls this weak, since God recounts and praises their words, so they must be truthful.
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r3.anchor: إلا أن هذا ضعيف ، وذلك لأن الله تعالى لما حكاه عنهم في معرض المدح لهم والثناء عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī ends this dispute by asking God to show mercy to their incapacity and limited understanding and forgive their errors, affirming that they seek only truth.
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r4.anchor: فإنا لا نطلب إلا الحق ، ولا نروم إلا الصدق

RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r5.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the language treats kasb and iktisāb as synonyms; Dhū al-Rummah's verse and Qurʾānic uses interchange them in 74:38, 6:164, 2:81, and 33:58.
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r5.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : الصحيح عند أهل اللغة أن الكسب والاكتساب واحد لا فرق بينهما

RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r6.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r6.claim: Some accept a distinction: kasb can be for oneself or another, while iktisāb is only what one acquires for oneself; one can be a breadwinner for one's family but not an acquirer for them.
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r6.anchor: ومن الناس من سلم الفرق ، ثم فيه قولان أحدهما : أن الاكتساب أخص من الكسب

RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r7.claim: Al-Kashshāf says good is called kasb and evil iktisāb because evil is desired by the commanding soul, which works harder to acquire it, whereas the good term does not imply such exertion.
RAZI-FULL:v7p123/r7.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : إنما خص الخير بالكسب

RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer that people create their own acts: attributing good and evil to them would be invalid if God created those acts, as with involuntary traits.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r1.anchor: المعتزلة احتجوا بهذه الآية على أن فعل العبد بإيجاده وتكوينه

RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r2.claim: The Qadi argues that if God creates human acts, obligation loses its purpose; on that view, asking for lighter duties is also pointless because God creates both burdens and ease without fatigue.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r2.anchor: لو كان خالقا أفعالهم فما الفائدة في التكليف

RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r3.claim: The author’s school rejects moral annihilation: reward for good and liability for evil can coexist, and the arrival of one does not erase the other.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r3.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على فساد القول بالمحابطة

RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r4.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r4.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi reads the verse conditionally: reward remains only if not invalidated, and punishment only if not expiated by repentance, since pure everlasting reward and punishment cannot coexist.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r4.anchor: ظاهر الآية وإن دل على الإطلاق إلا أنه مشروط والتقدير

RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r5.claim: Al-Razi says the debate over annulment was treated fully under the prohibition on nullifying charity through reproach and injury.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r5.anchor: أن الكلام على هذه المسألة مر على الاستقصاء في تفسير

RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r6.speaker: كثير من المتكلمين
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r6.claim: Many theologians use the verse to argue that God does not punish children for their parents’ sins, as also stated by 6:164.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r6.anchor: احتج كثير من المتكلمين بهذه الآية على أن الله تعالى لا يعذب الأطفال بذنوب آبائهم

RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r7.speaker: الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r7.claim: Jurists infer that ownership ordinarily continues and remains attached to what a person has acquired.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r7.anchor: الفقهاء تمسكوا بهذه الآية في إثبات أن الأصل في الإمساك البقاء والاستمرار

RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says each person has a stronger claim to their earnings than their parents, children, or other people; al-Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124/r8.anchor: وتأكد ذلك بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r1.claim: A guarantor’s payment does not transfer ownership of the guaranteed property: the original basis for ownership remains, while usurpation or liability does not remove it, as illustrated by an umm walad and a mudabbara.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r1.anchor: أن المضمونات لا تملك بأداء الضمان

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r2.claim: Incorporating a usurped yard into a building or milling usurped grain does not extinguish the owner’s title.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r2.anchor: إذا غصب ساحة وأدرجها في بنائه

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r3.claim: A neighbor has no right of preemption: a co-owner has priority, the parties are not equal, neighborly harm is less, and a neighbor’s sale requires no partition.

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r4.claim: Amputation does not end ownership or the duty to compensate; if stolen property still exists, it must be returned to its owner.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r4.anchor: ومنها أن القطع لا يمنع وجوب الضمان

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r5.claim: Those denying obligatory zakat cite the verse, but al-Razi answers that the specific proofs requiring zakat take precedence over this general text.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r5.anchor: ومنها أن منكري وجوب الزكاة احتجوا به

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi calls this verse a major foundation for numerous branches of jurisprudence.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r6.anchor: فهذه الآية أصل كبير في فروع الفقه

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r7.claim: A Prophetic report calls supplication the core of worship; al-Razi states no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r7.anchor: لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r8.claim: Supplication displays the worshipper’s poverty, need, and humility before God’s majesty and self-sufficiency, so the surah closes with entreaty; al-Razi discusses prayer under 2:186.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r8.anchor: ختم هذه السورة الشريفة المشتملة على هذه العلوم العظيمة بالدعاء والتضرع إلى الله

RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r9.claim: Al-Razi counts four kinds of supplication: the first three begin with “Our Lord,” while the fourth omits that vocative.
RAZI-FULL:v7p124#2/r9.anchor: أنه تعالى حكى عن المؤمنين دعاءهم

RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r1.claim: “Do not take us to account” means “do not punish us.”

RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r2.claim: One explanation for the reciprocal form is that the forgetful person exposed himself to harm through his own action, making the punisher seem to assist in harming him.
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r2.anchor: لأن الناسي قد أمكن من نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r3.claim: Al-Razi’s alternative is that God takes the sinner through punishment while the sinner clings to God for pardon, so each is figuratively taking the other.

RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r4.claim: The first of two interpretations takes forgetfulness in its ordinary sense, as the opposite of remembering.
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r4.anchor: في النسيان وجهان الأول : أن المراد منه

RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says error, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from the community; al-Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r5.anchor: رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r6.claim: Al-Razi answers that forgetfulness may be culpable when someone neglects precautions, but excusable when warning signs were absent or the person took reasonable care; he gives examples involving impurity, mistaken shooting, and forgetting memorized Qurʾan.

RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet tied a thread around his finger when he wanted to remember a need; al-Razi uses it to show deliberate memory precautions.
RAZI-FULL:v7p125/r7.anchor: وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا أراد أن يذكر حاجته شد خيطا في أصبعه

RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r1.claim: The prayer may be hypothetical: these righteous believers only risked such lapses inadvertently, so they disclaim liability even if inadvertent acts could in principle be punished.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r1.anchor: أن يكون هذا دعاء على سبيل التقدير وذلك لأن هؤلاء المؤمنين الذين ذكروا هذا الدعاء كانوا متقين

RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r2.claim: Supplication can express humility rather than ask for an uncertain outcome; al-Razi compares requests for just judgment, fulfillment of promises, and forgiveness for repentant believers.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r2.anchor: المقصود من الدعاء إظهار التضرع إلى الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r3.claim: Punishing a forgetful person is not rationally impossible: fear of later punishment can sustain memory, though constant vigilance is difficult, making a request for pardon fitting.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r3.anchor: أن مؤاخذة الناسي غير ممتنعة عقلا

RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r4.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r4.claim: Al-Razi’s Ashʿari associates argue that the verse supports the rational possibility of obligating what cannot be done: a forgetful person cannot avoid the act, yet asks God not to punish him for it.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r4.anchor: أصحابنا الذين يجوزون تكليف ما لا يطاق يتمسكون بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r5.claim: A second sense of forgetfulness is abandonment, supported by Qurʾanic usage at 20:115 and 9:67.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني : في تفسير النسيان ، أن يحمل على الترك

RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r6.claim: On the abandonment reading, error means doing an act on the basis of a mistaken interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126/r6.anchor: والمراد بالخطأ ، أن يفعل الفعل لتأويل فاسد

RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r1.claim: If forgetting and error mean intentionally doing wrong, the commanded prayer gives grave sinners grounds to hope for pardon: God instructs believers to ask not to be punished for such sins.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r1.anchor: فأما الاحتمال الأول فإنه يدل على حصول العفو لأصحاب الكبائر

RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r2.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r2.claim: The alternative cases, where one or both terms mean an unintentional act, are excluded within the opponent’s premises, since punishment would be wrong and cannot properly be requested.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r2.anchor: وأما القسم الثاني والثالث فباطلان لأن المؤاخذة على ذلك قبيحة عند الخصم

RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r3.claim: Although neglecting precautions may be culpable, the person is then punished for deliberately failing to take care, not for the lapse itself; the verse therefore still supports hope of pardon for grave sinners.
RAZI-FULL:v7p126#2/r3.anchor: فهو في الحقيقة مؤاخذ بترك التحفظ قصدا وعمدا

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r1.speaker: النابغة
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r1.claim: Al-Nabigha’s verse uses isr for a burden borne to shield a tribe from oppression, evidencing the word’s sense of weight and hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r1.anchor: قال النابغة : يا مانع الضيم أن يغشى سراتهم

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r2.claim: A covenant is called an isr because it is weighty; 3:81 uses the word for God’s covenant and pact.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r2.anchor: ثم سمي العهد إصرا لأنه ثقيل

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r3.claim: Isr can also mean affection or kinship: caring for someone makes the hardships that befall them weigh on one’s heart.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r3.anchor: والإصر العطف ، يقال : ما يأصرني عليه آصرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r4.claim: Exegetes explain the prayer as asking not to impose the severe obligations placed on Jews: traditions cited include fifty prayers, a quarter of wealth in alms, cutting away garment impurity, worldly penalties for lapses, and loss of formerly lawful foods.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r4.anchor: أهل التفسير فيه وجهين الأول : لا تشدد علينا في التكاليف

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r5.claim: Al-Qaffal says examining the fifth book of the Torah claimed by the Jews reveals many severe covenants and remarkable details.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r5.anchor: ومن نظر في السفر الخامس من التوراة التي تدعيها هؤلاء اليهود

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r6.claim: Al-Razi says God removed such burdens and shackles from this community, citing the description at 7:157.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r6.anchor: ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التى كانت عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r7.claim: A Prophetic report says the community was spared transformation, landslides, and drowning; al-Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r7.anchor: رفع عن أمتي المسخ والخسف والغرق

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r8.claim: A Prophetic report describes his mission as the tolerant, easy monotheistic way; al-Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r8.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( بعثت بالحنيفية السهلة السمحة

RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r9.claim: Believers request easier obligations because severity invites shortcoming, which brings punishment they cannot endure; hence they ask for ease in duties.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127/r9.anchor: التشديد مظنة التقصير ، والتقصير موجب للعقوبة

RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r1.speaker: أهل التفسير
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r1.claim: The second interpretation asks that God not impose a covenant as severe as that imposed on earlier people; al-Razi says it essentially returns to the first view with an extra unstated element, so the first is preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r1.anchor: والقول الثاني : لا تحمل علينا عهدا وميثاقا يشبه ميثاق من قبلنا

RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r2.claim: The Muʿtazilites say different duties suit different people: Jews’ harsh temperaments required severe commands, whereas this community’s refined character made lighter duties beneficial.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r2.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : من الجائز أن يكون الشيء مصلحة في حق إنسان

RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi’s associates answer by asking why God gave Jews harsh natures and this community refined ones; the explanation merely shifts the question about divine choice.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r3.anchor: أجاب الأصحاب بأن السؤال الذي ذكرناه في المقام الأول ننقله إلى المقام الثاني

RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi rejects the Muʿtazilite temperamental explanation as unsound, affirming that God acts as He wills and is not questioned, as stated at 21:23.
RAZI-FULL:v7p127#2/r4.anchor: ومن تأمل وأنصف علم أن هذه التعليلات عليلة فجل جناب الجلال عن أن يوزن بميزان الاعتزال

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r1.claim: Ṭāqa is a verbal noun from iṭāqa, like ṭāʿa from iṭāʿa and ijāba from ijāba, and is used in place of the verbal noun.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r1.anchor: الطاقة اسم من الإطاقة ، كالطاعة من الإطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r2.claim: Al-Razi’s associates argue that the prayer proves the rational permissibility of imposing an obligation beyond capacity, since it asks God to refrain from it.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r2.anchor: من الأصحاب من تمسك به في أن تكليف ما لا يطاق جائز إذ لو لم يكن جائزا لما حسن طلبه بالدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r3.claim: The Muʿtazilites read “beyond our capacity” as an act that is extremely difficult, as in colloquial claims of being unable to look at someone or bear a task.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r3.anchor: ما لا طاقة لنا به } أي يشق فعله مشقة عظيمة

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r4.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r4.claim: The cited poem uses ṭāqa for what is difficult to bear, supporting the Muʿtazilite reading of the phrase as severe hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر : إنك إن كلفتني ما لم أطق

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says a servant should receive food and clothing and not be assigned work beyond what he can bear; al-Razi cites it for the hardship sense and gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r5.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال في المملوك

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r6.claim: Imran ibn Husayn reports that the Prophet instructed the ill to pray sitting, or on their side if unable; jurists read inability as severe hardship, not literal incapacity. No grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r6.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r7.claim: The Muʿtazilites read “they could not hear” at 11:20 as meaning that hearing was difficult for them.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r7.anchor: أجاب المعتزلة عنه من وجوه الأول

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r8.claim: Their second reply says taḥmīl is placing an unbearable load, so the phrase means punishment that cannot be endured; reading it as obligation is figurative.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r8.anchor: التحميل هو أن يضع عليه ما لا طاقة له بتحمله فيكون المراد منه العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r9.claim: Their third reply is that praying against an act does not establish that God could do it, just as prayers against unjust judgment, disgrace, disobedience, or loss of deeds do not establish those outcomes as possible.
RAZI-FULL:v7p128/r9.anchor: هب أنهم سألوا الله تعالى أن لا يكلفهم بما لا قدرة لهم عليه لكن ذلك لا يدل على جواز أن يفعل خلافه

RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r1.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r1.claim: Al-Razi’s school rejects the hardship-only gloss: it would duplicate the preceding prayer, and ṭāqa means ability, so the apparent sense is what one has no power to do; “hard” is only figurative.
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r1.anchor: محمولا على أن لا يشدد عليهم في التكليف

RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r2.claim: They answer that Qurʾanic usage associates bearing with obligation, as in the human bearing of the trust at 33:72; even without that idiom, the phrase covers both punishment and obligation, so narrowing it needs proof.
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r2.anchor: التحمل مخصوص في عرف القرآن بالتكليف

RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r3.claim: They argue that a genuinely impossible act cannot be requested in supplication, like combining opposites or making the eternal originated; abandoning this rule in particular cases needs specific evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r3.anchor: فعل الشيء إذا كان ممتنعا لم يجز طلب الامتناع منه على سبيل الدعاء والتضرع

RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r4.claim: A difficult burden can be carried or imposed, while what is beyond capacity cannot be carried at all; therefore the verse uses “impose” for the impossible and both verbs for hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v7p129/r4.anchor: الشاق يمكن حمله أما ما لا يكون مقدورا

RAZI-FULL:v7p129#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p129#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p129#2/r1.claim: Al-Razi imagines two stations: outward religious law asks for no severe duties; the beginning of unveiling asks not to demand praise, gratitude, or knowledge commensurate with divine majesty, which humans cannot attain. Law precedes inner reality, explaining the order.
RAZI-FULL:v7p129#2/r1.anchor: للعبد مقامين أحدهما : قيامه بظاهر الشريعة

RAZI-FULL:v7p129#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p129#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p129#2/r2.claim: The plural prayer seeks fuller acceptance: when people’s spiritual intentions and desires converge on one request, its realization is stronger.
RAZI-FULL:v7p129#2/r2.anchor: المقصود منه ببيان أن قبول الدعاء عند الاجتماع أكمل وذلك لأن للهمم تأثيرات

RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r1.claim: The fourth prayer omits “Our Lord” because a call is needed at a distance; its omission signals that persistent entreaty brings the servant near to God.

RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r2.claim: ʿAfw means removing punishment, whereas maghfira conceals the sin and protects the sinner from the shame and exposure of punishment in the grave.

RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r3.claim: After seeking release from bodily punishment and spiritual disgrace, believers seek reward: mercy asks for bodily delights of Paradise, while “You are our Protector” asks for spiritual reward culminating in witnessing divine majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r3.anchor: فلما تخلص منهما أقبل على طلب الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r4.speaker: كثير من المتكلمين
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r4.claim: Some theologians reduce these requests to acts of obedience; al-Razi grants this as the limit of their knowledge while retaining the deeper bodily and spiritual interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v7p130/r4.anchor: كثيرا من المتكلمين يستبعدون هذه الكلمات

RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r1.claim: Calling God their Mawla expresses utmost humility and dependence: God gives every blessing and honor, as a guardian tends a child or a master orders a servant’s affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r1.anchor: هذه الكلمة تدل على نهاية الخضوع والتذلل والاعتراف بأنه سبحانه هو المتولي لكل نعمة

RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r2.claim: Here Mawla means helper or protector, as in 8:40, 2:257, 66:4, and 47:11.

RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r3.claim: The requested victory includes military struggle, debate by proof, and Islam’s political ascendancy over other religions, as promised at 9:33.

RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r4.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r4.claim: Some spiritual authorities interpret victory as God’s angelic, spiritual power overcoming bodily forces that urge the soul toward what is other than God.
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r4.anchor: ومن المحققين من قال : { فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين } المراد منه إعانة الله بالقوة الروحانية الملكية

RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi transmits from Muqatil a report that during the night journey the Prophet received the closing verses of al-Baqara and Gabriel taught him these prayers; God answered each petition with forgiveness, no burden, and victory. Some versions add that angels said “Amen”; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v7p131/r5.anchor: وروى الواحدي رحمه الله عن مقاتل بن سليمان أنه لما أسري بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى السماء أعطى خواتيم سورة البقرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p131#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p131#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p131#2/r1.claim: At the close of his tafsir, Razi says he wrote seeking God's pleasure, asks acceptance for what is correct, and pardon for any error.
RAZI-FULL:v7p131#2/r1.anchor: كل ما للبته وكتبته ما أردت به إلا وجهك ومرضاتك ، فإن أصبت فبتوفيقك أصبت فاقبله
